pieces.label: Wake (Him/Her)
pieces.text: (Neighbour) creeps close, takes (sleepwalker)'s arm, and says (sleepwalker.his/her) name, loud and clear. (Sleepwalker) jerks awake, sees the drop below (sleepwalker.his/her) feet, and gasps...

pieces.label: Guide (Him/Her) Back Asleep
pieces.text: (Neighbour) takes (sleepwalker)'s hand very gently. "Come on," (friend.he/she) whispers. "Time to go home." (Sleepwalker) turns, still asleep, and follows, step by careful step...

pieces.label: Call for Help
pieces.text: Call for Help.

pieces.label: Sing Softly
pieces.text: Sing Softly.
(Sleepwalker) trips in fright and hits (sleepwalker.his/her) head. The sleepwalking stops, and so does the name.
(Sleepwalker) wakes and steps the wrong way. The village builds a low stone wall along the headland.
On the way home (sleepwalker) weeds the garden perfectly, fast asleep. The village learns to leave tools out.
Safe home, but (sleepwalker) never naps again. A string of shells rattles across the doorway.
Eyes open but seeing nothing.
The path to the headland is lit by moonlight.
Never wake a sleepwalker suddenly, the old people say.

pieces.label: The Clay from the Old Kiln
pieces.text: (Sculptor) has made a life-sized clay figure of (sculptor.himself/herself) from the old kiln pit, whose potters mixed in a glowing powder that made figures "almost breathe," and it's going to rain.

pieces.label: Leave It Out in the Rain
pieces.text: The rain comes down hard in the night, drumming on the roof. (Sculptor) lies awake, listening, and thinks (sculptor.he/she) hears something out by the kiln sit up...

pieces.label: Cover It Up
pieces.text: (Sculptor) drags a big palm mat over the figure and weighs the corners down with stones. All night the rain hammers on the mat. In the morning, (sculptor) lifts it, half afraid of what (sculptor.he/she) will see...

pieces.label: Smash It
pieces.text: Smash It.

pieces.label: Show the Elders
pieces.text: Show the Elders.
A second (sculptor), still damp, sits on the doorstep in the morning, and insists it was the other one made of clay.
Someone with (sculptor)'s face and nothing of (sculptor)'s heart walks in, and becomes the best potter in the village.
Just clay, slightly cross-eyed. The children call it "the other (sculptor)."
The figure crumbles, and (sculptor)'s own face is new. "The clay wanted to be you."
The old kiln has long since fallen in.
It's a very good likeness.
Nobody has used the clay pit in a hundred years.

pieces.label: The Wishing Tree
pieces.text: On the longest night of the year, (hopeful_parent) and (friend), who want a child more than anything, climb to the old wishing tree hung with hundreds of woven tokens, with a little woven fish of their own.

pieces.label: Tie It to the Lowest Branch
pieces.text: They kneel in the roots together and tie the little fish on with three knots, the way the elders said. A breeze moves through the tree, and every token on it sways and clicks like a hundred tiny wooden bells...

pieces.label: Climb to the Very Top
pieces.text: (Friend) climbs, branch by twisted branch, until (friend.he/she) is swaying at the very top with the stars all round, and ties the little fish to the highest twig. The whole tree shivers...

pieces.label: Tie It Together Halfway Up
pieces.text: Tie It Together Halfway Up.

pieces.label: Leave It in the Roots
pieces.text: Leave It in the Roots.
A month later a baby is expected, and they tie a woven bird to give thanks. "Polite tree."
The healer listens a while longer: {#babies:just the one|twins|triplets}. "The couple who planted it had eleven."
The tree heard the wish from whoever was closest to the top. It's (friend) who is expecting.
No baby this year. They teach the little ones to weave fish tokens, and the tree waits with them.
The tokens sway and click like a hundred tiny wooden bells.
Planted by a couple who longed for children and ended up with eleven.
A little woven fish, tied with three knots.

pieces.label: The Smoke on the Horizon
pieces.text: After three days of smoke on the horizon, two canoes come in low and slow, the paddlers grey with ash. Their mountain woke up and covered their gardens in ash.

pieces.label: Run to the Healer
pieces.text: The healer comes down the beach at a run with a basket of water gourds and clean cloths, and starts washing the ash out of the newcomers' eyes before anyone has even said hello...

pieces.label: Run to the Head Cook
pieces.text: The head cook takes one look at the grey, hollow faces and starts filling bowls. "Talk later," the cook says. "Eat first..."

pieces.label: Run to the Builders
pieces.text: Run to the Builders.

pieces.label: Wave Them In
pieces.text: Wave Them In.
A tired parent, a teen who won't admit their arms hurt, and a child who never stops talking. They decide to stay.
Two adults and a furious, ash-wrapped baby sleep a day and a night, then ask where they can help.
Fed, rested and on their way south to family, with full canoes.
"Stay until you're fat again, then decide." One family can't imagine getting back in a canoe.
The paddlers are grey with ash from head to foot.
A mountain that "breathes."
"Talk later. Eat first."

pieces.label: The Rival Builders
pieces.text: (First_builder) builds low and wide, (second_builder) builds tall and narrow, and after a storm both have completely different plans to fix the roofs. The elders are tired of the shouting.

pieces.label: Make Them Work Together
pieces.text: The elders put them on the same roof with one ladder and one bundle of thatch. The village gathers to watch, as if it's a festival...

pieces.label: Half the Huts Each
pieces.text: The elders draw a line down the middle of the village. (First_builder) gets the huts on the beach side, and (second_builder) the huts on the hill side. They set to work without speaking...

pieces.label: Let the Children Judge
pieces.text: Let the Children Judge.

pieces.label: Hold a Building Contest
pieces.text: Hold a Building Contest.
By evening they finish each other's sentences, and argue on the same side.
Racing each other, they fix every roof in three days. The roofs are odd but don't leak.
Two of (second_builder)'s tall roofs blow off in front of everyone, and building stops being a joy.
(First_builder) crosses the line just to have someone to disagree with.
Every hut in the village has been built by one and criticised by the other.
One ladder and one bundle of thatch.
The village gathers to watch, as if it's a festival.

pieces.label: The Bonesetter's Choice
pieces.text: (Patient) has fallen from a coconut palm and broken (patient.his/her) leg badly. (healer) can pull it straight now, fast and painful, or give the sleeping drink and wait while the swelling grows.

pieces.label: The Quick Way
pieces.text: (healer) nods to two strong villagers to hold (patient) down, puts both hands on the leg, counts to three, and pulls on two...

pieces.label: The Slow Way
pieces.text: (healer) mixes the sleeping drink, and (patient) drinks it, and they wait. The swelling grows. (Patient)'s eyes start to droop...

pieces.label: Ask the Oldest Healer
pieces.text: Ask the Oldest Healer.

pieces.label: Splint It and Wait
pieces.text: Splint It and Wait.
The leg heals crooked, and (patient) is faster on (patient.his/her) polished crutch than most people walk.
A terrible noise, and it's done. The young healers can't stop talking about (healer)'s hands.
A fever follows and breaks on the fourth day. "I don't mind lying down anymore."
(Patient) sleeps through it. "When are you going to do it?"
The leg is at an angle that makes the children turn away.
"Just do it. Whatever's best."
The swelling grows by the hour.

pieces.label: The Mask with Another Face
pieces.text: In an old storehouse (finder) finds a carved mask with "Azizi" scratched on the back, made long ago "for anyone who wants to be someone else for a while."

pieces.label: Put It On
pieces.text: (Finder) ties the mask on. It's warm, as if someone just took it off. Through the eye holes, the village looks a little brighter, a little sharper, as if (finder.he/she) is seeing it with someone else's eyes...

pieces.label: Hang It on the Wall
pieces.text: (Finder) decides it's too old and too strange to wear. (finder.He/She) hangs it on the wall of (finder.his/her) hut, where its half-closed eyes seem to follow (finder.him/her) round the room...

pieces.label: Show the Elders
pieces.text: Show the Elders.

pieces.label: Wrap It Up Again
pieces.text: Wrap It Up Again.
At sunset the face underneath is new, between (finder.his/hers) and the mask's. "Never quite the same."
By evening (finder) answers only to "Azizi," and the name stays when the mask comes off.
(Finder) sleeps under the mask and wakes years younger in the face. The painted mouth seems to smile.
Nothing happens, and years later the old style is carved all over the village.
A calm face with half-closed eyes, painted red and white.
The mask is warm, as if someone just took it off.
Its eyes seem to follow (finder.him/her) round the room.

pieces.label: The Overturned Canoe
pieces.text: A rogue wave flips the canoe, and (fisher) surfaces to see (friend) under the water, tangled in the net, while the canoe drifts towards the coral.

pieces.label: Dive and Cut the Net
pieces.text: (Fisher) takes the biggest breath of (fisher.his/her) life and dives, knife in hand, down into the churning blue. The net is everywhere, wrapped round (friend)'s arm and leg...

pieces.label: Hold On and Shout
pieces.text: (Fisher) bellows across the water, and the nearest canoe turns towards them. The fisher in it is already reaching for (fisher.his/her) own knife...

pieces.label: Pull on the Net
pieces.text: Pull on the Net.

pieces.label: Cut the Net from the Hull
pieces.text: Cut the Net from the Hull.
(Fisher) drags (friend) up, but (friend) had been under too long. (Fisher) did everything anyone could have done.
Cut free and coughing. That evening every fisher practises cutting free from a net, blindfolded.
Another fisher cuts (friend) free. (Fisher) still fishes, but never goes past the reef again.
Three fishers dive together. "Next time I'll hold the canoe, and you can get tangled."
The canoe is drifting towards the coral.
A dark shape under the water, tangled in the net.
The biggest breath of (fisher.his/her) life.

pieces.label: The Raft on the Morning Tide
pieces.text: At first light (finder) finds a raft on the beach with an exhausted traveller and a crying baby tied to their chest. (Finder) can only carry one of them up at a time.

pieces.label: Carry the Baby First
pieces.text: (Finder) takes the baby and runs, shouting for the healers. Behind (finder.him/her), the traveller sinks back onto the raft with a look of enormous relief...

pieces.label: Help the Traveller Up First
pieces.text: (Finder) gets an arm under the traveller and half carries, half drags the traveller up the sand, the baby screaming between them...

pieces.label: Shout for Help
pieces.text: Shout for Help.

pieces.label: Give Them Water on the Sand
pieces.text: Give Them Water on the Sand.
The traveller holds on just long enough to hear the baby is safe. "I'll tell this little one all about you. Every year."
(Finder) does the night feeds, and by the time the traveller is strong, the baby has two parents.
The baby screams whenever anyone else holds it. "It's all right. We'll share."
A second raft brings the traveller's partner, who has searched the sea for two days.
A few logs lashed together and a torn sail.
"Please," the traveller whispers, and holds the baby up.
Cracked lips and eyes barely open.

pieces.label: The Lagoon That Keeps Time
pieces.text: (Swimmer) has lost a bet and must swim across the still, round lagoon that the fishers say "keeps time," giving some back or taking some for itself.

pieces.label: Swim with the Current
pieces.text: (Swimmer) slips in and lets the slow circle carry (swimmer.him/her). It's warm, and easy, like being rocked. The far shore comes closer, then further, then closer...

pieces.label: Swim Against the Current
pieces.text: (Swimmer) kicks hard against the slow circle. It's like swimming through honey. Every stroke feels like an hour...

pieces.label: Float Across
pieces.text: Float Across.

pieces.label: Refuse the Bet
pieces.text: Refuse the Bet.
(Swimmer) climbs out ten years younger. "It gave me some back."
The lagoon takes ten years for itself. "I won the bet back, at least." (swimmer.He/She) didn't.
"It took the time back from my face and put it all in my legs."
"It didn't want my time," says (swimmer), almost offended.
The water is perfectly still, even in a storm.
A slow, glittering current goes round in a circle.
The fishers won't fish in it.

pieces.label: The Festival of Lanterns
pieces.text: On lantern night every family floats a little bark lantern on the lagoon for the people they've lost. (Lantern_keeper) is in charge, and a stiff wind is blowing from the sea towards the huts.

pieces.label: Go Ahead Tonight
pieces.text: The whole village gathers at the water's edge, and one by one the little lanterns are lit and set on the water. The wind catches them...

pieces.label: Wait for a Still Night
pieces.text: The children groan, but (lantern_keeper) holds firm. They wait, one night, two nights, and on the third, the wind drops to nothing and the lagoon is flat as glass...

pieces.label: Float Them from the Far Shore
pieces.text: Float Them from the Far Shore.

pieces.label: Light Them on the Beach Instead
pieces.text: Light Them on the Beach Instead.
The wind carries the lanterns past the reef in a river of light until they're lost among the stars.
A gust blows a lantern onto a roof. The patches get a little lantern painted on each.
On the third night the lagoon is flat as glass, and there seem to be twice as many lights.
Three days of stories, and lantern night feels like a long, quiet conversation.
Little lanterns of bark and leaves.
The children have been folding them for a month.
Their reflections hang beneath them on the water.

pieces.label: The Wind from the Bell Rocks
pieces.text: Crossing the mountain pass, (traveller) is caught in the ringing of the hollow bell rocks, where a healer once hung chimes "to ring away bad memories," and the wind still carries memories off, good and bad alike.

pieces.label: Run for the Far Side
pieces.text: (Traveller) runs, stumbling on the loose stones, the bells ringing louder and louder until (traveller.he/she) is through and out and the sound drops away behind (traveller.him/her)...

pieces.label: Crouch Down and Cover the Ears
pieces.text: (Traveller) drops into a hollow and presses (traveller.his/her) hands over (traveller.his/her) ears and waits, eyes squeezed shut, while the bells ring and ring and the wind howls overhead...

pieces.label: Sing Over the Bells
pieces.text: Sing over the Bells.

pieces.label: Turn Back
pieces.text: Turn Back.
(Traveller)'s own name is rung right out of (traveller.his/her) head. The village calls (traveller.him/her) "?".
The memory of loving the rain has gone off on the wind.
The bells leave a new name behind, clear as a bell, and it fits.
Name, home and friends all there, and (traveller) is deaf as a stone for a day.
The hollow rocks ring like bells.
(traveller.He/She) can feel it in (traveller.his/her) teeth.
Something loosens in (traveller.his/her) head, like a knot slipping.

pieces.label: The Elder's Last Winter
pieces.text: Very old (elder) has been ill since the rains, and (healer) has a strong remedy two days' journey away. "I've had a long life. Spend the two days with me instead."

pieces.label: Fetch the Bark
pieces.text: (healer) leaves at dawn, running most of the way, and comes back on the second evening, scratched and limping, with a bundle of grey bark under (healer.his/her) arm...

pieces.label: Stay with (Him/Her)
pieces.text: (healer) puts the bundle of travelling things away and sits down by the mat. For two days, (healer.he/she) and (elder)'s family take turns holding (elder)'s hand and telling (elder.him/her) the village news...

pieces.label: Send Someone Else for the Bark
pieces.text: Send Someone Else for the Bark.

pieces.label: Try the Old Remedies
pieces.text: Try the Old Remedies.
The rattle goes, and getting well takes years off (elder)'s face. "I told you not to make a fuss."
(Elder) went that afternoon, peacefully, and sent (healer) thanks.
The rattle fades. "No fuss. Just company."
In the waking hours (elder) passes on everything (elder.he/she) knows.
(elder.His/Her) breathing rattles.
Grey bark from a tree on the far side of the island.
"Spend the two days with me instead."

pieces.label: The Shadow Net
pieces.text: (Weaver) is testing a spider-silk net, said to "catch anything," at dusk, when (weaver.his/her) own long shadow stretches into it and the net goes tight.

pieces.label: Haul It In
pieces.text: (Weaver) hauls, hand over hand. The net is heavy, and cold, and getting heavier. Out of the dark mesh, something is starting to take shape...

pieces.label: Let It Go
pieces.text: (Weaver) opens (weaver.his/her) hands. The net doesn't fall. It goes on pulling, harder, towards the dark trees, and (weaver)'s feet start sliding across the grass...

pieces.label: Call the Weavers
pieces.text: Call the Weavers.

pieces.label: Step Out of the Shadow
pieces.text: Step Out of the Shadow.
The net comes in with (weaver)'s shadow made solid. Only one of them casts a shadow.
A person with (weaver)'s face and someone new inside asks what it should be called.
The silk is wound round (weaver.his/her) wrist, and (weaver) is pulled into the trees. The net is found empty.
The wind gusts and the pulling stops. The net is for pigs from then on.
Light as mist, strong enough to hold a pig.
Her grandmother caught a shadow in one.
The net is cold, and getting heavier.

pieces.label: The Teaching Day
pieces.text: On the yearly teaching day, (elder) is paired with (young), who has never shown the slightest interest in anything (elder) does, and is already bored.

pieces.label: Teach It Properly
pieces.text: (Elder) starts at the beginning, the way (elder.he/she) was taught: slowly, carefully, every step explained twice. (young) yawns. Then, despite (elder.himself/herself), (young.he/she) starts to watch...

pieces.label: Find What (Young Name) Cares About
pieces.text: "What do you like?" (elder) asks. (young) shrugs. "Nothing." (Elder) waits. Eventually, sullenly, (young) admits to liking watching the birds...

pieces.label: Let (Young Name) Teach Instead
pieces.text: Let (Young) Teach Instead.

pieces.label: Make It a Game
pieces.text: Make It a Game.
By evening (young) is arguing about the right way, and is occasionally right.
A crowd drifts over to listen, and three go home with their hands itching to try. "I was here first."
Tying thatch is just bird-work with bigger hands, and rough wood stops bothering (young).
"You ruined birds." (Elder) might have overdone it. No more lessons, ever.
Every elder teaches one young person everything they can in a single day.
Arms folded, already bored.
Every step explained twice.

pieces.label: The Dance of Shared Hearts
pieces.text: At the midsummer dance, (first_dancer) and (second_dancer) stand palm to palm for the old dance of shared hearts, stopped long ago because "sometimes the hearts get shared too well."

pieces.label: Spin All Three Times
pieces.text: One. Two. On the third spin the drums seem to stop, though the drummers are still drumming, and the fire leans towards them like a listening face...

pieces.label: Stop at Two and Bow
pieces.text: After two spins, (first_dancer) squeezes (second_dancer)'s hands and they let go, and bow, and the circle cheers. But the fire is still leaning towards them, and (second_dancer)'s palm is still tingling...

pieces.label: Ask the Elders to Join
pieces.text: Ask the Elders to Join.

pieces.label: Spin Four Times
pieces.text: Spin Four Times.
They let go, and (first_dancer) staggers backwards in (second_dancer)'s body. Shared too well.
The circle roars, the elders show everyone how, and the old step is back.
They dream of the third spin and wake up swapped. "The dance knew what you meant."
The tingling fades. Next year, they say. Next year, they don't.
The fire leans towards them like a listening face.
Palm to palm in the middle of the circle.
The drums seem to stop, though the drummers are still drumming.

pieces.label: The Coconut Season
pieces.text: It's coconut season, and (dozer) is dozing under the big palm by the gardens when (dozer.he/she) looks up at a bunch of coconuts, heavy as a child, swaying loose overhead.

pieces.label: Roll Out of the Way
pieces.text: (Dozer) rolls. The coconuts let go. There's a thud, and a second thud, and a third, much closer, and then a very loud one...

pieces.label: Try to Catch It
pieces.text: (Dozer) leaps up, arms out, like a fisher waiting for a thrown net. The bunch comes down faster than (dozer.he/she) expected...

pieces.label: Shout for Help
pieces.text: Shout for Help.

pieces.label: Stay Very Still
pieces.text: Stay Very Still.
One coconut bounces off the trunk onto (dozer)'s head. (dozer.He/She) remembers the rule, but not (dozer.his/her) name.
The coconuts land where (dozer.his/her) head was a moment ago. (Dozer) naps at home from now on.
(Dozer) catches all six, and by the end of the week everyone calls (dozer.him/her) (renamed), after the coconut catcher in the children's song.
A catch that makes (dozer) feel (dozer.he/she) can do anything, and for a while (dozer.he/she) does.
Don't stand under the palms when the wind gets up.
The best shade in the village.
A bunch of coconuts, heavy as a child.

pieces.label: The Baby at the Healers' Door
pieces.text: (Finder) finds a fed, warm baby in a sling on the healers' doorstep, with a carved shell token from a village three days' paddle away. Whoever left the baby loved it.

pieces.label: Take the Baby In
pieces.text: (Finder) lifts the sling and the baby settles against (finder.him/her) with a sigh, as if (finder.he/she) has been waiting for exactly this. The healers come out and look, and then look at (finder)...

pieces.label: Send Word to the Shell Village
pieces.text: A canoe goes out that morning, carrying the shell token and a message. (Finder) cares for the baby while they wait, sleeping with the sling beside (finder.his/her) mat...

pieces.label: Give the Baby to the Healers
pieces.text: Give the Baby to the Healers.

pieces.label: Ask (Name2)
pieces.text: Ask (Friend).
"The baby seems to have found you." The shell hangs on a cord round the baby's neck.
(Friend) simply holds out (friend.his/her) arms. A cradle by noon, a name by evening.
An exhausted young parent comes back with the canoe and stays, and the baby is never short of laps.
No answer comes, and the baby grows up spoiled rotten by the healers.
A little carved shell token tucked into the wrap.
The baby is fed, warm, and wrapped in good cloth.
The herb-smell of the healers' hut.

pieces.label: The Fruit with Two Stones
pieces.text: The old tree planted by two sisters so alike their mother mixed them up has given a single golden fruit, with two identical stones inside. "Eat it all, and it gives you what it gave the sisters."

pieces.label: Eat It All
pieces.text: It's the sweetest fruit (finder) has ever tasted, like honey and sunshine. (finder.He/She) eats every scrap, licks (finder.his/her) fingers, and then feels very, very strange, as if (finder.he/she) is standing in two places at once...

pieces.label: Plant the Stones
pieces.text: (Finder) plants the two stones side by side in the soft earth by the old tree, waters them, and goes home. In the night, there's a sound from the garden like something breathing...

pieces.label: Share It with a Friend
pieces.text: Share It with a Friend.

pieces.label: Give It to the Elders
pieces.text: Give It to the Elders.
On the step {#made:stands someone|stand two people|stand three people} exactly like (finder). "Sisters. Or close enough."
Another (finder) is eating breakfast by the fire, and they agree to take turns with the chores.
A soil-covered person with (finder)'s face and nothing else of (finder) sits in the garden.
The seedlings wither, and (finder)'s face is new. "That's fair."
The fruit is golden and heavy, the sweetest (finder) has ever tasted.
Two stones inside, side by side, exactly the same.
A sound from the garden like something breathing.

pieces.label: The Pearl Bed
pieces.text: After three deep dives, (diver), the best diver, has found a clam as big as a sleeping mat with a pearl the size of a fist, but (diver.his/her) ears ache and (diver.his/her) chest is tight.

pieces.label: Dive Once More
pieces.text: (Diver) takes three long breaths and goes down, into the cold, down past where the light turns green, then grey...

pieces.label: Wait for Tomorrow
pieces.text: (Diver) hauls (diver.himself/herself) into the canoe. (diver.His/Her) ears are ringing, and they're still ringing that evening, and the next morning...

pieces.label: Send Another Diver
pieces.text: Send Another Diver.

pieces.label: Leave It Forever
pieces.text: Leave It Forever.
The divers count far past where (diver) should have come up. Nobody dives the channel for a long time.
(Diver) comes up with a pearl that shines like the moon.
The ringing fades, and most of (diver)'s hearing with it. (diver.He/She) teaches diving by signs.
The clam has closed. "It'll keep."
Down past where the light turns green, then grey.
A clam as big as a sleeping mat.
(diver.His/Her) ears are ringing.

pieces.label: The Old Couple's Wish
pieces.text: On their fiftieth anniversary, (first_elder) and (friend) are offered a little pot of stream water by a travelling storyteller: drink it to get their youth back, or pour it into the stream where they met.

pieces.label: Drink It Together
pieces.text: They pass the pot back and forth, a sip each, until it's gone. The water tastes of moss and stones and, very faintly, of the morning they met...

pieces.label: Pour It into the Stream
pieces.text: They walk down to the stream together, slowly, and pour the water into the place where they met. The stream seems to brighten for a moment, and then runs on as before...

pieces.label: Give It to the Village
pieces.text: Give It to the Village.

pieces.label: Drink Half Each and Pour the Rest
pieces.text: Drink Half Each and Pour the Rest.
Fifteen years gone from both, and two elders splash about in the stream like children.
Young faces, old knees. "At least we look nice while we complain."
A feast by the stream, and the story of the day they met told until the children can recite it.
"I'd rather have the years we had than get them back."
(First_elder) fell in and (friend) laughed so hard (friend.he/she) fell in too.
The water tastes of moss and stones.
Fifty years of small things.

pieces.label: The Turtle's Nest
pieces.text: On a moonlit walk, (hopeful_parent) and (friend), who have hoped for a child for a long time, find a sea turtle blocked by a log on her way to lay her eggs. Helping a mother turtle brings children, the fishers say.

pieces.label: Move the Log
pieces.text: They heave the log out of the way, and the turtle drags herself up past the tide line, digs her nest, and lays her eggs, while (hopeful_parent) and (friend) sit in the sand holding hands and watching...

pieces.label: Keep Back and Watch
pieces.text: They sit back in the shadow of the palms and watch. The turtle rests for a long time. Then, slowly, she finds her own way round the end of the log...

pieces.label: Guard the Nest All Night
pieces.text: Guard the Nest All Night.

pieces.label: Fetch the Fishers
pieces.text: Fetch the Fishers.
A month later a baby is expected, and every year they make sure the hatchlings reach the sea.
The healer listens again and laughs: {#babies:one big, strong baby|twins|triplets}. "I'm just glad she didn't give us all of them."
No baby that year. They count the hatchlings to the sea. "Next year."
The week the hatchlings come out, a baby is expected. "She took her time too."
The turtle looks at them with old, wet eyes.
She drags herself up past the tide line.
The hatchlings run for the waves.

pieces.label: The Granary Floor
pieces.text: The granary floor drops a hand's width with a crack while (storekeeper) is inside counting baskets. (builder) can prop the split stilt while (storekeeper) hands the food out, or (storekeeper) can jump out now.

pieces.label: Prop It and Save the Food
pieces.text: (builder) jams a log under the split stilt and leans on it with all (builder.his/her) weight. "Go!" (builder.he/she) shouts. "Hand them down! Quickly!" (Storekeeper) starts passing baskets out of the door as fast as (storekeeper.he/she) can...

pieces.label: Get Out Now
pieces.text: (Storekeeper) drops everything and jumps from the door. Behind (storekeeper.him/her), with a long, slow groan, the granary leans, and leans, and falls...

pieces.label: Throw the Baskets Out the Door
pieces.text: Throw the Baskets Out the Door.

pieces.label: Call the Whole Village
pieces.text: Call the Whole Village.
Not a basket lost. (builder) can't lift (builder.his/her) arms for two days.
A second stilt goes without warning, and the granary comes down with (storekeeper) inside.
The new granary on ironwood stilts is the best-built thing in the village.
The scholars' spare bark records were under the floor. They aren't out of the rain anymore.
A crack like a breaking bone.
Dust pours down from the roof.
The granary leans, and leans, and falls.

pieces.label: The Mist Canoe
pieces.text: On a misty morning, alone on the beach, (watcher) sees the shape of a canoe waiting past the shallows, the one the old stories say comes from "the island behind the mist" and sometimes waits for a passenger.

pieces.label: Wade Out
pieces.text: (Watcher) wades out, knee deep, waist deep. The canoe is closer than it looked, and further, both at once. A hand that (watcher.he/she) can't quite see reaches down to help (watcher.him/her) in...

pieces.label: Call Out from the Beach
pieces.text: "Who's there?" (watcher) calls. The paddling stops. For a long moment the mist is completely silent. Then someone, somewhere, calls back...

pieces.label: Run for the Fishers
pieces.text: Run for the Fishers.

pieces.label: Light a Fire on the Beach
pieces.text: Light a Fire on the Beach.
(Watcher)'s footprints go down to the water's edge and stop. Friends leave a light burning on misty mornings.
Only a moment passes, but (watcher)'s face has aged as if (watcher.he/she) had been gone for years. "Very peaceful, and very far."
The canoe is solid, with two lost adults and a baby in it. They decide to stay.
The voice calls back (watcher)'s own name, and the mist goes in a rush.
The shape of a canoe, and the soft sound of paddles.
Closer than it looked, and further, both at once.
A single white seabird on the water.

pieces.label: The Healers' Garden
pieces.text: Three villagers have a stomach sickness and caterpillars have eaten the right herbs in the neglected healers' garden. (Helper) can save the garden, or walk all day to where the herb grows wild.

pieces.label: Save the Garden
pieces.text: (Helper) kneels in the dirt and starts picking caterpillars off the leaves one by one, dropping them in a bowl to carry out to the forest...

pieces.label: Walk to the Far Valley
pieces.text: (Helper) sets off at dawn with an empty basket, over the ridge and down into the far valley, where the wild herbs grow thick along the stream...

pieces.label: Send the Children for Caterpillars
pieces.text: Send the Children for Caterpillars.

pieces.label: Ask the Healers What Else Works
pieces.text: Ask the Healers What Else Works.
Every healer comes out to help, and they learn more about their garden in a day than in a year.
At sunset there's still a caterpillar on every plant, looking at (helper).
Back after dark with an overflowing basket, and by morning the sick are sitting up.
Somewhere along the long walk (helper) stops minding it, and stops minding the smell of herbs too.
Caterpillars dropped in a bowl to carry out to the forest.
The wild herbs grow thick along the stream.
Fingers green, back screaming.

pieces.label: The Forgetting Fruit
pieces.text: Out gathering, (gatherer) has eaten a handful of small blue fruits, the kind the old healers once gave to people in great pain to make them forget, and that made them forget other things too.

pieces.label: Try to Bring It Back Up
pieces.text: (Gatherer) sticks a finger down (gatherer.his/her) throat and is very sick in the bushes. (gatherer.He/She) sits back, shaky and sweating, and tries to remember (gatherer.his/her) way home...

pieces.label: Sit Down and Wait
pieces.text: (Gatherer) sits down against a tree and waits. The forest seems very bright and very quiet. Thoughts drift through (gatherer.his/her) head and float away like leaves on a stream...

pieces.label: Run for the Healers
pieces.text: Run for the Healers.

pieces.label: Drink from the Stream
pieces.text: Drink from the Stream.
(Gatherer) knows every friend, but not the name they're calling. The village calls (gatherer.him/her) "?".
A lifelong fear of the dark is simply gone.
(Gatherer)'s love of learning floats away like a leaf on a stream.
Nothing is missing, and the shrub goes behind a fence in the healers' garden.
The taste is like cold water and mint.
(gatherer.His/Her) head feels like a hut swept clean.
Thoughts float away like leaves on a stream.

pieces.label: The Wave That Gives Back
pieces.text: The "wave that gives back" rises over the reef on a calm day, and right in front of (beachcomber), something glints in the sand: (beachcomber.his/her) own bone necklace, lost for years. The sea sometimes takes a thing in exchange.

pieces.label: Grab It and Run
pieces.text: (Beachcomber) snatches up the necklace and turns to run, but the wave is faster. It picks (beachcomber.him/her) up, rolls (beachcomber.him/her) over and over in green water, and drops (beachcomber.him/her) on the sand...

pieces.label: Just Run
pieces.text: (Beachcomber) leaves the necklace and runs up the beach as fast as (beachcomber.he/she) can. The wave crashes down behind (beachcomber.him/her), and foams up to (beachcomber.his/her) heels, and stops...

pieces.label: Stand and Face the Wave
pieces.text: Stand and Face the Wave.

pieces.label: Shout a Warning
pieces.text: Shout a Warning.
Coughing beside (beachcomber) is somebody with (beachcomber.his/her) face and a different laugh.
The wave rolls back and the beach is empty, except for the necklace.
Someone lies on the sand wearing the necklace, with (beachcomber)'s face and someone else's everything.
The necklace is still there, washed clean, and the wave asks for nothing.
A green wall rising over the reef.
Old paddles, lost nets, once a whole canoe.
Half hoping and half afraid.

pieces.label: The Wrestling Match
pieces.text: In the last round of the harvest wrestling match, (challenger) has the champion (champion) almost down, but (champion) is twisting (challenger.his/her) arm back and it hurts, badly.

pieces.label: Push Through It
pieces.text: (Challenger) grits (challenger.his/her) teeth and heaves. There's a sound from (challenger.his/her) shoulder that the whole ring hears, and then (champion) is going over, and down, and the crowd roars...

pieces.label: Tap the Sand
pieces.text: (Challenger) slaps the sand three times. (Champion) lets go at once, and helps (challenger.him/her) up, and the crowd cheers for both of them...

pieces.label: Twist Free
pieces.text: Twist Free.

pieces.label: Call for the Referee
pieces.text: Call for the Referee.
(Challenger) wins, and (challenger.his/her) shoulder never works properly again. (challenger.He/She) becomes the best referee the beach has ever had.
(Champion) hits the sand, laughing. "Finally. Someone to train with."
"I gave it everything. That's enough." (Challenger) never wrestles or races again.
The best match in years, and little wrestling matches break out all over the village.
The whole village is in a ring around them, chanting.
Every harvest, (champion) wins.
Months of training in secret.

pieces.label: Two of the Same Name
pieces.text: Two villagers share a first name, and it has caused a disaster: the wrong fish, the wrong love note, nearly the wrong remedy. (Younger), the younger, is expected to offer to change.

pieces.label: Offer to Change It
pieces.text: (Younger) stands up in the meeting and says (younger.he/she) will change. Everyone looks relieved, and then everyone starts suggesting names at once...

pieces.label: Ask for Another Way
pieces.text: "Why don't we just call us something different?" (younger) says. "Like 'the tall one' and 'the one with the goat'?" The elders look at each other...

pieces.label: Ask (Name2) to Change
pieces.text: Ask (Namesake) to Change.

pieces.label: Draw Lots
pieces.text: Draw Lots.
"(renamed). The name of the earliest riser I ever knew." It fits.
A name pulled from a bowl of leaves. "That'll do."
Adding a little bit to each name mostly works, and (younger) is so relieved that (younger.he/she) starts coming to village gatherings.
"Which one?" becomes a village joke.
The healers nearly gave the wrong remedy.
Everyone starts suggesting names at once.
"The tall one" and "the one with the goat."

pieces.label: The Termites
pieces.text: Termites have moved into the village, and too many posts sound hollow when (builder), the best builder, knocks on them. Smoke them out and sleep on the beach, or replace every post with ironwood.

pieces.label: Smoke Them Out
pieces.text: The whole village carries its sleeping mats down to the beach, and (builder) lights the bitter-leaf fires. The smoke is yellow, and smells like burnt hair and rotten fruit...

pieces.label: Replace the Posts with Ironwood
pieces.text: Everyone who can carry wood heads up into the hills where the ironwood grows. It is so heavy it takes four people to carry one post...

pieces.label: Patch the Worst and Hope
pieces.text: Patch the Worst and Hope.

pieces.label: Ask the Old Builders
pieces.text: Ask the Old Builders.
Three nights on the beach, and the huts smell of bitter leaves for a month. Nobody minds.
The builders rebuild with raised stones under every post, and all come out of it better.
Every hut stands on ironwood. "Built to last." The post rings like a bell.
"I've built enough. Let someone else knock on things."
A door frame turned to powder in someone's hand.
The smoke smells like burnt hair and rotten fruit.
It takes four people to carry one ironwood post.

pieces.label: The Old Woman of the Tide Pools
pieces.text: At low tide (gatherer) finds the old woman the children talk about, combing her grey hair with a fish bone. She offers to take some years off (gatherer.him/her), or to give (gatherer.him/her) some of hers.

pieces.label: Sit and Let Her Comb
pieces.text: (Gatherer) sits on the warm rock, and the old woman combs (gatherer.his/her) hair with the fish bone, slowly, humming a song (gatherer.he/she) almost knows. The tide pools sparkle...

pieces.label: Politely Say No
pieces.text: "Thank you," says (gatherer), "but I'm happy with the years I have." The old woman laughs, a sound like water running out of a pool, and keeps on combing...

pieces.label: Ask Who She Is
pieces.text: Ask Who She Is.

pieces.label: Offer to Comb Her Hair
pieces.text: Offer to Comb Her Hair.
A still pool shows (gatherer)'s face younger. "Better," she says, and slips into the water.
"I gave you some of mine. They're good years. Look after them."
"Polite. That deserves something." A cold wet finger on the forehead, and (gatherer)'s face is years younger.
The rock is empty except for a fish bone and a few long grey hairs.
She combs her long grey hair with a fish bone.
A laugh like water running out of a pool.
The children say she's as old as the sea.

pieces.label: The Sick Canoe
pieces.text: A canoe brings a family who left an island where a fever went round. One of them is coughing. (healer) worries the fever could come with them.

pieces.label: Let Them In
pieces.text: (healer) checks each of them carefully, listening to their chests and looking in their eyes, and then waves them up to the village...

pieces.label: Camp at the Far End First
pieces.text: The family nods; they understand. They pitch a shelter at the far end of the beach, and the village leaves food and water halfway between, every morning, for ten days...

pieces.label: Check Them on the Beach
pieces.text: Check Them on the Beach.

pieces.label: Ask the Elders
pieces.text: Ask the Elders.
The cough was only a cough. A parent, a teen and a child settle in, and decide to stay.
The cough wasn't only a cough. Three villagers are feverish, and the family helps nurse them before moving on.
On the tenth day they're all well, and the hidden baby is passed round like a prize.
They don't want to be a worry and paddle on to cousins.
Food and water left halfway between, every morning.
The sea is getting rough.
They pitch a shelter at the far end of the beach.

pieces.label: The Rope Swing over the Gorge
pieces.text: Swinging out over the gorge on a vine rope is the bravest thing the young people know. (Swinger) has done it ten times, but today the vine looks frayed where it rubs the branch.

pieces.label: Swing
pieces.text: (Swinger) runs, and jumps, and the gorge opens up beneath (swinger.him/her), wide and green and roaring. At the top of the swing, (swinger.he/she) hears a soft creak from the branch...

pieces.label: Replace the Rope First
pieces.text: "The rope's going," (swinger) says, and lets go of it. The others groan and mock, and then one of them looks at the frayed part, and stops mocking...

pieces.label: Swing Low
pieces.text: Swing Low.

pieces.label: Fetch the Builders
pieces.text: Fetch the Builders.
The rope parts at the top of the swing. Nobody swings over the gorge again.
(Swinger) hits the trunk on the way back, and wakes knowing everything but (swinger.his/her) name.
The rotten branch cracks, and (swinger)'s back is never the same. (swinger.He/She) tells the young people which branches to trust.
The builders make a proper swing, and soon even the elders are screaming with joy.
The gorge opens up, wide and green and roaring.
A soft creak from the branch.
The river is a long, long way down.

pieces.label: The Paired Gourds
pieces.text: (First_friend) and (second_friend) find a pair of carved gourds made for two old friends who wanted to "know each other's minds." Whoever drinks from them together gets their wish, more or less.

pieces.label: Drink from Both Together
pieces.text: They fill the gourds, count to three, and drink. The water is very cold, and tastes of the other person's favourite food...

pieces.label: Share One Gourd
pieces.text: They fill one gourd and pass it back and forth, a sip each, until it's empty. The other gourd, still on its cord, seems to sway a little on its own...

pieces.label: Pour Them Out
pieces.text: Pour Them Out.

pieces.label: Ask the Elders
pieces.text: Ask the Elders.
Each sees (first_friend.himself/herself). "More or less," the elders said. Rather more.
"You're thinking about lunch." "That's not magic. That's you."
The empty gourd falls off its peg, and they wake in the wrong bodies. "The elders said safer."
Each can suddenly do what the other does best.
Two faces carved looking at each other.
The water tastes of the other person's favourite food.
The other gourd sways a little on its own.

pieces.label: The Gourd Cradle on the River
pieces.text: The river is high and brown after the rains, and a hollowed gourd tied with vine comes spinning past (rescuer) with a baby peering out of it, heading for the rapids.

pieces.label: Climb Out on the Log
pieces.text: (Rescuer) edges out along the slippery log, the brown water roaring underneath, and lies flat, arm out, as the gourd comes spinning towards (rescuer.him/her)...

pieces.label: Run to the Calm Pool
pieces.text: (Rescuer) runs, slipping in the mud, along the bank, past the roaring rapids, to where the river widens into a brown, slow pool. (rescuer.He/She) wades in up to (rescuer.his/her) chest and waits...

pieces.label: Throw a Rope
pieces.text: Throw a Rope.

pieces.label: Shout for (Name2)
pieces.text: Shout for (Friend).
(Rescuer) drags the gourd to the bank. Nobody comes down the river after the baby.
(Friend) grabs (rescuer)'s ankle just in time. "I suppose we're keeping the baby."
The gourd floats into (rescuer)'s arms, and an hour later two muddy parents come stumbling down the bank.
The healers warm the baby until the little one is pink and screaming, and a cousin comes from upriver.
A small face peering out of a hole in the gourd.
The river is high and brown and fast.
The fallen log is slippery under (rescuer)'s hands.

pieces.label: The Banyan's Bark
pieces.text: The oldest banyan is shedding its soft silver bark, which old healers laid over faces because the tree "shares its years," sometimes old, sometimes young.

pieces.label: Lay It Over the Face
pieces.text: (Wearer) lies back in the shade and lays the bark over (wearer.his/her) face. It settles like a damp cloth. Through it (wearer.he/she) can hear the tree creaking, like an old person stretching...

pieces.label: Wrap It Round the Arm
pieces.text: (Wearer) wraps the strip round (wearer.his/her) forearm and ties it with grass, and goes about (wearer.his/her) day. By evening the bark has grown warm, and then hot, and then cool again...

pieces.label: Sleep Under the Tree
pieces.text: Sleep Under the Tree.

pieces.label: Give It to the Healers
pieces.text: Give It to the Healers.
(Wearer)'s face is years younger, and the bark has gone grey and brittle.
(Wearer)'s face has the tree's years on it now. "They're the ones it values most."
(Wearer)'s face is new, like a new branch on the same tree.
Only a pale patch in the shape of the bark, which fades in a week.
The bark comes off soft and silver, and smells of rain.
The tree creaks like an old person stretching.
New shoots from old wood.

pieces.label: The Torch Fishers
pieces.text: Torch-fishing on the reef flats on a moonless night, (fisher) has followed a school of silver fish too far. The other torches are far away, the water is rising and (fisher.his/her) torch is sputtering.

pieces.label: Head for the Other Torches
pieces.text: (Fisher) wades towards the lights. The water is at (fisher.his/her) waist, then (fisher.his/her) chest. Then the torch goes out...

pieces.label: Follow the Reef Edge
pieces.text: (Fisher) turns along the reef edge, feeling for the coral with (fisher.his/her) feet. The water stays at (fisher.his/her) knees. It's slow. The torch sputters lower...

pieces.label: Stand Still and Shout
pieces.text: Stand Still and Shout.

pieces.label: Climb Onto a Coral Head
pieces.text: Climb onto a Coral Head.
(Fisher)'s torch goes out and there's no answer. The fishers leave a torch burning on the beach on moonless nights.
A hand grabs (fisher)'s arm in the dark: the oldest fisher, counting the steps out loud.
In the dark, (fisher) steps into the fast channel. The fishers mark it with white stones.
The silver fish swirl back round (fisher)'s knees, and (fisher.he/she) wades in at dawn with a full basket.
The fish swim up to the light.
The other torches are far away.
The tide comes in fast over the flats.

pieces.label: The Wedding Night Feast
pieces.text: At (newlywed) and (friend)'s wedding feast, the oldest woman brings them two cups of a sweet drink from wedding flowers, "for a family, if you want one." They do.

pieces.label: Drink the Flower Cups
pieces.text: The drink tastes of honey and petals and something sharp, like lemon. The old woman watches them drink every drop, then nods and walks off without a word...

pieces.label: Join the Game
pieces.text: They put the cups aside for later and join the blindfold game, which involves a great deal of falling over and everyone shrieking with laughter...

pieces.label: Share One Cup
pieces.text: Share One Cup.

pieces.label: Save Them for Tomorrow
pieces.text: Save Them for Tomorrow.
By the next feast a baby is expected, and the old woman takes full credit.
The healer hears {#babies:one strong heartbeat|two heartbeats|three heartbeats}. "I may have made it a bit strong."
The cups are empty and a sleepy goat lies beside them. That spring, the goat has three kids.
No flowers at all, and a baby is expected anyway. "Laughter's better than flowers."
Flowers that bloom only at weddings.
The drink tastes of honey and petals and something sharp.
The fire burns low.

pieces.label: The Floating Chest
pieces.text: After a storm a canoe lies wrecked on the reef, and a matting-lined chest floats in the lagoon with a baby inside, put there by someone who loved the baby when the storm hit.

pieces.label: Take the Baby Home
pieces.text: (Finder) wraps the baby in the soft cloth from the chest and carries the little one up the beach. The baby grips (finder.his/her) finger hard, as if to make sure (finder.he/she) doesn't put the baby down...

pieces.label: Keep Searching the Reef
pieces.text: (Finder) passes the baby to the healers and paddles out to the wreck with the fishers. They search every crack in the reef, calling, until the tide turns...

pieces.label: Give the Baby to the Healers
pieces.text: Give the Baby to the Healers.

pieces.label: Call (Name2)
pieces.text: Call (Friend).
Nobody else is found. A cradle is built from the chest's own wood.
(Friend) starts clearing a space by the fire, and the baby wakes up laughing every morning.
"The baby wouldn't stop crying for you. We think the baby has decided."
An aunt comes from two islands away and takes the baby home. Glad and sad, both at once.
A wooden chest lined with matting.
A water gourd and a bundle of soft cloth.
The canoe is broken in two on the outer reef.

pieces.label: The Twin Stars
pieces.text: Two shooting stars fall side by side into the hills, and at first light (finder) finds two warm, glittering stones. The elders say twin stars "make two of whatever they touch."

pieces.label: Pick Up Both
pieces.text: (Finder) picks up a stone in each hand. They're warm, and grow warmer, and (finder.his/her) hands begin to glow, and then (finder.his/her) arms, and then all of (finder.him/her)...

pieces.label: Pick Up Just One
pieces.text: (Finder) picks up one stone and leaves the other. The stone in (finder.his/her) hand glows briefly, then dims. The one on the ground flickers, as if it's looking for something...

pieces.label: Fetch the Elders
pieces.text: Fetch the Elders.

pieces.label: Throw Them in the Sea
pieces.text: Throw Them in the Sea.
The light flashes, and {#made:a second (finder) stands|two more (finder)s stand|three more (finder)s stand} in the scorched grass. "We did warn you."
A second (finder) rubs (finder.his/her) eyes in the grass, and the elders bury the other stone very quickly.
One star alone copies only the outside. The newcomer is someone else entirely.
The stone glitters faintly on a shelf for years. Nothing gets doubled.
A soft double thump felt through the sand.
Two small, warm stones in a scorched patch of grass.
An elder once saw a fishing net doubled.

pieces.label: The Wild Boar
pieces.text: A wild boar as big as a small canoe has been raiding the gardens, and at dusk it comes out of the trees, lowers its head and looks right at (defender).

pieces.label: Stand and Shout
pieces.text: (Defender) bangs two pots together and yells at the top of (defender.his/her) lungs. The boar paws the ground, snorts, and charges...

pieces.label: Climb the Tree
pieces.text: (Defender) scrambles up the nearest tree just as the boar thunders past underneath. It circles the trunk, grunting, and settles down to wait...

pieces.label: Throw Fruit the Other Way
pieces.text: Throw Fruit the Other Way.

pieces.label: Run for the Village
pieces.text: Run for the Village.
The boar crashes through the stakes and catches (defender) with a tusk. (Defender)'s leg is never strong again, and the boar never comes back.
Three steps away, the boar swerves and bolts. (Defender) sits down very suddenly in the beans.
Near dawn the branch gives way, and (defender)'s back never fully heals.
A night up a tree with a boar underneath, and the thrill of running is gone.
Tearing up taro and flattening the beans.
A fence of sharpened stakes.
The boar paws the ground and snorts.

pieces.label: The Shaking Ground
pieces.text: The ground shakes for as long as a long breath. Roofs have slid, and inside the half-collapsed hut next to (rescuer), someone is calling for help. A second shake often follows.

pieces.label: Go In Now
pieces.text: (Rescuer) ducks under the sagging doorway into the dusty dark. The voice is coming from under a fallen shelf. (Rescuer) heaves at it...

pieces.label: Wait for the Builders
pieces.text: (Rescuer) shouts through the wall, "Hold on! We're coming!" and runs for (builder), who comes at once with three builders and an armful of posts...

pieces.label: Dig Through the Wall
pieces.text: Dig Through the Wall.

pieces.label: Call Everyone
pieces.text: Call Everyone.
An elder crawls out coughing and furious and unhurt, and brings (rescuer) stew for a month.
The second shake comes just as (rescuer) pushes the elder through the doorway.
Posts wedged, the elder out, and the props hold through the second shake.
A beam swings down across (rescuer)'s back. (rescuer.He/She) spends a lot of time in the sun after that.
The village is full of dust and screaming chickens.
A whole row of drying racks has gone over.
"Hold on! We're coming!"

pieces.label: The Day the Sun Went Dark
pieces.text: At midday the sun goes dark, and the elders say that in the dark "shadows wander, and can come home to the wrong person." (First) and (second)'s shadows are touching on the sand.

pieces.label: Stand Still and Wait
pieces.text: They stand frozen, hardly breathing. In the strange half-dark, their shadows ripple on the sand like water, and slide together, and apart...

pieces.label: Run Apart
pieces.text: They turn and run in opposite directions along the sand. Behind them, in the half-dark, their shadows stretch and stretch, still touching, longer than any shadow should be...

pieces.label: Hold Hands
pieces.text: Hold Hands.

pieces.label: Go Indoors
pieces.text: Go Indoors.
The shadows come home to the wrong person. The next dark sun is not due for a hundred years.
The sun slides back, and each shadow is where it should be.
Stretched too far, the shadows snap back to the wrong ends. "That didn't work."
For weeks both of them check their shadows every time they step out of a doorway.
As if something is taking a bite out of the sun.
The birds stop singing.
Their shadows ripple on the sand like water.

pieces.label: The Sea-Glass Window
pieces.text: (Maker) has finished a round window of sea glass in (maker.his/her) hut wall. In the old days, someone who made something beautiful could take a new name; and sea-glass light "shows you as the sea sees you."

pieces.label: Ask for a New Name
pieces.text: The elders confer for a long time, heads together, muttering, and then the oldest one stands up and clears (maker.his/her) throat...

pieces.label: Stand in the Colours
pieces.text: (Maker) stands in the middle of the floor while the sun pours through the window, and green and blue and white light washes over (maker.his/her) face. It's warm, and cool, like being underwater...

pieces.label: Let the Children Decide
pieces.text: Let the Children Decide.

pieces.label: Thank the Elders and Say No
pieces.text: Thank the Elders and Say No.
"(renamed). The first person who ever set sea glass in a wall." The window becomes (renamed)'s window.
The children choose a perfectly ordinary name nobody has. "Because it's new."
(Maker)'s face is smoothed and reshaped like glass the sea has rolled for years.
Just light, and a sunburn on (maker)'s nose.
Green and blue and white sea glass.
The morning sun throws colours all over the floor.
Like being underwater.

pieces.label: The Waterfall Curtain
pieces.text: Filling gourds at the waterfall, (water_carrier) has stood too long in the spray, and the reflection in the falling curtain steps forward. "The waterfall learns your face," the elders say.

pieces.label: Reach into the Water
pieces.text: (Water_carrier) reaches out. (water_carrier.His/Her) hand goes through the falling water, cold as ice, and closes round another hand, warm, on the other side...

pieces.label: Step Back
pieces.text: (Water_carrier) takes a step back, and then another. The reflection in the water doesn't step back. It stays where it is, close to the front of the curtain, as if it is waiting...

pieces.label: Call Out
pieces.text: Call Out.

pieces.label: Throw a Gourd Through
pieces.text: Throw a Gourd Through.
Someone comes through the curtain with (water_carrier)'s face and nothing else of (water_carrier).
The warm hand pulls harder, and (water_carrier) is gone through the curtain.
It walks out onto the rocks with someone else's opinions about everything. "Hello."
The spray gives (water_carrier)'s face back years younger.
A thin, shining curtain over a dark hollow.
The children say someone lives behind it.
Cold as ice on one side, warm on the other.

pieces.label: The Ancestor Masks
pieces.text: Once a generation the village brings out two carved masks, an old face and a child's face, that "lend their years" for a song and sometimes forget to take them back. (Dancer) is chosen to dance.

pieces.label: Wear the Old Face
pieces.text: The old mask is heavy, and smells of smoke and wood oil. Behind it, (dancer) feels (dancer.his/her) back bend and (dancer.his/her) steps slow, and (dancer.he/she) dances the old dance the way the old ones did...

pieces.label: Wear the Child's Face
pieces.text: The child's mask is light as a leaf. Behind it, (dancer) feels like running, and does, round and round the fire, laughing, while the drums go faster and faster...

pieces.label: Wear Both Masks
pieces.text: Wear Both Masks.

pieces.label: Let Someone Else Dance
pieces.text: Let Someone Else Dance.
The mask keeps its years in (dancer), ten of them. "It forgets sometimes. It's very old."
(Dancer)'s face comes out younger. "You gave them back with interest."
Five years of aches and worries simply gone. "That one forgets as well."
Just a dance, and the children make (dancer.him/her) do it again and again.
The old mask smells of smoke and wood oil.
The child's mask is light as a leaf.
The drums go faster and faster.

pieces.label: The Canoe That Didn't Come Back
pieces.text: (First_fisher) and (second_fisher) went fishing two days ago and a storm blew through. This morning (first_fisher) sees smoke on a sandbar that only shows at low tide, and the sea is still rough.

pieces.label: Go Now
pieces.text: Three canoes go out into the rough water, paddlers soaked to the skin, fighting every wave. The smoke gets closer, and then they can see figures on the sand, waving...

pieces.label: Wait for the Sea to Calm
pieces.text: The fishers wait, pacing the beach all day and all night. At dawn the sea is flat, and they go out fast, and the sandbar is just breaking the surface...

pieces.label: Light an Answering Fire
pieces.text: Light an Answering Fire.

pieces.label: Send the Strongest Paddlers Only
pieces.text: Send the Strongest Paddlers Only.
Only (second_fisher) is on the sandbar. (First_fisher) was swept away in the storm.
Both are there, with a parent, a teen and a child they pulled from the water. Everyone comes home.
(First_fisher) held (second_fisher) above the water all night, and (second_fisher) didn't last until morning.
Both are safe, arguing about whose fault it was, for most of the next year.
A faint smudge of smoke on a sandbar.
The sandbar will be under water again by evening.
A little fire of driftwood.

pieces.label: The Scholar's Mixture
pieces.text: (Scholar) has brewed a mixture from the old scholars' notes that "copies what it touches," and a drop of it splashes onto (scholar.his/her) hand.

pieces.label: Wash It Off at Once
pieces.text: (Scholar) plunges (scholar.his/her) hand into the water bowl and scrubs. The water turns green, then bright green, then starts to steam...

pieces.label: Watch What It Does
pieces.text: (Scholar) holds (scholar.his/her) hand very still, and watches. The drop spreads, and glows, and then the glow climbs up (scholar.his/her) arm, and over (scholar.his/her) shoulder, and then all over (scholar.him/her)...

pieces.label: Call the Other Scholars
pieces.text: Call the Other Scholars.

pieces.label: Wipe It on a Sandal
pieces.text: Wipe It on a Sandal.
The fumes "take the newest things first," and (scholar)'s name goes.
The steam settles like dew, and (scholar)'s face is years younger.
The glow peels away and becomes another (scholar). "We should write this down."
Nothing is copied, but (scholar) understands the mixture at last.
A pale green steam.
It copied a scholar's sandal and then the scholar's foot.
Ground shell, a glowing moss and three drops of sap.

pieces.label: The Remedy from the Deep
pieces.text: (Patient) has had a deep, wet cough for a month. The oldest fisher swears by deep-water octopus ink with honey; the healers' slow remedy smells awful and takes a month.

pieces.label: The Octopus Ink
pieces.text: The oldest fisher dives three times and comes up with a bowl of black ink and a scowl. Mixed with honey it looks like tar, and tastes like the bottom of the sea...

pieces.label: The Healers' Slow Remedy
pieces.text: Every morning for a month, (patient) holds (patient.his/her) nose and drinks the healers' brew, which smells like a wet dog and tastes worse...

pieces.label: Both at Once
pieces.text: Both at Once.

pieces.label: Rest in the Sun
pieces.text: Rest in the Sun.
Three spoonfuls, three days, and the cough is gone.
The cough goes, and every fish tastes faintly of octopus ink forever.
Slow but sure. (Patient) keeps coming by the healers' hut for the fruit.
The cough fades with the dry season, and nobody can say which remedy did it.
Ink that looks like tar and tastes like the bottom of the sea.
A brew that smells like a wet dog.
A deep, wet cough that nothing will shift.

pieces.label: The Moon Charm
pieces.text: (First_partner) and (second_partner) have hoped for a child for two years. The wise-woman's charm: hold a carved wooden fish in the full moonlight by the lagoon and ask. "Sometimes it listens to who's holding the fish."

pieces.label: (Name1) Holds the Fish
pieces.text: They sit by the lagoon with the moon on the water, and (first_partner) holds the carved fish in both hands, and they ask, quietly, together...

pieces.label: (Name2) Holds the Fish
pieces.text: (First_partner) puts the carved fish into (second_partner)'s hands. "You ask," (first_partner.he/she) says. They sit together in the moonlight, and (second_partner) asks...

pieces.label: Hold It Together
pieces.text: Hold It Together.

pieces.label: Ask the Wise-Woman to Hold It
pieces.text: Ask the Wise-Woman to Hold It.
A month later a baby is expected, and the carved fish hangs over the cradle.
Nothing changes, and the full moon becomes their favourite night of the month.
It's (second_partner) who is expecting: {#babies:one baby|twins|triplets}. "The moon was in a generous mood."
On the next full moon after the rains, a baby is expected. "The moon is slow, but it listens."
The moon on the water.
A carved wooden fish held between them.
They ask, quietly, together.

pieces.label: The Giant Eel
pieces.text: A moray eel as thick as a man's leg is coiled in the village's best fish trap, with teeth that "could take a hand off without noticing."

pieces.label: Open the Trap Carefully
pieces.text: (Fisher) wades in and reaches for the lashing at the end of the trap, keeping (fisher.his/her) other hand well away. The eel's head turns, slowly, to follow (fisher.his/her) fingers...

pieces.label: Go Back for Help
pieces.text: (Fisher) backs away and runs for the village. By the time (fisher.he/she) comes back with four fishers and a long pole, the eel is thrashing in the trap, and the trap is creaking...

pieces.label: Wait for It to Sleep
pieces.text: Wait for It to Sleep.

pieces.label: Lift the Whole Trap Out
pieces.text: Lift the Whole Trap Out.
The eel catches (fisher)'s hand on the way out. (fisher.He/She) makes the best fish hooks in the village instead.
(Fisher) steps back onto the slick rocks and the current takes (fisher.him/her). The traps move upstream.
A forked pole, a twist of the lashing, a hard shove. (Fisher) practises it all season.
The eel bursts out through the trap. Three seasons of work wrecked, and the joy of fishing with it.
Something has been stealing fish from the traps.
The eel's head turns slowly to follow (fisher.his/her) fingers.
Three seasons in the making.

pieces.label: The Rope Bridge
pieces.text: The young people have built a swaying rope bridge across the ravine, designed by (designer), and (designer) wants to be the first across. (builder) has gone pale.

pieces.label: Walk Across
pieces.text: (Designer) steps onto the first plank. The bridge dips and sways. (designer.He/She) takes another step, and another, arms out, the ravine yawning below...

pieces.label: Let the Builder Test It
pieces.text: (builder) swings a heavy sack of stones onto the bridge and hauls it across on a rope. Halfway, there's a crack...

pieces.label: Cross on Hands and Knees
pieces.text: Cross on Hands and Knees.

pieces.label: Send the Sack of Stones First
pieces.text: Send the Sack of Stones First.
A plank tips, (designer) cracks (designer.his/her) head on the rope post, and wakes with no name.
All the way across, and then (builder) re-ties eleven knots without a word.
A plank snaps under the sack. "Good design. Bad knots. Let me show you."
It holds. The bridge becomes the young people's favourite place.
The bridge sways alarmingly.
The ravine yawns below.
The young people chant (designer)'s name.

pieces.label: The Coral That Grows Twice
pieces.text: (Diver) is floating above the "twice coral," which grows a second of whatever rests on it, and (diver.his/her) foot is touching it. (diver.He/She) is running out of breath.

pieces.label: Push Off from the Coral
pieces.text: (Diver) plants both feet on the coral and kicks hard for the surface. The pink branches flex, and glow, and something follows (diver.him/her) up through the water...

pieces.label: Swim Up Slowly
pieces.text: (Diver) lifts (diver.his/her) foot away gently and swims up, lungs burning, careful not to brush the coral again. Below, the pink branches stop swaying...

pieces.label: Break Off a Piece
pieces.text: Break Off a Piece.

pieces.label: Call the Divers Down
pieces.text: Call the Divers Down.
{#made:Another head pops up|Two more heads pop up|Three more heads pop up}, all (diver). "Oh no," they say at once.
Someone surfaces with (diver)'s face, who can't swim very well and laughs at the wrong moments.
(Diver) surfaces alone and leaves the twice coral to the stories.
(Diver)'s face itches all night and is new by morning.
The pink branches sway as if breathing.
Two shells where there was one.
A careless diver once woke up with company.

pieces.label: The Garden Raft
pieces.text: A raft of woven reeds drifts into the lagoon with a little garden growing on it, carrying a family who have drifted for a month since their island's shore washed away.

pieces.label: "Stay as Long as You Like."
pieces.text: The family tie their raft to the jetty, and come ashore slowly, as if they've forgotten how solid ground feels. The village crowds round the raft to look at the floating garden...

pieces.label: "Fill Your Gourds and Good Luck."
pieces.text: The family fill their gourds at the stream, and thank (first_to_talk) gravely, and the village gives them some fruit for the journey...

pieces.label: Ask About the Garden
pieces.text: Ask About the Garden.

pieces.label: Fetch the Elders
pieces.text: Fetch the Elders.
The raft garden is planted in the village soil, and the banana is the best on the island. They decide to stay.
A grandparent, a teen who steered and a child in charge of the beans. They decide to stay.
They drift out through the reef with more food than they planned.
The raft tears on the coral. "I suppose that settles it."
Beans and taro and a single banana plant.
A lean-to of leaves.
They come ashore as if they've forgotten how solid ground feels.

pieces.label: The Elder in the Hills
pieces.text: A year ago (elder) moved to a hut in the hills "to listen to the birds." Today (young) finds (elder.him/her) very thin, wrapped in a blanket in the warm sun. "Sit. Listen."

pieces.label: Sit and Listen
pieces.text: (young) sits. For a long time, neither of them says anything. The birds sing. The wind moves in the grass. (Elder)'s hand finds (young)'s...

pieces.label: Run for the Healers
pieces.text: (young) runs all the way down the hill and comes back with two healers and a stretcher. (Elder) rolls (elder.his/her) eyes at the fuss, but lets them carry (elder.him/her) down...

pieces.label: Carry (Him/Her) Down
pieces.text: Carry (elder.Him/Her) Down.

pieces.label: Stay the Night
pieces.text: Stay the Night.
As the sun goes down, (elder) leans against (young)'s shoulder, and is still.
A year of saved words: every trick and shortcut and mistake.
A slow fever breaks in the healers' hut. (Elder) takes a hut nearest the trees.
(Elder) finds (elder.he/she) has missed the noise and the children. "The birds will manage."
"I've talked enough. I want to listen to the birds."
Wrapped in a blanket though it's warm.
The wind moves in the grass.

pieces.label: The Walker in the Fog
pieces.text: In a thick sea fog, (watcher) sees a figure with a greenish lamp walking the beach, like the drowned fisher of the old story: whoever follows the light finds what they've lost, though some never come back.

pieces.label: Follow the Light
pieces.text: (Watcher) walks after the green lamp, along the wet sand, further and further, until the village sounds are gone and there is only the hiss of the waves and the lamp swinging ahead...

pieces.label: Call Out to It
pieces.text: "Who's there?" (watcher) shouts. The lamp stops. Slowly, it turns, and comes back along the beach towards (watcher.him/her), the green light growing...

pieces.label: Go Back for the Fishers
pieces.text: Go Back for the Fishers.

pieces.label: Stand Still Until It Passes
pieces.text: Stand Still Until It Passes.
(Watcher)'s footprints turn straight into the sea, beside a set of very old prints.
The light goes out at (watcher)'s own door, and inside is the bracelet lost a year ago.
The lamp comes close enough to feel the cold. (Watcher) comes home grey at the temples.
It's a young fisher with leaves round the lamp. They walk home laughing too loudly.
People hold each other's shoulders to get from hut to hut.
The hiss of the waves and the lamp swinging ahead.
A greenish light.

pieces.label: The Baby in the Hollow Log
pieces.text: After the great wind, a hollow log washes up with a baby wedged safe inside, wrapped in bark cloth with a gourd of milk, and a broken outrigger lies on the reef.

pieces.label: Take the Baby Home
pieces.text: (Finder) carries the baby home tucked inside (finder.his/her) wrap. By the time (finder.he/she) gets there, half the village is following, asking questions (finder.he/she) can't answer...

pieces.label: Take the Baby to the Healers
pieces.text: The healers check the baby over: well fed, a little cold, perfectly healthy. Then they all look at (finder), who hasn't let go of the baby's foot...

pieces.label: Search the Reef First
pieces.text: Search the Reef First.

pieces.label: Wake (Name2)
pieces.text: Wake (Friend).
Nobody ever comes looking, and the child plays inside the log for years.
The baby grabs (friend)'s nose, and that's the end of the argument.
"The baby seems to have chosen. Look at that grip."
A couple who have hoped for a child take the baby in, and the baby always reaches for (finder)'s finger.
A gourd of milk tied beside the baby.
A broken outrigger on the reef.
The baby is chewing (finder)'s finger.

pieces.label: The Lightning Stone
pieces.text: Caught on the hill by a fast storm beside the black stone that lightning strikes every few years, where touching it means being "struck twice, once on each side," (walker) feels the air buzzing.

pieces.label: Hold Onto the Stone
pieces.text: (Walker) wraps (walker.his/her) arms round the cold black stone and shuts (walker.his/her) eyes. There's a flash so bright (walker.he/she) sees it through (walker.his/her) eyelids, and a crack like the sky breaking...

pieces.label: Run for the Trees
pieces.text: (Walker) runs. Behind (walker.him/her), the lightning hits the stone with a crack that knocks (walker.him/her) flat. (walker.His/Her) shadow, thrown out long by the flash, seems to keep running without (walker.him/her)...

pieces.label: Lie Flat in the Grass
pieces.text: Lie Flat in the Grass.

pieces.label: Shout for Help
pieces.text: Shout for Help.
Someone is on the other side of the stone with (walker)'s face. Struck twice, two of them.
Burns branch across (walker)'s arms like tree roots. The children think the marks are beautiful.
(Walker)'s shadow came loose and kept running, and now it has a face.
(Walker) lies flat counting between flash and thunder. (walker.His/Her) hair stands up for two days.
The sky turns purple overhead.
The air is buzzing.
A crack like the sky breaking.

pieces.label: The Name Day
pieces.text: On name day anyone may stand at the evening fire and ask for a new name. (Namer) has stood up, after a lifetime with a name that never fit.

pieces.label: Let the Village Choose
pieces.text: The fire crackles while the village argues, cheerfully and loudly, about what suits (namer). One of the elders raises a hand for quiet...

pieces.label: Choose for (Himself/Herself)
pieces.text: (Namer) takes a deep breath and says the name (namer.he/she) has been carrying around in (namer.his/her) head for years, out loud, for the first time...

pieces.label: Ask the Children
pieces.text: Ask the Children.

pieces.label: Sit Back Down
pieces.text: Sit Back Down.
"(renamed). My oldest friend's name, always looking up at the sky when there was work to do."
"Why don't we just call (namer.him/her) what we always call (namer.him/her)?"
The village says it back all together, and it sounds right.
A new name, and a face that looks as if a weight has come off it.
The fire crackles while the village argues.
A name carried around in (namer.his/her) head for years.
An elder raises a hand for quiet.

pieces.label: The Hailstones
pieces.text: White stones of ice the size of quail eggs are falling from the sky for the first time anyone can remember, punching through the thatch. The food store roof is tearing, and so is (subject)'s own.

pieces.label: Help with the Food Store
pieces.text: (Subject) runs for the food store with a sleeping mat over (subject.his/her) head, and the ice drums on it like a hundred fists...

pieces.label: Save the Hut
pieces.text: (Subject) dives into (subject.his/her) own hut and starts stuffing (subject.his/her) things under the sleeping shelf, out of the ice and the leaks...

pieces.label: Get the Children Inside
pieces.text: Get the Children Inside.

pieces.label: Hold Mats Over the Store
pieces.text: Hold Mats over the Store.
Every spare mat on the store roof, and by nightfall every hut is dry.
A gust tears the mat away and (subject) falls from the roof. (subject.He/She) keeps the store's count from a seat beside it.
(builder) hands (subject) a bundle of thatch without a word, and they patch until dark.
The store roof gives way and half the baskets fill with icy water.
The ice drums on the mat like a hundred fists.
The children collect the last of the ice in bowls to watch it melt.
Nobody in the village has ever seen it before.

pieces.label: The Pond of Two Moons
pieces.text: Once a year the moon rises in the sky and in the hill pond at once, and two people who look in at that moment "see each other as the moon does." (First) and (second) kneel at the edge as the reflection creeps towards them.

pieces.label: Look
pieces.text: They lean over the water together. The two moons meet. For a moment (first) sees (second)'s face where (first.his/her) own should be, and (second) sees (first)'s...

pieces.label: Close Their Eyes
pieces.text: They squeeze their eyes shut and hold hands and wait, while the cold moonlight crawls over them. (Second) whispers that (friend.he/she) can feel it, like water...

pieces.label: Look One at a Time
pieces.text: Look One at a Time.

pieces.label: Throw a Pebble In
pieces.text: Throw a Pebble In.
Each is looking at (first.himself/herself), and they never get back to their own sides.
For a moment each sees what the other really thinks, and it is kinder than either expected.
Eyes closed made no difference. "That's the last time I listen to you."
Just black water, and next year it's cloudy.
The reflection creeps across the black water.
For a moment they're the same moon.
Cold moonlight like water.

pieces.label: The Grey Morning
pieces.text: (Sleeper) slept in the long grass near the old burial ground, dreamed of quiet people smiling down, and woke with pure white hair. The mark can be given back if the sleeper asks politely, the elders say.

pieces.label: Go Back and Ask
pieces.text: (Sleeper) lies down in the same long grass that night, and before (sleeper.he/she) sleeps, (sleeper.he/she) asks, out loud and politely, for (sleeper.his/her) own hair back...

pieces.label: Keep the Mark
pieces.text: (Sleeper) looks at (sleeper.his/her) white hair in the water bowl for a long time. Then (sleeper.he/she) shrugs. "It's a nice colour," (sleeper.he/she) says...

pieces.label: Ask the Elders to Ask
pieces.text: Ask the Elders to Ask.

pieces.label: Dye It with Berries
pieces.text: Dye It with Berries.
An old woman with a kind face touches (sleeper)'s hair in the dream, and the white and some years are gone.
No dream comes, and (sleeper)'s face settles to match the white hair.
(Sleeper) grows into the white hair, and becomes the one people go to for advice.
The white fades to a single streak, which (sleeper) is quite proud of.
A crowd of quiet people walking past.
The children think (sleeper.he/she) looks like a cloud.
Every strand gone pure white.

pieces.label: The Wet Rocks at the Falls
pieces.text: On the ledge halfway up the falls, with the water high and white after the rains and the rocks slick with spray, (jumper)'s friends in the pool are shouting for (jumper.him/her) to jump.

pieces.label: Jump
pieces.text: (Jumper) takes a run up along the wet ledge and leaps out over the white water. For a moment (jumper.he/she) is flying...

pieces.label: Climb Back Down
pieces.text: (Jumper) shakes (jumper.his/her) head and starts climbing back down the slick rocks, ignoring the jeers. Halfway down, (jumper.his/her) foot slides on the wet stone...

pieces.label: Sit on the Ledge Until the Water Drops
pieces.text: Sit on the Ledge Until the Water Drops.

pieces.label: Wave the Friends Away
pieces.text: Wave the Friends Away.
A rock hidden under the foam. (Jumper) knows everything except (jumper.his/her) own name.
The best jump of the year, and enough for one lifetime.
(Jumper)'s foot slides on the wet stone. The young people carve steps into the rock beside the ledge.
(Jumper)'s leg heals short and stiff, and (jumper.his/her) friends bring the best fruit from the falls.
The water is high and white after the rains.
The rocks are slick with spray.
Every year at least one of them comes home bruised.

pieces.label: The Singing on the Reef
