pieces.text: (Decider) and (builder) light bundles of bitter herbs inside every hut, one by one, and stuff the doorways with wet leaves. Thick yellow smoke comes out of every crack. The village has to sleep on the beach...

pieces.label: Replace the Posts
pieces.text: The whole village goes into the jungle with axes and ropes. They cut new posts of hardwood, the kind termites hate, and drag them back one by one through the mud...

pieces.label: Feed Them to the Chickens
pieces.text: Feed Them to the Chickens.

pieces.label: Ask the Elders
pieces.text: Ask the Elders.
The termites march off, deeply offended, and the builders learn to build better. The huts smell for a year.
The smoke works everywhere but the research hut, where a season of notes goes up.
Three weeks of mud and splinters, and every villager knows how to set a hardwood post.
A hardwood tree falls the wrong way, and (builder) pushes two others clear. The last post has (decider.his/her) name on it.
The chickens eat termites until they can't move, and the posts fall down anyway.
A doorpost crumbles like dry bread.
Long pale rivers of termites.
Thick yellow smoke from every crack.
The village sleeps on the beach.

pieces.label: The Spirit Feast
pieces.text: On the longest night, (watcher) hides behind a rock to see who eats the village's feast for the island spirits, and tall pale lights come walking up out of the flat sea, and one stops to look straight at the rock.

pieces.label: Step Out and Greet Them
pieces.text: (Watcher) stands up, trembling, and says the old greeting. The lights go still. Then the tall one holds out a hand made of something like moonlight on water, and beckons...

pieces.label: Stay Hidden
pieces.text: (Watcher) presses (watcher.himself/herself) flat behind the rock and doesn't breathe. The tall light looks at the rock for a long time. Then it turns back to the feast...

pieces.label: Offer the Stew
pieces.text: Offer the Stew.

pieces.label: Run Home
pieces.text: Run Home.
(Watcher) goes with them. (watcher.His/her) clothes are folded by the clean plates, and footprints go into the sea.
The spirits share the feast, and everything (watcher) eats afterwards tastes of ashes. Baskets of strange fish appear.
(Watcher) falls asleep behind the rock and wakes under a dry seaweed blanket. "Always make extra."
The tall one waits at the water's edge without looking back, and (watcher) gets up and follows.
(Watcher) runs and doesn't stop until (watcher.he/she) is under (watcher.his/her) blanket. The next year, (watcher.his/her) plate is the only one not washed.
The sea goes perfectly flat.
A hand like moonlight on water.
Plates washed clean and stacked at the tideline.
One more place set at the feast every year.

pieces.label: The Grey Clay
pieces.text: Tired of not being listened to, young (young_one) considers sleeping in the healers' grey clay, which (healer) half-joked "draws out the years you've got stored up," (healer) said.

pieces.label: Paint On the Clay
pieces.text: That night (young_one) sneaks into the healers' hut, smears the cold clay all through (young_one.his/her) hair and over (young_one.his/her) cheeks, and lies down to sleep, stiff and itchy and very determined...

pieces.label: Find Another Way
pieces.text: (Young_one) puts the clay back. If they won't listen, (young_one.he/she) will show them. (young_one.He/She) picks the job (young_one.he/she) knows best, and spends the whole next day doing it (young_one.his/her) own way, in plain sight...

pieces.label: Ask (Healer Name) First
pieces.text: Ask (Healer) First.

pieces.label: Shout at the Fire
pieces.text: Shout at the Fire.
(Young_one) wakes with grey hair and soft lines, and the older villagers start listening. "I was JOKING."
Too old: white hair, deep lines, and everyone offering a stick. (Young_one) stops leaping about at the dances.
(Young_one) does it (young_one.his/her) own way in plain sight, and the next day two elders copy (young_one.him/her).
(elder) shows (young_one.him/her) why the old way is the old way, and they start asking (young_one.his/her) opinion anyway.
(Young_one) shouts, and everybody goes very quiet, and then pats (young_one.his/her) arm.
Cold grey clay from the riverbank.
Smiles and pats on the arm.
Stiff and itchy and very determined.
"I was JOKING."

pieces.label: The Two Round Stones
pieces.text: (Hopeful_parent) and (friend) go down to the Twins, two pig-sized round stones in the stream; a couple who carry them to the top of the falls together will have children, "as many as the stones think fair."

pieces.label: Carry the Twins Up
pieces.text: They count to three and lift. The stones are heavy and cold and slippery with moss, and they have to stop every few steps on the climb, panting, their arms shaking, the waterfall roaring beside them...

pieces.label: Leave a Gift Beside Them
pieces.text: They look at the stones, then at the climb, then at each other. (Friend) lays a string of shells on the bank beside the Twins, and (hopeful_parent) adds a flower. They sit on the bank for a while, holding hands, and listening to the falls...

pieces.label: Roll Them Up the Path
pieces.text: Roll Them Up the Path.

pieces.label: Ask the Elders How
pieces.text: Ask the Elders How.
They drop the stones at the top at sunset. By morning the stones are back, and (hopeful_parent) is expecting {#babies:a baby|twins|triplets}.
One stone goes bounding back into the stream. (Hopeful_parent) carries the other alone. "One was fair, given the circumstances."
The gift is gone in the morning, the Twins have moved closer, and (hopeful_parent) is pregnant.
The shells are scattered and the flower floats in the pool. "The Twins like you to work for it."
The stones roll back down twice, nearly taking (friend) with them. They give up for today.
Two stones the size of sleeping pigs.
Slippery with moss and very cold.
The waterfall roars beside them.
"As many as the stones think fair."

pieces.label: The Shadow That Stayed
pieces.text: At midday, (shadowless)'s shadow is lying on the grass a few steps away, on its own, resting, as in a story about a shadow that was worked so hard it decided to live its own life.

pieces.label: Pick Up the Shadow
pieces.text: (Shadowless) walks over to the shadow and stands on its feet, as if to stick it back on. It doesn't stick. It slides out from under (shadowless.him/her), sits up, and looks at (shadowless.him/her)...

pieces.label: Let It Rest
pieces.text: (Shadowless) sits down on the grass beside (shadowless.his/her) shadow and decides to rest too. The two of them sit side by side in the sun, for the first time in (shadowless.his/her) life...

pieces.label: Talk to It
pieces.text: Talk to It.

pieces.label: Stand in the Sun Until It Comes Back
pieces.text: Stand in the Sun Until It Comes Back.
The shadow stands up and fills in from the feet like a pot of water. Another (shadowless), glad to have a face.
The shadow fills in on the outside only, with strong opinions about everything (shadowless) does.
They rest side by side all afternoon, and (shadowless) starts taking a day off every week.
The shadow walks off at sunset and comes back three days later smelling of the sea.
Everyone's shadow is a small puddle under their feet.
The shadow lags behind like a tired child.
It fills in like a pot filling with water.
The shadow smells faintly of the sea.

pieces.label: The Love Charm Mix-Up
pieces.text: (apprentice), the healers' newest apprentice, asks (arguer1) and (arguer2), who have been arguing for a month about fetching water, to wear a charm from an old scroll that "helps you see it from each other's side." There's a smudge on the scroll.

pieces.label: Wear the Charms
pieces.text: They put the little bags round their necks, feeling silly, and go to sleep in their own huts. The herbs smell of mint and burnt hair. In the night, both of them dream of walking down to the stream with a heavy pot...

pieces.label: Settle It the Normal Way
pieces.text: "We'll sort it out ourselves," says (arguer1). (Arguer2) agrees, for once. They sit down by the fire with a pile of shells to make a rota, which immediately starts a new argument about how many shells a day is worth...

pieces.label: Read the Scroll First
pieces.text: Read the Scroll First.

pieces.label: Fetch the Water Together
pieces.text: Fetch the Water Together.
They wake in each other's bodies. They are seeing it from each other's side completely.
Swapped, and each now loves the thing the other loved best. "Almost as if nothing happened. Except everything did."
A rota of shells, made by midnight, and an hour of laughing. They mind the water a lot less.
(apprentice) wears both charms and they argue all night. A headache, a nosebleed, and no more scroll.
They fetch the water together and find they're both too stubborn to put the pot down first.
A smudge on an old bark scroll.
The herbs smell of mint and burnt hair.
"That's what the scroll says. Mostly."
A pile of shells for a rota.

pieces.label: The Memory Moths
pieces.text: On a hot night, a cloud of pale memory moths, which drink small memories the way moths drink nectar, crowd round (one_in_the_cloud)'s head, so thick (one_in_the_cloud.he/she) can feel their wings on (one_in_the_cloud.his/her) eyelids.

pieces.label: Stay Still
pieces.text: (One_in_the_cloud) closes (one_in_the_cloud.his/her) eyes and stands very still. The moths settle on (one_in_the_cloud.his/her) face and hair like a grey veil. (one_in_the_cloud.He/She) feels them drinking, small cold tugs, one after another, and tries to think about something unimportant...

pieces.label: Run to the Sea
pieces.text: (One_in_the_cloud) runs, flapping at the moths, down the path to the beach, and wades in up to (one_in_the_cloud.his/her) chest and ducks under. The moths hover over the water in a grey cloud, waiting...

pieces.label: Think About Something Unimportant
pieces.text: Think About Something Unimportant.

pieces.label: Smoke Them Off
pieces.text: Smoke Them Off.
The moths drink (one_in_the_cloud)'s name out of everyone round the fire. The village calls (one_in_the_cloud.him/her) "?".
One moth leaves a different name behind, like pollen from another flower. Now (one_in_the_cloud.he/she) is (made1).
The moths give up. (One_in_the_cloud) only forgets breakfast, and where the knife is (in the cooking pot).
(One_in_the_cloud) ducks under until dawn and keeps (one_in_the_cloud.his/her) name, and catches a fever.
The smoke drives them off, and everyone round the fire forgets the last hour, including why they lit it.
A dry papery sound like someone turning leaves.
The moths settle like a grey veil.
Small cold tugs, one after another.
Moths drink small memories the way other moths drink nectar.

pieces.label: Grandmother's Comb
pieces.text: (Heir) runs (heir.his/her) late grandmother's turtle-shell comb through (heir.his/her) hair for the first time, and feels it pulling gently, as if it remembers someone else's hair.

pieces.label: Keep Wearing It
pieces.text: (Heir) wears the comb all day. Everyone who passes says it looks lovely. A few of the old people stop and stare, as if seeing someone they used to know...

pieces.label: Put It Back
pieces.text: (Heir) takes the comb out and puts it back in the basket. It feels too much like borrowing something without asking. That night, (heir.he/she) dreams of (heir.his/her) grandmother sitting at the end of the bed, combing her own white hair...

pieces.label: Show It to the Elders
pieces.text: Show It to the Elders.

pieces.label: Give It to a Child
pieces.text: Give It to a Child.
(Heir)'s hair starts falling and curling exactly like (heir.his/her) grandmother's did.
The comb remembers all of her, and (heir)'s hair goes white as sea foam. "She was the beautiful one."
In a dream (heir.his/her) grandmother says, "It's for wearing, silly." (Heir) adds shells and carved fish.
The elders tell the comb's story back, with all the parts the grandmother left out.
The child loses it in a day, and finds it a week later in a hen's nest.
Little carved fish swim along the comb's back.
Hair as white as sea foam.
Old people stop and stare, as if seeing someone they used to know.
"It's for wearing, silly. Not for baskets."

pieces.label: The Old Well
pieces.text: (child)'s goat has fallen through the forgotten cover of the old dry well and is bleating far below, and the walls are loose, slippery old stones.

pieces.label: Climb Down
pieces.text: (Rescuer) ties the rope round a tree, then round (rescuer.his/her) waist, and starts down into the dark, feet against the stones. The goat bleats louder. A stone comes loose under (rescuer.his/her) hand and falls for a long time...

pieces.label: Wait for the Ladder
pieces.text: "Wait," says (rescuer), and holds (child)'s hand while they wait, telling the goat to be brave. (builder) comes running with the long ladder from the store, the one they use for the roofs...

pieces.label: Lower a Basket
pieces.text: Lower a Basket.

pieces.label: Call the Goat Up
pieces.text: Call the Goat Up.
The wall comes down. The goat comes up alive and furious. A fig tree is planted on the filled-in well.
The goat is saved, and a falling stone leaves (rescuer) walking bent, with a stick. (child) brings goat's milk every morning.
The ladder reaches, just, and the goat comes up very indignant. A feast, and the goat eats the flowers.
The ladder is two steps short, and (builder) hangs by one hand to grab the goat by an ear.
The goat bleats, and does not come up, and nobody is surprised.
A stone falls for a long time.
A very indignant goat.
The cover of woven branches, long forgotten.
(child) crying at the edge.

pieces.label: The Brother Who Came Back
pieces.text: Twenty years after (sibling)'s older brother sailed off to see what was over the horizon, a canoe comes in with a grey-haired man with (sibling)'s nose, a tired woman, a teenage boy and a little girl. "I didn't say when."

pieces.label: Hug Him
pieces.text: (Sibling) grabs him and holds on, hard. He smells of salt and strange spices. His wife climbs out of the canoe, smiling uncertainly. The little girl hides behind her mother's legs...

pieces.label: Ask Where He's Been
pieces.text: (Sibling) folds (sibling.his/her) arms. "Twenty years," (sibling.he/she) says. "Twenty years, and not a word." The brother sits down on the sand and starts to tell (sibling.him/her). It takes until dark...

pieces.label: Hit Him
pieces.text: Hit Him.

pieces.label: Fetch the Family
pieces.text: Fetch the Family.
They all stay. The brother takes his spear from the rafters and goes fishing as if he never left.
The brother can't stay anywhere long. His wife and children stay, and (sibling) teaches them everything.
Islands of fire and ice and stone. The researchers write it all down, and he stays with his stories.
Still angry. By morning they're gone, and there's a carved turtle on the doorstep.
He smells of salt and strange spices.
The old fishing spear in the rafters.
The little girl hides behind her mother's legs.
"I said I'd be back. I didn't say when."

pieces.label: The Shrine Basket
pieces.text: At the old shrine on the hill, (finder1) and (finder2) find a basket with two babies in fine cloth nobody here could weave, fresh fruit on the shrine stone and a message in an unknown language scratched in the dirt.

pieces.label: One Each
pieces.text: They carry the babies down the hill, one each, and the babies stop crying halfway down and stare at each other across the gap between their new parents' shoulders...

pieces.label: Take Both to the Healers
pieces.text: They carry the basket down between them, to the healers' hut, where (healer) takes one look and puts the cooking pot on for warm milk...

pieces.label: Wait by the Shrine
pieces.text: Wait by the Shrine.

pieces.label: Ask a Trader to Read the Message
pieces.text: Ask a Trader to Read the Message.
One baby each, in huts across the path. The babies cry if they can't see each other, so the doors stay open.
The babies won't be parted, and (finder2) moves (friend.his/her) mat into (finder1)'s hut. "Just until they're bigger."
(healer) says two more won't make much difference, and says so loudly every night for a year.
The message says, "For the one who finds them first."
Two babies, one at each end of the basket.
Cloth nobody in the village could have woven.
They cry like two halves of one noise.
A message scratched in the dirt.

pieces.label: The Teaching Turtle
pieces.text: A huge old sea turtle with barnacles older than the village has come up the beach, and today it crawls to (sitter)'s feet, lays its head on (sitter.his/her) foot and closes its good eye.

pieces.label: Sit With the Turtle
pieces.text: (Sitter) sits down. The turtle breathes slowly against (sitter.his/her) foot, a long, slow breath every minute or so. The sun goes across the sky. (Sitter) finds (sitter.his/her) own breath slowing down to match...

pieces.label: Get Back to Work
pieces.text: (Sitter) gently slides (sitter.his/her) foot out from under the turtle's head and goes back to work. The turtle opens its eye, and watches (sitter.him/her) go, and sighs...

pieces.label: Scrape Its Barnacles
pieces.text: Scrape Its Barnacles.

pieces.label: Bring It Fish
pieces.text: Bring It Fish.
(Sitter)'s breath slows to the turtle's, and the next day everything at work goes slowly and well.
(Sitter) scrapes the barnacles off while it sleeps, and is never in a hurry again.
The turtle follows (sitter) to work every day for a month. Nobody can rush with a turtle underfoot.
The turtle goes back into the sea and never returns. "They don't ask twice."
Barnacles older than the village.
One good eye, one cloudy.
A long, slow breath every minute or so.
(Sitter) swears it winked.

pieces.label: The Path That Wasn't There
pieces.text: Halfway to the far gardens, (walker1) and (walker2) find a second path that wasn't there yesterday, paved with clean white stones, smelling of unknown flowers, with someone singing an old tune round the bend.

pieces.label: Follow the White Path
pieces.text: They step onto the white stones together. They're warm under their feet, like stones that have been in the sun all day, though the sun has only just come up. The singing gets louder as they walk, and the trees close in overhead...

pieces.label: Keep to the Old Path
pieces.text: "No," says (walker1), firmly, and takes (walker2)'s arm. "Gardens." They walk on, not looking left. The singing follows them for a while, and then, slowly, stops...

pieces.label: Call Out to the Singer
pieces.text: Call Out to the Singer.

pieces.label: Mark the Spot and Fetch the Elders
pieces.text: Mark the Spot and Fetch the Elders.
At the bend, (walker1) stops, and (walker2) walks on smiling, as if called. Then there are only two trees.
They go round the bend together, and only their baskets are found, side by side.
Every plant in the far gardens has flowered in colours nobody has seen. A week later they're beans.
The path is still there on the way home. "Tell them I wasn't scared."
By the time the elders arrive, the trees are the usual distance apart and the mark is gone.
Flat white stones without a single leaf on them.
The stones are warm, as if they've had the sun all day.
Two trees that were not that close together yesterday.
"When the island wants someone, it opens a path."

pieces.label: The Double Fruit
pieces.text: (Finder) finds a ripe, faintly glowing double breadfruit on the path; the elders say a forest spirit has slept in the tree, and whoever eats one "gets a bit doubled."

pieces.label: Eat It
pieces.text: (Finder) breaks it apart at the join. Both halves are sweet and soft and taste faintly of rain. (finder.He/She) eats one half, then, since it seems rude not to, eats the other...

pieces.label: Take It to the Elders
pieces.text: (Finder) carries the fruit very carefully to the elders, holding it out in front of (finder.him/her) like a hot pot. The eldest elder looks at it for a long time, then holds out (finder.his/her) hand...

pieces.label: Share It
pieces.text: Share It.

pieces.label: Tie It Back to the Tree
pieces.text: Tie It Back to the Tree.
(Finder) burps, and there are two of (finder.him/her) on the path, both looking equally guilty.
Each half was doubled too. Three of (finder), all with juice on their chins. "We told you."
(elder) eats it before anyone can stop (finder.him/her). "I've always wanted another pair of hands."
Tied back to the tree, the fruit is gone by morning, and the tree is covered in ordinary fruit.
Split between four friends, it only gives everyone hiccups.
Two fruits joined like a pair of fists.
It tastes faintly of rain.
Still warm from the sun.
"Gets a bit doubled."

pieces.label: The Mirror Shell
pieces.text: A trader paid for a night's food with a polished silver shell that "shows you what you could be," and left at dawn rather quickly; now (looker)'s reflection in it is a little different every time.

pieces.label: Keep Looking
pieces.text: (Looker) sits down on the doorstep and looks into the shell for a long time. The reflection looks back, and tilts its head, and slowly, very slowly, starts to lean forward out of the silver...

pieces.label: Throw It in the Sea
pieces.text: (Looker) walks down to the beach and throws the shell as far as (looker.he/she) can. It skips once on the water, flashing silver, and sinks. Then, a little way out, the water starts to churn...

pieces.label: Bury It
pieces.text: Bury It.

pieces.label: Show It to Everyone
pieces.text: Show It to Everyone.
The reflection climbs out of a hand-sized shell: (looker)'s face and none of (looker)'s habits.
Two climb out, loud and quiet, and the shell cracks as if exhausted.
Someone with (looker)'s face walks up out of the waves. "That was rude."
Nothing comes up. A month later a fisher throws it back without looking.
Everyone who looks sees someone slightly different, and nobody sleeps well that night.
Black sand, and a sea as warm as soup.
The reflection tilts its head.
Someone else trying (looker.his/her) face on.
The shell skips once, flashing silver.

pieces.label: The Dreaming Hammock
pieces.text: (Older), who has aching knees, and young (younger), who knows everything, dare each other to sleep in the dreaming hammock nobody remembers putting up, where sleepers dream of being somebody else.

pieces.label: Both Climb In
pieces.text: The hammock is just big enough for two, if they lie head to foot. It sways. The grass smells of hay and something sweet. Within moments, to their own surprise, they are both asleep...

pieces.label: (Name1) Backs Down
pieces.text: (Older) looks at the hammock, looks at (younger), and laughs. "I'm too old for dares," (older.he/she) says. (Younger) climbs in alone, looking very pleased with (friend.himself/herself), and falls asleep almost at once...

pieces.label: (Name2) Backs Down
pieces.text: (Younger) Backs Down.

pieces.label: Cut It Down
pieces.text: Cut It Down.
They wake in each other's bodies. "Your KNEES. You never said it was this bad."
(Older) wakes with (younger)'s smooth young face. "You can keep the knees."
(Younger) dreams all night of being (older), and at breakfast doesn't say anything clever at all.
The hammock sways, empty, and (younger) laughs from inside a dream, far away.
The knife won't cut the strange grass, and the hammock keeps swaying, very smug.
Woven from grass that doesn't grow on the island.
It smells of hay and something sweet.
It sways, though there is no wind.
Head to foot, just big enough for two.

pieces.label: The Coconut Shy
pieces.text: The overdue coconuts by the cooking fire are as big as a child's head, the wind is getting up, and (climber) is the only one free to climb up and cut them.

pieces.label: Climb Now
pieces.text: (Climber) loops the rope round the trunk and starts to climb, leaning back, walking up the palm the way the old climbers taught (climber.him/her). The higher (climber.he/she) gets, the more the tree sways...

pieces.label: Clear the Area and Wait
pieces.text: (Climber) shoos everyone away from the palms, the cooks complaining loudly, and ropes off the whole cooking area with a vine. Then (climber.he/she) sits down at a safe distance and waits for the wind to drop...

pieces.label: Throw Stones at Them
pieces.text: Throw Stones at Them.

pieces.label: Ask (Builder Name) to Climb
pieces.text: Ask (Builder) to Climb.
The wobbling coconut hits (climber) on the head. "Hello. Who am I?" The village calls (climber.him/her) "?".
The rope slips at the top. (Climber)'s hip heals, but (climber.he/she) never walks without a stick again.
The wind shakes every coconut down into the empty cooking area. "That's one way to harvest."
The only casualty is the big cooking pot, which nobody moved.
Coconuts as heavy as a child's head.
Thud, thud, thud.
Walking up the palm the way the old climbers taught.
The cooks complaining loudly.

pieces.label: The Salve in the Clay Jar
pieces.text: Clearing out the back of the healers' hut, (healer) finds a forty-year-old jar of green salve that the last healer used on the sick "and on (healer.his/her) own face, every night. Never had a wrinkle."

pieces.label: Try It on (Name2)
pieces.text: (Healer) breaks the wax and rubs a little of the salve on (patient)'s rash. (Patient) hisses. It's cold, and then very warm, and then it starts to tingle...

pieces.label: Try It on (Himself/Herself) First
pieces.text: (Healer) dabs a little on the back of (healer.his/her) own hand, just to see. It's cold, then warm, then it tingles all the way up (healer.his/her) arm...

pieces.label: Smell It First
pieces.text: Smell It First.

pieces.label: Bury It
pieces.text: Bury It.
By morning the rash and fever are gone, and there's enough left for three more patients.
The fever goes, and (patient)'s face is as smooth as a child's. The jar goes on the highest shelf.
Safe on (healer)'s hand, and (patient) is cured. The healers go back through all the old jars.
The salve has gone bad, and (healer) spends a week in bed beside (patient), both scratching.
The buried jar is dug up by the pigs, who have very smooth snouts for a month.
A fish scratched on the wax-sealed lid.
Crushed leaves and honey.
Cold, then warm, then tingling.
"Never had a wrinkle."

pieces.label: After the Big Wave
pieces.text: A big wave out of a calm sea has soaked the beach huts, and the chief asks (decider) to decide whether to rebuild them where the families' grandparents built them, or move them up the hill.

pieces.label: Rebuild Where They Were
pieces.text: (Decider) tells the families they can stay. Everyone sets to work shovelling sand out of the huts with coconut shells, pulling seaweed out of the walls and hanging the mats out to dry...

pieces.label: Move Them Up the Hill
pieces.text: (Decider) decides the huts must move. There's a lot of shouting. One grandmother sits down in her doorway and refuses to get up. In the end, the village carries the walls up the hill one by one, with her still sitting in hers...

pieces.label: Build a Sea Wall
pieces.text: Build a Sea Wall.

pieces.label: Let the Families Decide
pieces.text: Let the Families Decide.
A week of shovelling sand with coconut shells, and the huts are as good as new. The chicken stays on the roof.
A second wave three nights later turns a season of research notes into mush.
The huts go up the hill with a grandmother still sitting in her doorway. A view of the whole bay, and a feast.
The huts move, and the families stay angry. The smell of new thatch reminds (decider) of the quarrel.
The sea wall is built in a day, and the huts are dried out behind it.
A very surprised chicken.
Seaweed pulled out of the walls.
Sand shovelled out with coconut shells.
A grandmother sitting in her doorway.

pieces.label: The Elders' Dance
pieces.text: At the full moon festival, the elders ask (leader) to lead the Turning-Back Dance, which, danced right, turns back the years for one night; (elder) remembers most of the steps.

pieces.label: Follow the Steps Exactly
pieces.text: (Leader) leads the elders round the fire, stamping and clapping exactly as (elder) taught (leader.him/her). Stamp, stamp, turn, clap. The elders follow, slow at first, then faster, and the drums speed up to match...

pieces.label: Dance It (His/Her) Own Way
pieces.text: (Leader) starts with the old steps, then lets the drums carry (leader.him/her) somewhere else. The elders follow (leader.him/her), confused at first, then laughing, then dancing like nobody has seen them dance in years...

pieces.label: Let (Elder Name) Lead
pieces.text: Let (Elder) Lead.

pieces.label: Ask the Drummers
pieces.text: Ask the Drummers.
Every elder at the fire has the face they had at twenty-five. Their knees are still old.
The turn should have been left. A heap of elders, and only (elder) at the bottom is a sprightly fifty.
A brand-new dance, and (leader) comes out of it at dawn with a younger face. They call it (leader)'s Dance.
Nothing turns back, but everyone dances till midnight and nobody can walk properly in the morning.
Stamp, stamp, turn, clap.
Clapping in odd places.
(elder) argues with (leader.himself/herself) about the rest of the steps.
"It was LEFT. I see that now."

pieces.label: The Race to the Reef
pieces.text: On a rough day, (challenger), three years in second place, dares (champion), the three-time champion, to race out to the reef and back for the shark-tooth necklace, though (fisher) says they shouldn't.

pieces.label: Race Anyway
pieces.text: They run into the surf together, dive under the first wave and come up swimming, side by side, heads down, arms flashing. The crowd on the beach roars. At the reef, the waves are taller than they look from the shore...

pieces.label: Say No
pieces.text: "Not today," says (champion), loudly, so the whole beach can hear. "(fisher) is right. Next calm day, I'll race you, and I'll beat you." The crowd groans. (Challenger) goes very red...

pieces.label: Race With a Canoe Alongside
pieces.text: Race With a Canoe Alongside.

pieces.label: Let (Name2) Win
pieces.text: Let (Challenger) Win.
A wave throws (challenger) against the coral, and it is too late. Now they race only on calm days, with a canoe.
(Champion) turns back to drag (challenger) clear. The leg is saved, and the necklace given. "You'd have won."
On a flat calm day, (challenger) wins by a hand, and works twice as hard all year.
(Challenger) swims out alone to prove it, and comes back with a dozen cuts.
The canoe hauls both of them out of the surf halfway, and nobody wins.
Waves breaking white across the reef.
Heads down, arms flashing.
A shark-tooth necklace for a year.
"Scared?"

pieces.label: The Chore Spirit
pieces.text: After (scholar) neglects every job to sit with the scrolls in the research hut, a frowning carved chore spirit with a broom appears on (scholar.his/her) doorstep. "They take away what a person loves too much, so the rest gets done."

pieces.label: Keep the Figure
pieces.text: (Scholar) puts it on the shelf in (scholar.his/her) hut, facing the wall. In the night, (scholar.he/she) hears it humming louder, and then a soft sweeping sound, as if someone is tidying the floor...

pieces.label: Take It to the Shrine
pieces.text: (Scholar) carries the figure up the hill to the shrine and sets it down with a flower. "I'll do the other jobs," (scholar.he/she) says. "I promise. You don't need to stay." The humming stops...

pieces.label: Do All the Chores Tonight
pieces.text: Do All the Chores Tonight.

pieces.label: Find Who Asked
pieces.text: Find Who Asked.
The marks on the scrolls are just marks now, and (scholar) goes and does the other jobs. The figure is gone.
The spirit is thorough: no wonder in the scrolls and no morning run. Friends take (scholar.him/her) singing until (scholar.he/she) laughs.
(Scholar) keeps the promise, does the chores first, and comes to the scrolls fresh.
(Elder) asked the spirit, and the spirit decided (elder) needed the lesson. Now (elder) can't sit still.
(Scholar) does every chore by torchlight, and the figure is gone by morning, looking satisfied.
A frowning face and a little broom.
A soft sweeping sound in the night.
The figure is warm, and faintly humming.
Somebody has shouted. Several somebodies.

pieces.label: The Naming Feast
pieces.text: At the once-a-generation Naming Feast, (honoured_one) has earned a new name, for "the business with the pig," and can draw a name from the elders' bowl of shells or stand up and choose (honoured_one.his/her) own.

pieces.label: Pick a Shell
pieces.text: (Honoured_one) closes (honoured_one.his/her) eyes and puts (honoured_one.his/her) hand in the bowl. The shells are cool and clink together. (honoured_one.His/her) fingers close on one that feels warmer than the rest...

pieces.label: Choose (His/Her) Own Name
pieces.text: (Honoured_one) stands up. The drums stop. Everyone stares. "I'd like to choose," (honoured_one.he/she) says, and (honoured_one.his/her) voice only shakes a little. (elder) raises one eyebrow very high, and nods...

pieces.label: Ask About the Pig
pieces.text: Ask About the Pig.

pieces.label: Let the Children Choose
pieces.text: Let the Children Choose.
The shell says (made1). The village shouts it three times and the drums start up.
The shell says "Kayak," the name of the chief's old pig. A name drawn is a name kept.
(Honoured_one) stands up and chooses Ginger, after the ginger root by the stream. "It's allowed. It's just never done."
The elders would have to ask someone who died a hundred years ago, so (honoured_one) keeps (honoured_one.his/her) old name.
A bowl of shells, each with a name scratched on it.
The drums stop, and everyone stares.
One eyebrow goes up very high.
"The business with the pig."

pieces.label: The Lantern Night
pieces.text: On Lantern Night, (hopeful_parent) and (friend)'s coconut-shell lantern, which should drift out through the gap in the reef to bring a baby, has stuck in a tangle of seaweed near the shore.

pieces.label: Wade In and Free It
pieces.text: (Friend) wades in up to (friend.his/her) waist, holding the shell up out of the seaweed, and gives it a little push towards the gap. Everyone on the beach is watching. Some of them are laughing...

pieces.label: Leave It to the Breeze
pieces.text: "It's not meant to be helped," says (hopeful_parent). They sit on the sand holding hands and watch their lantern flicker in the seaweed, while the others drift out one by one...

pieces.label: Light a Second Lantern
pieces.text: Light a Second Lantern.

pieces.label: Blow on It
pieces.text: Blow on It.
The lantern sails out ahead of all the others, and before the year is out (hopeful_parent) is pregnant.
It bumps two others loose and they go out together. (Hopeful_parent) is expecting {#babies:a baby|twins|triplets}.
The breeze turns at midnight and carries it out, the very last one. "Last, but it got there."
It burns out in the seaweed, and turns up on their doorstep in the morning.
A candle of fish oil in a coconut shell.
A hundred lanterns on the black water.
A turtle carved on the side.
The lantern flickers in the seaweed.

pieces.label: The Trader's Baby
pieces.text: A trader, (trader), found a baby a week ago in an empty village where a sickness had passed, and asks (kind_one), who has "kind hands," to give the baby a home that doesn't move.

pieces.label: Take the Baby
pieces.text: (Kind_one) holds out (kind_one.his/her) arms. The trader unties the sling, slowly, and hands the baby over, and then stands with (kind_one.his/her) arms hanging empty, as if (kind_one.he/she) doesn't know what to do with them...

pieces.label: Find Someone Else
pieces.text: (Kind_one) feels the baby's hand in (kind_one.his/her) hair and is very tempted. But (kind_one.he/she) knows someone who has been hoping for a baby for years. "Wait here," (kind_one.he/she) says, and runs...

pieces.label: Ask the Trader to Stay
pieces.text: Ask the Trader to Stay.

pieces.label: Take the Baby to the Chief
pieces.text: Take the Baby to the Chief.
The baby settles at once, and every year the trader's canoe brings a present.
"I'll just make sure (kind_one.he/she) is settled." After a month (trader) sells the canoe.
(Trader), who has wanted a child for years, sits down in the sand with the baby in (friend.his/her) lap.
The baby screams at three good parents and reaches for (kind_one). "I think (kind_one.he/she)'s decided."
Pots for sale, with a baby on the trader's back.
Arms hanging empty.
The baby reaches for (kind_one)'s hair.
A hut full of pots that never sold.

pieces.label: The Hammerhead Shallows
pieces.text: Gathering the best clams on the north shallows, (gatherer) notices that the hammerhead sharks, who come in to rest at midday, are sliding in behind (gatherer.him/her).

pieces.label: Keep Gathering
pieces.text: (Gatherer) moves very slowly, bending (gatherer.his/her) body down into the water, pulling up clams one at a time. The sharks lie still. One of them turns its strange flat head towards (gatherer.him/her)...

pieces.label: Wade Back Now
pieces.text: (Gatherer) turns and wades for the shore, slow and steady, not splashing. The water seems to get deeper with every step. Behind (gatherer.him/her), the grey shapes stir...

pieces.label: Stand Very Still
pieces.text: Stand Very Still.

pieces.label: Throw the Basket
pieces.text: Throw the Basket.
A clam splashes, and the shark moves faster than anything that big should. The leg is saved, not its strength.
The shark looks for a long time, then goes back to sleep. A full basket, and legs that give out on the shore.
(Gatherer) runs, splashing. A shark's tooth on a pole marks the shore after that.
(Gatherer) reaches the sand without a ripple. "They don't bother anyone who doesn't bother them."
The thrown basket draws the sharks off, and (gatherer) gets out with nothing but (gatherer.his/her) skin.
Sharks lying in the warm water like logs.
A strange flat head turning.
Waist-deep water that seems to get deeper.
The voice of people who have been bothered.

pieces.label: The Falling Star
pieces.text: (Finder) finds where last night's falling star came down: a smoking hole in the ferns, and a warm black stone with tiny sparks moving inside it like fish in a pool.

pieces.label: Pick Up the Stone
pieces.text: (Finder) climbs down into the hole and picks up the stone. It's heavy and warm, and the sparks inside rush to where (finder.his/her) fingers are, as if they are curious...

pieces.label: Fetch the Others First
pieces.text: (Finder) runs back to the village and fetches (researcher) and (healer), who argue the whole way there. By the time they get back, the hole has stopped smoking...

pieces.label: Bury It
pieces.text: Bury It.

pieces.label: Watch the Sparks
pieces.text: Watch the Sparks.
(Finder) sees everything the star ever saw, and comes back without (finder.his/her) name.
The sparks swirl into a second (finder), very surprised to have legs.
The researchers watch the sparks go out over a week and learn a great deal.
(researcher) picks it up bare-handed and comes up in a rash of little stars.
Buried, the stone glows through the soil for a month, and the ferns over it grow blue.
A sound like a giant clapping once.
A long white streak across the sky.
Sparks moving like fish in a pool.
The hole stops smoking.

pieces.label: The Feather Cloak
pieces.text: Cleaning the chief's hut, (cleaner) finds the chest left open, and inside is the first chief's red, yellow and black feather cloak, said to make its wearer look wise beyond their years.

pieces.label: Try It On
pieces.text: (Cleaner) lifts the cloak out of the chest. It's lighter than it looks, and it settles round (cleaner.his/her) shoulders with a soft rustle, like birds landing...

pieces.label: Close the Chest
pieces.text: (Cleaner) closes the lid, very gently, and goes back to sweeping. Something rustles inside the chest. Then it rustles again, louder...

pieces.label: Ask the Chief First
pieces.text: Ask the Chief First.

pieces.label: Show It to the Children
pieces.text: Show It to the Children.
(Cleaner)'s hair goes grey and kind lines appear. "Everyone does, eventually." People start asking (cleaner.him/her) for advice.
A line of red and yellow feathers stays on (cleaner)'s shoulders and arms, and won't come off.
The chief is so impressed (cleaner) didn't try it on that (cleaner.he/she) teaches (cleaner) all afternoon.
The rustling is moths, hundreds of them. The cloak is saved, with a small bald patch.
Thousands of feathers, each tied on by hand.
It settles with a rustle like birds landing.
A chest opened only for great occasions.
A small bald patch nobody mentions.

pieces.label: The Sunken Canoe
pieces.text: The fishers have found an old carved canoe on the bottom of the lagoon, with a glinting bundle in oiled cloth inside, and (diver), the best diver, is over the spot with (fisher).

pieces.label: Dive Now
pieces.text: (Diver) takes three long breaths and goes down, kicking hard, into the blue. The light fades. The cold bites. The old canoe comes up out of the dark below (diver.him/her), and the bundle inside it glints...

pieces.label: Mark the Spot
pieces.text: (Diver) ties a float to a long rope and drops a weighted end down to the canoe. "Tomorrow," (diver.he/she) says. "With three divers and a rope each." (fisher) looks relieved...

pieces.label: Dive on a Rope
pieces.text: Dive on a Rope.

pieces.label: Leave It Where It Is
pieces.text: Leave It Where It Is.
The current comes. Bubbles, and then nothing, and the canoe is gone from the bottom too.
Bone needles, a blade sharper than anything the village can make, and a carved fish.
Three divers on ropes bring up the bundle and two paddles carved like the oldest huts.
A storm in the night, and (fisher), out at first light to check the float, is found on the reef.
The old canoe stays on the bottom, and the fish move in.
Patterns nobody in the village uses any more.
The light fades and the cold bites.
Lungs on fire.
A current that comes and goes.

pieces.label: The Shared Gourd
pieces.text: On a dare, (climber1) and (climber2) climb to the Spring of Understanding, where two people who drink from one gourd "understand each other completely," and sometimes come down very strangely.

pieces.label: Share the Gourd
pieces.text: (Climber1) fills the gourd and drinks half, and hands it to (climber2), who drinks the rest. The water tastes of cold stone and nothing else. They look at each other, waiting for something...

pieces.label: Drink From Their Own Hands
pieces.text: "Let's not be silly," says (climber2). They kneel at the spring and drink out of their own cupped hands, side by side, and sit back on their heels...

pieces.label: Pour It Over Each Other
pieces.text: Pour It Over Each Other.

pieces.label: Walk Back Down
pieces.text: Walk Back Down.
They understand each other completely. From the inside. "That's what they meant by strangely."
Swapped, and understanding every ache and habit. "I'm sorry about the knee." "I'm sorry about the stomach."
Nothing happens, and they talk all the way down in the dark, understanding each other fine.
(Climber1) slips, and (climber2) carries (climber1.him/her) down on (friend.his/her) back all night.
They get soaked and laugh, and nothing else happens at all.
Water so clear it seems not to be there.
It tastes of cold stone and nothing else.
It is very quiet at the top.
"That's what they meant by strangely."

pieces.label: The Copycat
pieces.text: For a week someone has copied (copied)'s washing, cooking and singing, and tonight (copied) follows the song to the empty hut at the end of the path and sees someone by the fire in (copied.his/her) spare clothes.

pieces.label: Go In
pieces.text: (Copied) pushes the door open. The figure by the fire turns round. It has (copied)'s face. It smiles, (copied)'s own smile, a little shy...

pieces.label: Call Out from the Doorway
pieces.text: "Who are you?" calls (copied), staying very close to the door. The figure by the fire goes very still. Then, without turning round, it says, in (copied)'s own voice, "I was hoping you'd know..."

pieces.label: Fetch the Neighbours
pieces.text: Fetch the Neighbours.

pieces.label: Leave Food at the Door
pieces.text: Leave Food at the Door.
It has (copied)'s face. "I've been practising. Am I doing it right?" Not quite, but it's very good at washing.
It's better at being (copied) than (copied) is, and the village gives it (copied.his/her) old name.
It's a shipwrecked teen who has been copying the village to learn how to live in it.
The fire goes out as if breathed on. Only the folded clothes and fish bones are left.
Identical washing on the opposite post.
The smell of fish with lime from an empty hut.
(Copied)'s own smile, a little shy.
"I was hoping you'd know."

pieces.label: The Fern That Remembers
pieces.text: (Gatherer) has found a patch of the jungle fern the healers call "too unpredictable": crushed on the face it curls the years back up; burned, its smoke unrolls them.

pieces.label: Rub It On
pieces.text: (Gatherer) crushes a handful of fronds and rubs them over (gatherer.his/her) cheeks and forehead. The juice stings, and smells green and sharp, and (gatherer.his/her) skin starts to feel tight, like it's drawing in...

pieces.label: Take It to the Healers
pieces.text: (Gatherer) carries the bundle home, careful not to crush it, and drops it on the healers' table. While (gatherer.he/she) is explaining, a frond slips off the table and lands in the healers' cooking fire...

pieces.label: Burn a Frond to See
pieces.text: Burn a Frond to See.

pieces.label: Plant It by the Hut
pieces.text: Plant It by the Hut.
(Gatherer)'s face curls back fifteen years. "Unpredictable. But I'll admit it suits you."
The juice burns and blisters. "Unpredictable" was the polite word.
A frond falls in the fire and the sweet grey smoke unrolls fifteen years in a breath. "I did say."
(healer) snatches it from the fire, and the healers test it carefully for a month.
Planted by the hut, it curls up every time anyone walks past, and grows nowhere.
A fern that curls up when it is touched.
The juice smells green and sharp.
A puff of sweet grey smoke.
"Too unpredictable."

pieces.label: The Family in the Storm
pieces.text: On the second night of a storm, (rescuer) finds a shipwrecked family stumbling along the beach: a man with a bleeding head, a girl of twelve, and a woman carrying a baby in a soaked shawl.

pieces.label: Take Them In
pieces.text: (Rescuer) half-carries the woman, and the man carries the girl, and they fall into (rescuer)'s hut together, dripping on everything. (Rescuer) builds the fire up as high as it will go...

pieces.label: Run for the Healers
pieces.text: (Rescuer) wraps (rescuer.his/her) own blanket round the woman and the baby, sits them all down out of the wind behind the canoe shed, and runs for the healers through the storm...

pieces.label: Light a Big Fire on the Beach
pieces.text: Light a Big Fire on the Beach.

pieces.label: Bring Them to the Chief's Hut
pieces.text: Bring Them to the Chief's Hut.
By morning they're warm, and the woman says she can't get in a canoe again. They stay.
The woman dies the next night, and the grieving family asks (rescuer) to keep the baby.
The healers save them all, and (rescuer), who ran without a blanket, is the one coughing.
A cousin's canoe comes for them a week later. "So you can find us," says the girl.
The fire brings the whole village, and the family is carried up the beach in a crowd of blankets.
A guttering torch moving along the beach.
A soaked shawl round the baby.
Shapes bent against the wind.
(Rescuer) builds the fire as high as it will go.

pieces.label: The Hole in the Garden
pieces.text: Overnight a perfectly round hole has opened in the yam garden, deep enough that a stone takes three heartbeats to land, and from down in the dark (rescuer) can hear water running and a missing goat bleating.

pieces.label: Climb Down on a Rope
pieces.text: (Rescuer) ties a rope round (rescuer.his/her) waist, and four farmers take the other end. (rescuer.He/She) goes down over the edge into the cold dark, feet against the crumbling side, a torch in (rescuer.his/her) teeth...

pieces.label: Fence Off the Hole
pieces.text: (Rescuer) sides with (farmer). The farmers cut stakes and build a fence all round the hole, and lower a basket of food down on a rope for the goat, in case...

pieces.label: Lower a Basket
pieces.text: Lower a Basket.

pieces.label: Look for Another Way In
pieces.text: Look for Another Way In.
The edge crumbles and the rope goes slack. The goat comes up alive; (rescuer) comes up wrapped in a mat.
(Rescuer) swings into the rock, reaches the goat, and never lifts (rescuer.his/her) arm above (rescuer.his/her) head again.
The goat walks in from the beach, having found a cave full of sweet water and crunchy mushrooms.
The bleating stops. In a year the hole is full of ferns and nesting birds.
Cold air breathes up, smelling of wet rock.
A dropped stone takes three heartbeats to land.
A torch held in (rescuer.his/her) teeth.
The farmers stand round the edge in a ring.

pieces.label: The Hot Spring in the Rocks
pieces.text: Since the ground shook, a milky-blue hot pool smelling of rotten eggs has appeared in the black rocks above the beach, and (patient) has been sick for a month with aching joints and a cough.

pieces.label: Bring (Name2) to Bathe
pieces.text: (Finder) and (healer) carry (patient) up to the rocks on a mat and lower (finder.him/her) into the milky water, very slowly. (Patient) gasps at the heat, then sighs, a long, long sigh...

pieces.label: Test It First
pieces.text: (Finder) decides to try it first. (finder.He/She) sits on the edge and lowers (finder.his/her) feet in, then (finder.his/her) legs, while (healer) watches with a gourd of cold water ready...

pieces.label: Bring Back a Gourdful
pieces.text: Bring Back a Gourdful.

pieces.label: Ask the Elders
pieces.text: Ask the Elders.
(Patient) walks down the hill without help, smelling powerfully of eggs and grinning.
The pool cures (patient) and leaves (finder.him/her) looking years younger, and works on nobody else's face.
(Finder) tests it and comes out pink and smooth-faced; the next day (patient) is cured.
(Finder)'s feet find a vent. "Some springs are for looking at."
Yellow crystals grow round the edge like frost.
Hot as a bath, milky blue.
A powerful smell of rotten eggs.
Fingers wrinkled from the water.

pieces.label: The Weed Year
pieces.text: A pretty purple-flowered vine has climbed every hut wall and pried apart the posts, and this morning the cooking hut's wall fell in with a soft crunch.

pieces.label: Tear It Out and Rebuild
pieces.text: The whole village spends a day pulling vine off the walls in long, tearing strips. It comes away with whole handfuls of thatch. Then the builders start on the walls...

pieces.label: Dig Up the Roots for Food
pieces.text: (In_charge) sides with (farmer). The farmers dig all round the huts, very carefully, and pull up the roots: long, pale, knobbly things like fat fingers...

pieces.label: Burn It Off
pieces.text: Burn It Off.

pieces.label: Let the Goats at It
pieces.text: Let the Goats at It.
Everyone pulls vine and sets posts, and the whole village is a little better at building.
The vine comes back through the floors until the posts are set on flat stones. The trees go very purple.
The roots taste like a yam crossed with a nut, and the vine withers off the walls. "Waste not."
The sap brings three diggers out in an itching rash. Arms in buckets of seawater for a week.
The wall falls in with a soft crunch.
Roots like fat, pale fingers.
The elders mostly hold the ends of things.
The burning flowers smell surprisingly nice.

pieces.label: The Mask of No Face
pieces.text: (Debtor) owes (fisher) a canoe-load of fish from a lost bet, and is alone in the elders' hut with the Mask of No Face, whose wearer is forgotten by the sea, and by everyone else too, a little.

pieces.label: Put On the Mask
pieces.text: (Debtor) lifts the mask down and ties it on. The wood is cool and smells of old smoke. Through the eye holes, the hut looks very slightly grey, as if everything has faded a little...

pieces.label: Pay the Debt
pieces.text: (Debtor) leaves the mask where it is. A debt is a debt. (debtor.He/She) takes (debtor.his/her) spear and nets and goes down to the water at dawn, to fill a canoe with fish...

pieces.label: Ask (Fisher Name) to Forgive It
pieces.text: Ask (Fisher) to Forgive It.

pieces.label: Hide in the Jungle
pieces.text: Hide in the Jungle.
(fisher) walks straight past. When the mask comes off, nobody can remember (debtor)'s name.
The village welcomes (debtor) as a newcomer and names (debtor.him/her) (made1). The debt is gone.
Four days of fishing, a full canoe, and half the fish given back.
(Debtor) bets the second half and loses. Now it's two canoe-loads.
(fisher) laughs and forgives it, then tells everyone about it for a year.
Smooth, pale wood with two eye holes.
Everything looks faded through the mask.
Reminders, loudly, for a week.
"A debt is a debt."

pieces.label: The Clay Figures
pieces.text: Making clay figures by the river for the children, (maker) makes one of (maker.himself/herself) from the red clay that "remembers being alive," and at sunset the little clay (maker) seems to turn its head.

pieces.label: Leave It to Dry
pieces.text: (Maker) tells (maker.himself/herself) not to be silly, and goes home. In the night, (maker.he/she) dreams of being small and hard and warm, lying in the sun by the river...

pieces.label: Break It Up
pieces.text: (Maker) picks up the clay (maker), which is still damp, and squashes it back into a ball. It is warm, warmer than the sun should have made it. (Maker) feels a sharp pang, as if (maker.he/she) has stubbed a toe somewhere inside (maker.himself/herself)...

pieces.label: Take It Home
pieces.text: Take It Home.

pieces.label: Make the Chief Instead
pieces.text: Make the Chief Instead.
Someone by the river rubs red clay out of (maker.his/her) hair: a perfect (maker). The children want a dragon.
A rough copy with (maker)'s face and a fondness for pigs. "You made me in a hurry."
(Maker) squashes it and throws it in the river, and the clay chief goes missing. The chief's nose itches.
Bruises come up on (maker)'s arms exactly where (maker.his/her) fingers squeezed the clay.
The chief with a very big nose.
Red river clay that remembers being alive.
Warmer than the sun should have made it.
Small and hard and warm, lying by the river.

pieces.label: The Dolphin Who Waits
pieces.text: For a week a dolphin has come into the bay each morning, only for (chosen), circling (chosen.him/her), then swimming out towards the open sea and waiting, and looking back.

pieces.label: Swim After It
pieces.text: (Chosen) dives in and swims after the dolphin, out past the shallows, out past the reef, into the deep blue water where the waves are long and slow. The dolphin swims just ahead, always just ahead...

pieces.label: Follow in a Canoe
pieces.text: (Chosen) and (fisher) take a canoe out after the dolphin, paddling hard to keep up. It leads them past the reef, past the point, round the far side of the island where nobody fishes...

pieces.label: Feed It a Fish
pieces.text: Feed It a Fish.

pieces.label: Ignore It
pieces.text: Ignore It.
(Chosen) swims out until (chosen.he/she) is a speck. Far away, a stranger walks out of the sea, tired and happy, and stays.
The dolphin herds a whole shoal into the bay with (chosen) swimming beside it.
A stranded baby dolphin in a rock pool, carried back to the sea between them.
The current tips the canoe at the far point. The dolphin pushes (chosen) to the rocks. Not (fisher).
After three days of being ignored, the dolphin squirts water at (chosen) and leaves, offended.
It rolls on its side and looks.
Long, slow waves in the deep blue water.
Always just ahead.
"My grandmother said a lot of things."

pieces.label: The Elder's Hat
pieces.text: Retiring from the council, (elder) gives (chosen.his/her) shell-brimmed hat to (chosen), though everyone who wears one long enough ends up looking like an elder: "the weight of the wisdom."

pieces.label: Accept the Hat
pieces.text: (elder) lifts the hat off (chosen.his/her) own head and settles it on (chosen)'s. It is heavier than it looks, and warm, and fits as if it was made for (chosen.him/her)...

pieces.label: Ask for Something Else
pieces.text: (Chosen) thanks (elder), very politely, and says (chosen.he/she) isn't ready for a hat. "Could you teach me something instead?" (elder) looks at (chosen.him/her) for a long moment, and laughs...

pieces.label: Wear It Only on Festival Days
pieces.text: Wear It Only on Festival Days.

pieces.label: Give It to a Friend
pieces.text: Give It to a Friend.
(Chosen)'s hair goes grey under the brim, and people ask (chosen.him/her) to settle arguments. "It knows its own."
(Chosen) adds a cloak and shells to match and looks every inch a councillor, without a grey hair.
A month of morning lessons, and the hat kept in a basket until (chosen) is ready.
(Retiring_elder) takes the hat, ages fifteen years in a season, and tells (chosen) what the council thinks.
A tall woven hat with shells round the brim.
It smells strongly of (elder).
Heavier than it looks, and warm.
"The weight of the wisdom."

pieces.label: The Thatcher's Ladder
pieces.text: The rains are a week away, half the roofs still have holes, and the only ladder left for (thatcher) is the old one, "fine, mostly, if you don't lean," for the highest roof in the village.

pieces.label: Use the Old Ladder
pieces.text: (Thatcher) props the old ladder against the chief's roof and climbs, very carefully, not leaning. At the top, the whole thing gives a long, low creak, like an old man getting out of bed...

pieces.label: Make a New One First
pieces.text: (Thatcher) goes into the forest and cuts three straight new poles, and spends the afternoon lashing rungs to them while the other builders shout at (thatcher.him/her) to hurry up...

pieces.label: Climb Up the Wall
pieces.text: Climb Up the Wall.

pieces.label: Borrow (Builder Name)'s Ladder
pieces.text: Borrow (Builder)'s Ladder.
A rung snaps. (Thatcher) walks with a stick after that, and every roof is finished by the others.
The ladder creaks like an old man getting out of bed, and holds, and every roof is tight.
The best ladder the village has ever had, and everyone learns (thatcher)'s lashing knot.
The rains come early and leak all over the chief. "At least it's a very good ladder."
Rungs mended so many times nobody knows which are original.
A long, low creak like an old man getting out of bed.
"Fine, mostly, if you don't lean."
Water dripping off (builder)'s nose.

pieces.label: The Coughing Season
pieces.text: A dry, barking cough has half the village, including (healer), the head healer, and (healer) must choose between (healer.his/her) mother's eucalyptus steam and a trader's honey and ginger.

pieces.label: The Old Steam Cure
pieces.text: (Healer) sets every pot in the village boiling with eucalyptus leaves. The sick sit in rows with blankets over their heads, breathing in the sharp green steam, coughing and spluttering...

pieces.label: The Trader's Honey and Ginger
pieces.text: (Healer) mixes honey with crushed ginger and hands out spoonfuls to everyone who's coughing. It's sweet and hot and makes people's eyes water. The children ask for seconds...

pieces.label: Both at Once
pieces.text: Both at Once.

pieces.label: Rest and Water
pieces.text: Rest and Water.
The steam does what the brew couldn't, and the healers add (healer)'s mother's cure to their songs.
The sickest is cured, but a spark catches a blanket and three people get scorched.
Sweet and hot, and the cough is gone in a week. The bees are less pleased.
The honey runs out, two get better, and the tired healers mix up their own brews.
Rows of the sick with blankets over their heads.
Sharp green eucalyptus steam.
Orders given between coughs.
The children ask for seconds.

pieces.label: The Crab Moon
pieces.text: (Walker1) and (walker2) are caught on the path in the middle of the yearly land-crab march, when the crabs "carry people's spirits back and forth in their claws, and don't always put them back where they found them."

pieces.label: Stand Still
pieces.text: They stand back to back in the moonlight, not moving, while the crabs flow round their ankles like water. Clicking. Scraping. Hundreds of little eyes on stalks, all turned towards them...

pieces.label: Run for It
pieces.text: "Run!" shouts (walker2), and they run, hopping and leaping, trying to land in the gaps. Crabs crunch under their feet. Both of them wince at every one...

pieces.label: Climb a Tree
pieces.text: Climb a Tree.

pieces.label: Step Very Carefully
pieces.text: Step Very Carefully.
A gentle pinch at the back of the neck, and the crabs put them back in the wrong places.
One crab pinches (walker2)'s toe on its way past, which is extremely rude. That's all.
The crabs take it personally, swarm them, and put each of them back in the other's body.
Home, breathless and laughing, watching the red tide go past. Small grumbles stop mattering.
Clicking and scraping across the village in a red tide.
Hundreds of little eyes on stalks.
Crabs flow round their ankles like water.
"Never be in the middle."

pieces.label: The Big Canoe
pieces.text: At the launch of the biggest canoe the village has ever built, (paddler), one of twenty paddlers, notices the mast leaning and a lashing fraying, while (builder) shouts with joy and hears nothing.

pieces.label: Stop the Launch
pieces.text: (Paddler) shouts and waves until the paddlers stop pushing and the drummers stop drumming and the whole beach goes quiet and stares at (paddler.him/her). (builder) comes stomping down the side of the canoe, red in the face...

pieces.label: Keep Pushing
pieces.text: (Paddler) decides it's probably fine. They push the canoe down into the surf, all twenty of them shouting, and leap in and start paddling. Out past the reef, the mast starts to sway...

pieces.label: Fix It Quietly
pieces.text: Fix It Quietly.

pieces.label: Tell the Chief
pieces.text: Tell the Chief.
(builder) goes pale, says thank you, and teaches (paddler) a knot that will never fray.
While everyone argues, a wave swings the canoe and catches (paddler) against a roller.
Past the reef the mast comes down. The canoe is named after (paddler).
(Paddler) climbs the swaying mast and re-ties it with (paddler.his/her) teeth. They fish further out than ever.
Carved from a single great tree.
Long enough for twenty paddlers.
The drummers stop drumming.
Nineteen people yelling advice.

pieces.label: The Burning Fever
pieces.text: (Sick_one) has the worst fever in years, and (healer) has one cure left: the old way, dipping the sick person three times in the cold sea at midnight. Once it worked. Once it didn't.

pieces.label: Take (Him/Her) to the Sea
pieces.text: Four healers carry (sick_one) down the beach on a mat by torchlight. The sea is black and cold. They wade in up to their waists and dip (sick_one.him/her) under, once, twice, three times...

pieces.label: Wait It Out
pieces.text: (healer) decides against the sea. They wrap (sick_one) in wet banana leaves and sit with (sick_one.him/her) all night, changing the leaves every hour, singing the old healing songs...

pieces.label: Cool (Him/Her) in the Stream
pieces.text: Cool (sick_one.Him/Her) in the Stream.

pieces.label: Sing All Night
pieces.text: Sing All Night.
On the third dip (sick_one) comes up shouting at them to stop, in (sick_one.his/her) own voice. Two out of three.
The fever breaks, and burns away one word on its way out: (sick_one)'s own name.
Wet banana leaves all night, and the fever breaks before dawn. The healers write it all down.
Near dawn (sick_one) goes quiet, and then still. (healer) stands in the cold sea alone the next midnight.
Talking to people who aren't there.
The sea black and cold under the torches.
Wet banana leaves, changed every hour.
A mark on the post by the door.

pieces.label: The Night-Blooming Flower
pieces.text: (Hopeful_parent) and (friend) climb the hill to sit all night under the vine whose white flowers bloom one night a year; a couple who stay awake under it will have a baby, "or more, if the flowers like them."

pieces.label: Tell Stories All Night
pieces.text: They lie on the blanket under the white flowers and tell each other every story they know: their grandparents' stories, the funny ones, the frightening ones, and some they make up as they go along...

pieces.label: Take Turns Sleeping
pieces.text: "You sleep first," says (hopeful_parent). "I'll wake you at the half-moon." (Friend) is asleep in moments. (Hopeful_parent) sits up alone among the white flowers, watching the stars wheel round...

pieces.label: Sing to the Flowers
pieces.text: Sing to the Flowers.

pieces.label: Bring the Whole Family
pieces.text: Bring the Whole Family.
Every flower drops one petal at dawn, and (hopeful_parent) is expecting {#babies:a baby|twins|triplets}.
They make it to dawn, just, and argue for years about the end of the last story.
Both asleep by the half-moon, with petals in their hair. No baby, and the nicest night's sleep ever.
Taking turns, watching each other sleep. The flowers don't mind.
Big white flowers opening with a sound like a sigh.
The air so sweet it makes them dizzy.
A gourd of coconut milk.
Petals in their hair at dawn.

pieces.label: The Canoe Shed Baby
pieces.text: In the canoe shed, (finder) finds a sleeping baby left by a passing fishing family, with a gourd of milk, red beads round its ankle and a bark message: "Too many mouths. Please."

pieces.label: Take the Baby Home
pieces.text: (Finder) picks up the basket, bark message and all. The baby wakes, looks up at (finder.him/her) with a frown, and starts to suck its fist thoughtfully...

pieces.label: Take It to the Chief
pieces.text: (Finder) carries the basket to the chief's hut. The chief reads the message, sighs, and calls the whole village together at the cooking fire...

pieces.label: Paddle After the Family
pieces.text: Paddle After the Family.

pieces.label: Ask the Healers
pieces.text: Ask the Healers.
(Finder) keeps the bark message to show the child one day: (finder.his/her) family found (finder.him/her) a home where there was food.
(Friend) reads it twice and holds out (friend.his/her) arms. "That's that decided."
(healer), with milk enough for two, stands up first. "Give (finder.him/her) here."
(Finder) is on (finder.his/her) feet before (finder.he/she) knows it, and every family brings something that night.
A string of red beads round the baby's ankle.
The bay empty to the horizon.
The baby sucks its fist thoughtfully.
"Too many mouths. Please."

pieces.label: The Bitter Honey
pieces.text: (Honey_lover), who loves honey more than anyone, finds a hive of dark, almost black swamp honey, and (gatherer) warns that it "takes the sweetness out of things. Not just your mouth."

pieces.label: Taste It
pieces.text: (Honey_lover) dips one finger into the comb and licks it. It's sweet. Then it's bitter. Then it's nothing at all, as if (honey_lover.his/her) tongue has gone to sleep...

pieces.label: Leave It
pieces.text: (Honey_lover) looks at the dark honey for a very long time. Then (honey_lover.he/she) sighs, and turns away, and walks home without even a taste. It's the hardest thing (honey_lover.he/she) has done all year...

pieces.label: Feed It to a Pig
pieces.text: Feed It to a Pig.

pieces.label: Smoke Out the Hive
pieces.text: Smoke Out the Hive.
(Honey_lover)'s taste comes back, but the joy doesn't. Food is just food now.
It takes the sweetness out of more than food: (honey_lover) stops running after the bees.
Sulking home, (honey_lover) finds an ordinary golden hive and gets stung four times. "That's honey."
(Gatherer) hears only "honey," eats a handful, and stops caring about food. The cooks are offended.
The hive is smoked out and burned, and the swamp smells of bitter caramel for a week.
Dark, almost black honey dripping from a hollow tree.
Sweet, then bitter, then nothing.
Swamp bees that feed on the grey flowers.
A week's fish for one small pot.

pieces.label: The Second Tide
pieces.text: On the Second Tide, when the lagoon empties to wet sand, (walker) finds someone with (walker.his/her) own face asleep in a still hollow of water, and the old fishers say what the sea gives back then should be left where it lies.

pieces.label: Wake the Sleeper
pieces.text: (Walker) kneels and touches the sleeper's shoulder. It's cold and wet, like a stone from the sea. Its eyes open, (walker)'s own eyes, and look up at (walker.him/her) without surprise...

pieces.label: Leave It Where It Lies
pieces.text: (Walker) backs away, slowly, and walks on across the lagoon, not looking back. Behind (walker.him/her), the water starts to come back in over the sand, very fast...

pieces.label: Run for the Fishers
pieces.text: Run for the Fishers.

pieces.label: Cover It With Seaweed
pieces.text: Cover It With Seaweed.
"Thank you," says the sleeper, and walks home beside (walker), the same in every way.
It has (walker)'s face, hates the sun and doesn't like fish. "The sea gives back what it wants."
The tide comes in over it, and (walker) dreams of sleeping peacefully at the bottom of the lagoon.
That evening it knocks, dripping. "You left me."
The reef stands up out of the water.
A field of wet sand and puddles.
Cold and wet, like a stone from the sea.
The water comes back very fast.

pieces.label: The Moth of Many Summers
pieces.text: A big moth with wings the colour of a summer sunset lands on (tired_one)'s hand by the fire and stays; the elders say these moths carry "the summers people have used up," and offer some back.

pieces.label: Let It Stay
pieces.text: (Tired_one) holds (tired_one.his/her) hand very still. The moth walks up (tired_one.his/her) wrist, and (tired_one.his/her) arm, and settles on (tired_one.his/her) shoulder, close to (tired_one.his/her) ear, and the soft wings brush (tired_one.his/her) cheek, warm as sunshine...

pieces.label: Shake It Off Gently
pieces.text: (Tired_one) doesn't want anyone's used-up summers. (tired_one.He/She) gives (tired_one.his/her) hand a little shake. The moth lifts off and flutters round (tired_one.his/her) head once, then flies away towards the children playing by the fire...

pieces.label: Offer It to a Friend
pieces.text: Offer It to a Friend.

pieces.label: Ask the Moth for Just One Summer
pieces.text: Ask the Moth for Just One Summer.
(Tired_one)'s knees stop aching, and (tired_one.his/her) face looks fifteen summers younger. "That was a generous moth."
The moth gives what it can: just the face, bright and smooth. The knees still ache.
The children chase it round the fire, and (tired_one) laughs harder than all year.
The moth comes back as if to say "really?", and (tired_one) lets it sit.
Wings the colour of a summer sunset.
Opening and closing its wings as if breathing.
Warm as sunshine on the cheek.
"Summers are hard to come by."

pieces.label: The Jumping Rock
pieces.text: (Jumper)'s friends have found a ledge above the river pool higher than anyone has ever jumped from, so high the pool looks like a coin, and they're all looking at (jumper) to go first.

pieces.label: Jump
pieces.text: (Jumper) takes three steps back, runs, and leaps off the ledge into the air. For a long moment (jumper.he/she) is flying, the wind screaming past (jumper.his/her) ears, the pool getting bigger and bigger...

pieces.label: Climb Back Down
pieces.text: (Jumper) looks down at the pool, and the rocks, and then at (jumper.his/her) friends. "No," (jumper.he/she) says. "That's too high." (jumper.He/She) starts to climb down. Behind (jumper.him/her), the others go quiet...

pieces.label: Throw a Rock First
pieces.text: Throw a Rock First.

pieces.label: Dare Someone Else
pieces.text: Dare Someone Else.
(Jumper) doesn't jump far enough out. A cairn of stones marks the ledge, and nobody jumps from it again.
(Jumper) bangs (jumper.his/her) head on the bottom and comes up without (jumper.his/her) name.
One by one the others climb down too, relieved, and jump from the old ledge all afternoon.
(Friend) laughs and jumps, lands in the shallows, and walks bent and slow from then on.
The pool looks like a coin.
The wind screaming past (jumper.his/her) ears.
Rocks at the edges.
Nobody wants to go first.

pieces.label: The Chief's Bad Day
pieces.text: On a bad day, the chief says (soup_carrier.he/she) would give anything to be (soup_carrier), and (soup_carrier) says (soup_carrier.he/she) would give anything to be chief, the exact words from (elder)'s full-moon story, and it is a full moon tonight.

pieces.label: Laugh It Off
pieces.text: "It's only a saying," says (soup_carrier), and the chief laughs too, tiredly. (elder) shakes (soup_carrier.his/her) head and goes back to the fire, muttering. That night the full moon comes up huge and white over the sea...

pieces.label: Take It Back
pieces.text: "I didn't mean it!" says (soup_carrier), loudly, to the sky. The chief looks at (soup_carrier.him/her) oddly. (elder) nods, satisfied. Then the chief says, very quietly, "I did, though..."

pieces.label: Ask (Elder Name) for the Story
pieces.text: Ask (Elder) for the Story.

pieces.label: Stay Indoors Until Dawn
pieces.text: Stay Indoors Until Dawn.
They wake in each other's bodies. "Be careful what you say under a full moon."
(Soup_carrier) wakes in a perfect copy of the chief's clothes. The moon has a sense of humour.
(Soup_carrier) took it back; the chief didn't. "One day. Just one day." It is longer than one day.
Nothing happens, and (soup_carrier) takes the pigs and the roof off the chief's hands.
Three arguments before breakfast.
The pigs in the garden.
The full moon huge and white over the sea.
"Just carry soup about. No decisions."

pieces.label: The Spirit of Old Age
pieces.text: Walking home late, (another_villager) meets an old woman with a stick and a basket of grey feathers on the path: the Spirit of Old Age, who gives those who carry her basket some of her years, "the good ones, and the others."

pieces.label: Carry the Basket
pieces.text: (Another_villager) picks up the basket. It's light, it's only feathers, but with every step it gets heavier, and the old woman walks beside (another_villager.him/her), chatting about the weather, the price of fish, the old days...

pieces.label: Walk On By
pieces.text: (Another_villager) knows the story. (another_villager.He/She) says "Sorry, I'm in a hurry," and walks past, very fast, not looking back. Behind (another_villager.him/her), the old woman laughs, a dry laugh like leaves...

pieces.label: Offer Her Food Instead
pieces.text: Offer Her Food Instead.

pieces.label: Ask Her Name
pieces.text: Ask Her Name.
(Another_villager) comes home silver-haired, knowing things about (another_villager.his/her) work that take a lifetime to learn.
The basket gets so heavy (another_villager)'s back stays bent. "The others," say the elders, gently.
(Name2) comes home grey and stooped. "There was an old woman, with a basket."
The tap of a stick follows (another_villager) home, and a grey feather lies on the step.
A basket of grey feathers.
A smile with no teeth at all.
A dry laugh like leaves.
"The good ones, and the others."

pieces.label: The Rain Drinker
pieces.text: (Rain_drinker), who drops everything to drink the rain because it "tastes of the sky," is caught in a downpour carrying the research hut's newest scrolls, with (researcher) running after (rain_drinker.him/her).

pieces.label: Get the Scrolls Indoors
pieces.text: With enormous effort, (rain_drinker) keeps (rain_drinker.his/her) chin down and runs for the research hut, hugging the scrolls to (rain_drinker.his/her) chest. The rain drums on (rain_drinker.his/her) back. It has never smelled so good...

pieces.label: Drink the Rain
pieces.text: (Rain_drinker) can't help it. (rain_drinker.He/She) stops in the middle of the path, tips (rain_drinker.his/her) head back, opens (rain_drinker.his/her) mouth, and drinks. The scrolls go limp in (rain_drinker.his/her) arms. (researcher) arrives, out of breath...

pieces.label: Hand the Scrolls Over
pieces.text: Hand the Scrolls Over.

pieces.label: Shelter Under a Roof
pieces.text: Shelter Under a Roof.
The scrolls get in dry, and for the first time the rain is just water falling.
Two steps from the door, the scrolls go into the biggest puddle in the village.
Soaked scrolls, and (researcher) walks away slowly in the rain without shouting.
The scrolls are in waxed leaves. "I know you," says (researcher), and drinks a little rain too.
Warm, fat drops of rain.
Rainwater tastes of the sky.
Ink running out in blue streams.
A cover of waxed leaves.

pieces.label: The Tag Champion
pieces.text: (Champion), the village's unbeatable tag champion, is running straight at a humming spirit-stone that, says (child), will catch "it" forever.

pieces.label: Dodge Past
pieces.text: (Champion) swerves at the last moment, quick as a lizard, and goes flying past the stone with (child) grabbing at empty air. Then (champion.his/her) foot catches on a root...

pieces.label: Touch the Stone
pieces.text: (Champion) runs straight at the stone and slaps it with both hands. "Only a story!" (champion.he/she) shouts. The humming stops, all at once. The jungle goes very quiet...

pieces.label: Stop Playing
pieces.text: Stop Playing.

pieces.label: Let (Child Name) Catch (Him/Her)
pieces.text: Let (Child) Catch (champion.Him/Her).
A root, a fall, and (champion) is caught for the first time ever, and doesn't want to play any more.
(Champion) rolls and keeps running. The stone stops humming. Only a story.
The stone takes away childhood, a little: (champion) is fifteen and long-legged.
Nothing happens, but (champion) scared (champion.himself/herself), and the others finally win.
Quick as a lizard.
A spirit-stone, smooth and warm and humming.
The jungle goes very quiet.
"Only a story!"

pieces.label: The Sleepy Spell
pieces.text: (Hard_worker) works harder than anyone and never stops, and (hard_worker)'s family have hidden (apprentice)'s untested sleeping-flower cake in (hard_worker.his/her) supper to "slow (hard_worker.him/her) down a bit."

pieces.label: Eat It Anyway
pieces.text: (Hard_worker) eats every bite, too tired to argue. Then (hard_worker.he/she) sits back, and the fire seems very warm, and the voices round it very kind, and (hard_worker.his/her) eyelids very heavy...

pieces.label: Push It Away
pieces.text: "Someone's put something in this," says (hard_worker), and pushes the bowl across the mat. Everyone round the fire looks innocent. (apprentice) looks so innocent (hard_worker.he/she) goes red...

pieces.label: Ask What's In It
pieces.text: Ask What's In It.

pieces.label: Give It to the Dog
pieces.text: Give It to the Dog.
A day and a half of sleep, and (hard_worker) stops when (hard_worker.he/she) is tired now, and comes to the fire.
Three days of sleep, and (hard_worker) is very, very calm about everything. "Half the honey."
The family tell (hard_worker) the truth, and (hard_worker.he/she) stays at the fire till the end.
(apprentice) eats it to prove it's safe and falls into the woodpile.
Crushed sleeping-flowers and honey.
First up, last to bed.
Hands that shake at supper.
(apprentice) looks so innocent (hard_worker.he/she) goes red.

pieces.label: The Scroll That Bit
pieces.text: (Scholar), who loves learning, finds a warm, unopened scroll tied with red cord and labelled "Cures. Do not read for fun," while (patient) lies ill and the healers are out of ideas.

pieces.label: Read It for a Cure
pieces.text: (Scholar) reads. The writing crawls across the bark into (scholar.his/her) eyes and into (scholar.his/her) head, cure after cure, more than (scholar.he/she) can hold, and the hut goes dark round the edges...

pieces.label: Tie It Back Up
