pieces.text: (Scholar) ties the red cord very tightly round the scroll, puts it back in its box and puts the box back at the very back of the hut. Then (scholar.he/she) goes to (patient)'s hut, and sits down, and thinks...

pieces.label: Read Only the First Line
pieces.text: Read Only the First Line.

pieces.label: Give It to the Healers
pieces.text: Give It to the Healers.
(Scholar) cures (patient), but the scroll took the fun out of learning.
The cures settle tidily in (scholar)'s head, every sick villager is well, and the scroll is blank.
An old healer's ordinary notes hold a forgotten brew that works.
The box is empty in the morning, and nobody admits anything.
"Cures. Do not read for fun."
The writing moves as if breathing.
A red cord, tied very tightly.
Elders who hide when they see (scholar.him/her) coming.

pieces.label: The Fastest Feet
pieces.text: (Runner), who has never walked anywhere if (runner.he/she) could run, is the village's choice for a race round the whole island against the next village's fastest runner, though (healer) says (runner.his/her) knee has been clicking all season.

pieces.label: Run the Race
pieces.text: The two runners set off from the beach at dawn, side by side, with both villages cheering. By noon they are halfway round, and (runner)'s knee is clicking with every step...

pieces.label: Let Someone Else Run
pieces.text: (Runner) looks at (runner.his/her) knee, and at (healer)'s face, and says (runner.he/she) will sit this one out. The whole village groans. (Second_fastest), the second fastest, steps forward, looking terrified...

pieces.label: Run It Slowly
pieces.text: Run It Slowly.

pieces.label: Bind the Knee and Run
pieces.text: Bind the Knee and Run.
The knee gives at the far point, and (runner) finishes hopping on a stick, after sunset. (Runner) never runs again.
(Runner) wins by a hand, and the next morning walks everywhere. "I think I ran it all out."
(Second_fastest) wins by the length of a canoe, and (runner) lifts (second_fastest) onto (runner.his/her) shoulders.
(Second_fastest) loses, the knee heals, and next year (runner) wins.
A carved paddle with a whale on it.
A knee clicking with every step.
Both villages waiting in silence.
The sun touches the sea.

pieces.label: The Washing Stones
pieces.text: (Washer), who loves washing everyone's clothes, finds a bundle of strange, beautifully woven, muddy clothes at the washing stones, and (gatherer) warns that the water spirits "don't like their laundry touched."

pieces.label: Wash Them
pieces.text: (Washer) can't resist. (washer.He/She) scrubs the mud out of the strange clothes on the flat stones, and the colours come up bright as parrot feathers, brighter than anything (washer.he/she) has ever washed...

pieces.label: Leave Them
pieces.text: (Washer) sits on (washer.his/her) hands on the bank and watches the strange clothes soaking in the stream. It is the hardest thing (washer.he/she) has ever done...

pieces.label: Wash Them Halfway
pieces.text: Wash Them Halfway.

pieces.label: Hang Them in a Tree
pieces.text: Hang Them in a Tree.
(Washer)'s own clothes vanish, and the bright ones are folded in (washer.his/her) size. A thank you, or a swap.
The clean clothes float away with nobody in them, and washing is just scrubbing now. "I did say."
A mist takes them, and leaves the stones cleaner than (washer) ever got them.
A shell necklace on a thread as fine as a hair, which never tangles and never gets wet.
Colours bright as parrot feathers.
Flat stones in the stream.
Scrubbing and singing.
"They don't like their laundry touched."

pieces.label: The Night Swim
pieces.text: Swimming in the glowing lagoon on a hot night, (swimmer2) has gone out past the reef, where something huge is moving in the black water, and glowing too.

pieces.label: Swim Out After (Name2)
pieces.text: (Swimmer1) swims hard, leaving a trail of blue sparks, out towards the reef and the dark water beyond it, where the huge glowing shape is turning slowly...

pieces.label: Shout from the Shallows
pieces.text: (Swimmer1) stands in the shallows and shouts (swimmer2)'s name until (swimmer1.his/her) voice cracks. Far out, (swimmer2)'s little trail of sparks stops, and turns, and then goes very still...

pieces.label: Wake the Fishers
pieces.text: Wake the Fishers.

pieces.label: Splash to Draw It Away
pieces.text: Splash to Draw It Away.
(Swimmer1) pushes (swimmer2) back to the reef, and the current takes (swimmer1). Never past the reef.
A whale glowing all over rolls once and blows a fountain of blue sparks. They sit till dawn, shaking and grinning.
The trail of sparks goes out and never lights again.
The sparks come back, and (swimmer2) says something passed underneath like a hill moving.
A swimmer leaves a trail like a comet.
A splash makes a shower of sparks.
"Not past the reef."
Something huge, turning slowly, glowing too.

pieces.label: The Eel Under the Rock
pieces.text: Old Thief, the arm-thick eel under the flat rock by the pool, has taken (fisher)'s whole catch, basket and all, and coiled round it in the dark.

pieces.label: Heave Up the Rock
pieces.text: (Fisher) wedges a stick under the edge of the rock, braces (fisher.his/her) feet on the slippery bank, and heaves. The rock lifts a hand's width. Underneath, Old Thief's eye opens...

pieces.label: Give It Up
pieces.text: (Fisher) sighs and lets the eel have it. "Enjoy it," (fisher.he/she) tells the rock, and walks back up the bank. Behind (fisher.him/her), something swirls in the pool...

pieces.label: Trade It a Fish
pieces.text: Trade It a Fish.

pieces.label: Reach Under the Rock
pieces.text: Reach Under the Rock.
The stick snaps, (fisher) hits (fisher.his/her) head on a stone, and the name just isn't there.
(Fisher) wrestles Old Thief for the basket and wins, and the children name (fisher.him/her) Unagi, because it sounds like an eel.
The empty basket comes back, and then three fish in the trap.
The children decide (fisher) is too polite for (fisher.his/her) old name, and (made1) sticks.
Older than the chief and as thick as a man's arm.
The children call it Old Thief.
An eye opens under the rock.
Splashing and slithering.

pieces.label: The Twin Pond
pieces.text: On a dare from (cousin), (swimmer) stands between the two mountain ponds, one warm and one cold, where anyone who swims across one and back through the other "comes out twice."

pieces.label: Swim Across and Back
pieces.text: (Swimmer) dives into the warm pond, swims across, climbs over the ridge at the far end, and slides into the cold one, gasping, and swims back. As (swimmer.he/she) climbs out, (cousin) stops grinning...

pieces.label: Just Paddle
pieces.text: (Swimmer) sits on the ridge beside (cousin) and dangles one foot in each pond, one warm, one cold. It is very strange. (swimmer.His/her) feet seem to be arguing with each other...

pieces.label: Push (Name2) In
pieces.text: Push (Cousin) In.

pieces.label: Swim Only the Warm One
pieces.text: Swim Only the Warm One.
Another (swimmer) climbs out of the warm pond, complaining about the cold. "Twice."
Two more (swimmer)s, one warm and cheerful, one cold and cross, arguing before they've stopped dripping.
One foot in each pond, and the two halves of (swimmer) make peace.
(Cousin) slips across both ponds, and another (cousin) climbs out, very cross.
A ridge of rock as narrow as a path.
One pond warm, one cold.
Feet that seem to be arguing.
"It was YOUR dare."

pieces.label: The Grandchild's Wish
pieces.text: (child), who has been learning little spells from the storyteller, wants to try a bigger one about "giving back time" on (grandparent), the oldest person (grandparent.he/she) loves.

pieces.label: Let (Him/Her) Finish
pieces.text: (Grandparent) closes (grandparent.his/her) eyes and lets the chanting wash over (grandparent.him/her). (child) scatters the dried flowers over (grandparent.his/her) head. They smell of summer, and they don't fall to the ground. They hang in the air, glowing...

pieces.label: Stop the Spell Gently
pieces.text: (Grandparent) takes (child)'s hands, very gently, and the chanting stops. "Not today," (grandparent.he/she) says. "I like being old. Tell me what the spell does instead..."

pieces.label: Ask the Storyteller
pieces.text: Ask the Storyteller.

pieces.label: Join In the Chant
pieces.text: Join In the Chant.
Twenty years, gone. (Grandparent) swings (child) round, which (grandparent.he/she) hasn't done in years.
(Grandparent) is twenty-five. "You'll still have to call me (Grandfather/Grandmother)."
Half a spell is still something: a smooth, bright face, and old knees.
(child) explains it all, learns all the ways it could go wrong, and gets very good at the little spells.
Dried flowers that hang in the air, glowing.
A song that makes flowers open.
A very serious face.
The storyteller stops dead.

pieces.label: The Frog Dance
pieces.text: (Frog), whose every dance turns into thirty hops round the fire, has been asked to lead the slow harvest dance, and (elder) warns that if (frog.he/she) hops, the old ones will try to keep up.

pieces.label: Dance It Slow
pieces.text: The drums start, slow and deep. (Frog) stamps, and sways, and holds the hops in with every muscle (frog.he/she) has. Round the fire behind (frog.him/her), the old ones follow, swaying, smiling...

pieces.label: Dance It (His/Her) Way
pieces.text: The drums start slow. (Frog) waits one beat, two, then gives the drummers a look, and the drums speed up, and (frog) starts to hop...

pieces.label: Hop Only at the End
pieces.text: Hop Only at the End.

pieces.label: Ask the Elders to Clap
pieces.text: Ask the Elders to Clap.
The slow stamp gets into (frog)'s feet and stays, and the itch to hop is gone.
The best harvest dance anyone remembers, and thirty hops round the fire at the very end.
(elder) hops once too often. "It was your dance. And it was worth it."
The old ones clap the beat while the young ones hop round them in a ring. A new dance.
Thirty hops round the fire.
Stamp and sway.
Slow, deep drums.
The elders call (frog.him/her) the Frog, not unkindly.

pieces.label: The Last Canoe
pieces.text: (carver), who has carved every canoe for fifty years, says this half-carved canoe will be (helper.his/her) last, and asks (helper) to help finish it.

pieces.label: Help Finish It
pieces.text: (Helper) works beside (carver) every day, doing the heavy work while the old carver does the fine shaping, (helper.his/her) shaking hands somehow steady on the wood...

pieces.label: Ask to Learn
pieces.text: (carver) looks at (helper) for a long time. Then (helper.he/she) hands (helper.him/her) the adze. "Then you'll carve it," (helper.he/she) says, "and I'll shout." (helper.He/She) sits down on a log, and starts shouting...

pieces.label: Bring More Helpers
pieces.text: Bring More Helpers.

pieces.label: Ask for Stories While Working
pieces.text: Ask for Stories While Working.
The most beautiful canoe (carver) ever made, and (helper)'s own work is better for life.
(carver) makes the last cut on the prow, smiles, and doesn't get up. (Helper) paddles it out first.
A lopsided first canoe that floats, and a carver who shouts from a log every day, happily.
The canoe is never finished, and the children play in it.
The shape of the hull just coming out of the wood.
Shaking hands somehow steady on the wood.
"Then you'll carve it, and I'll shout."
(carver)'s name carved on the prow.

pieces.label: The Seed of the Copy Tree
pieces.text: (Hopeful_parent) and (friend), long hoping for a baby, planted a trader's egg-sized seed from "the copy tree," which "gives you more of what you love most," and overnight it has sprouted into a humming silver-leaved sapling.

pieces.label: Ask the Tree for a Baby
pieces.text: They kneel by the sapling together, and (hopeful_parent) whispers to it, feeling silly. The humming changes. The silver leaves turn, all at once, as if listening...

pieces.label: Ask for Nothing
pieces.text: "Let's just see," says (friend). They sit down by the humming sapling and wait. It grows a little while they watch, and a single round fruit appears on it, silver and heavy...

pieces.label: Cut It Down
pieces.text: Cut It Down.

pieces.label: Ask It for Food
pieces.text: Ask It for Food.
The tree is gone by morning, leaving a ring of silver leaves, and a month later (hopeful_parent) is pregnant.
The tree decides what (friend) loves most is (hopeful_parent), and makes another. "I think it got confused."
They share the silver fruit, and (hopeful_parent) is pregnant. "It knew without asking."
A small silver orchard by the door, full of fruit that tastes of nothing in particular.
Leaves that are silver underneath.
A seed the size of an egg.
The silver leaves turn as if listening.
Two good baskets, and the trader left very early.

pieces.label: The Mango Tree
pieces.text: (Climber) has edged further out along the mango tree's longest branch, over the cliff above the bay, than anyone ever has, and the ripest mango is one arm's length away.

pieces.label: Reach for It
pieces.text: (Climber) stretches out, fingers spread, the branch dipping under (climber.him/her). (climber.His/her) fingertips brush the mango's warm skin...

pieces.label: Come Back
pieces.text: (Climber) looks down at the drop, and at the mango, and edges back along the branch, inch by inch, to the trunk. The elders on the ground let out a breath...

pieces.label: Hook It with a Stick
pieces.text: Hook It with a Stick.

pieces.label: Shake the Branch
pieces.text: Shake the Branch.
The branch cracks, and (climber) walks bent from then on. A mango every year, picked from a low branch.
The branch whips back, (climber)'s head hits the trunk, and the name never comes back. It was a very good mango.
A gust drops every mango into the bay, and the children swim out for them.
(Another_villager) laughs at (climber) for giving up, goes out on the branch, and it breaks.
Golden, enormous mangoes.
The branch dips over the drop.
The elders shout every year.
A thud the whole village hears.

pieces.label: The Wind Spirit's Visit
pieces.text: A young wind spirit, a whirlwind no taller than a child, has spent the morning poking at the village's thatch, and (elder) says if it's welcomed it will look after the roofs, and if crossed it will take them.

pieces.label: Welcome It
pieces.text: (Greeter) bows to the little whirlwind and says the old words of welcome. The whirlwind spins faster, delighted, and drops the spoon at (greeter.his/her) feet...

pieces.label: Chase It Out
pieces.text: (Greeter) waves (greeter.his/her) arms and shouts at the whirlwind, and some of the children join in, flapping mats at it. The whirlwind stops spinning for a moment...

pieces.label: Give It a Feather
pieces.text: Give It a Feather.

pieces.label: Follow It
pieces.text: Follow It.
It tucks every roof tight with woven leaves and settles in the tallest palm, humming on windy nights.
Wherever it spins, the villagers find a loose post, and by evening every hut is mended.
It swells up taller than a hut and throws (greeter)'s roof into the jungle. "I did say."
It drops its leaves in a sad heap and drifts away, and the spoon comes back by itself.
It came out of the cooking hut with a spoon.
Leaves and dust and feathers spinning.
Humming in the top of the tallest palm.
It seems to be looking at things.

pieces.label: The Apprentice's First Patient
pieces.text: Left in charge of the healers' hut for the first time, apprentice (apprentice) faces (patient) burning with fever and covered in spots, and must choose between (healer)'s way and a moss paste (healer) calls "old nonsense."

pieces.label: (Healer Name)'s Way
pieces.text: (Apprentice) brews the bitter bark tea exactly as (apprentice.he/she) has watched (healer) brew it a hundred times, and lays the cool cloths on (patient)'s forehead, and waits...

pieces.label: Try the Moss
pieces.text: (Apprentice) crushes the moss into a green paste and spreads it on (patient)'s spots, feeling (apprentice.his/her) heart pound. (Patient) says it smells like a wet dog...

pieces.label: Send for (Healer Name)
pieces.text: Send for (Healer).

pieces.label: Ask (Name2) What Helps
pieces.text: Ask (Patient) What Helps.
The fever breaks at midnight. (healer) nods once, and it is the proudest moment of (apprentice)'s life.
Three slow days, and then the two healers are teaching everyone what they found.
The moss works on everyone. "Old nonsense. I'll want to see the scroll."
The moss makes it much worse, and (healer) says nothing at all.
Bitter bark tea and cool cloths.
Moss paste that smells like a wet dog.
A year of fetching water and watching.
(healer) nods once. That's all.

pieces.label: The Swapping Shells
pieces.text: (Shell1) and (shell2) each hold one of a pair of pink conch shells "that talk to each other," and people who blow them together "end up in a muddle."

pieces.label: Blow at the Same Time
pieces.text: "One. Two. Three!" They blow together, and the two notes meet in the air between them and twist round each other into one long, strange sound that makes the gulls go up off the sand...

pieces.label: Wait
pieces.text: "Wait," says (shell1), and (shell2) blows on (friend.his/her) own. The note goes out over the sea, long and low, and (shell1) feels it in (shell1.his/her) teeth. Then, far out on the water, something answers...

pieces.label: Swap Shells First
pieces.text: Swap Shells First.

pieces.label: Throw Them in the Sea
pieces.text: Throw Them in the Sea.
The notes twist into one, and each is in the other's footprints. The shells go silent.
They've swapped hair, down to the cowlick.
Something beyond the horizon answers, and the shells talk to it all evening.
A moment late is close enough. "Close enough, apparently."
Two pink conch shells, exactly alike.
The gulls go up off the sand.
Felt in the teeth.
"On three."

pieces.label: The Lost Little Ones
pieces.text: A girl of about six walks out of the jungle carrying her baby brother, lost from her family when the river rose, and walks straight up to (healer): "Can you hold him? My arms are tired."

pieces.label: Take Them In
pieces.text: (Healer) takes the baby, who is heavy and asleep, and takes the girl's hand, and walks them both to (healer.his/her) hut. The girl eats three bowls of stew without stopping...

pieces.label: Search for the Family
pieces.text: (Healer) hands the children to the healers and gets the fishers together. They set off along the coast with canoes and torches, calling...

pieces.label: Feed Them First
pieces.text: Feed Them First.

pieces.label: Ask the Girl Where They Were
pieces.text: Ask the Girl Where They Were.
Nobody comes. The girl doesn't laugh for a long time, until (healer) does something silly with a spoon.
The parents come stumbling along the beach a week later, calling, and they stay.
The family is found on a sandbank, and the girl's scream sends the birds up off the whole island.
Only the empty camp. The girl nods as if she knew. (healer) takes the baby.
Two small children holding hands.
Three bowls of stew without stopping.
Scratched and filthy and very hungry.
"My arms are tired."

pieces.label: The Sleepwalker
pieces.text: For a week, (sleepwalker) has walked in (sleepwalker.his/her) sleep to the old burial ground every night; (healer) says tie (sleepwalker.him/her) up, and (sleepwalker.his/her) late grandmother always said whoever is calling should be answered.

pieces.label: Tie (Him/Her) to the Doorpost
pieces.text: They tie a soft rope round (sleepwalker)'s ankle and the other end to the doorpost. At midnight, (sleepwalker) gets up, eyes open and empty, and walks to the end of the rope, and pulls, and pulls...

pieces.label: Let (Him/Her) Walk
pieces.text: Let (sleepwalker.Him/Her) Walk.

pieces.label: And Follow
pieces.text: and Follow.

pieces.label: Wake (Him/Her) Up
pieces.text: Wake (sleepwalker.Him/Her) Up.

pieces.label: Sit Up with (Him/Her) All Night
pieces.text: Sit Up with (sleepwalker.Him/Her) All Night.
The rope holds all night, and (sleepwalker) wakes grey-haired, as if (sleepwalker.he/she) walked much further than the rope.
The rope is untied by small, careful fingers. Footprints walk in among the graves, none out.
At (sleepwalker.his/her) grandmother's grave (sleepwalker) listens, nods and sleeps, and wakes grey at the temples, calmer about everything.
A white mist wraps round (sleepwalker) at the grave, and there is nobody there.
Eyes open but empty.
Grey dust on (sleepwalker.his/her) feet in the mornings.
A covered torch between the old stones.
"Whoever is calling should be answered."

pieces.label: The Feather Crown
pieces.text: The great white bird that nested on (host)'s roof all season has left behind a ring of shining white feathers woven exactly like a crown, a once-a-lifetime gift for the house that sheltered it.

pieces.label: Wear It
pieces.text: (Host) lowers the feather crown onto (host.his/her) head. It's light, and cool, and it fits as if it grew there. The humming gets a little louder, then settles to a soft purr...

pieces.label: Hang It Up
pieces.text: (Host) hangs the crown from a peg over the door of (host.his/her) hut, where everyone can see it. It turns slowly in the breeze, shining...

pieces.label: Give It to the Chief
pieces.text: Give It to the Chief.

pieces.label: Put It Back on the Roof
pieces.text: Put It Back on the Roof.
The crown won't come off, and the feathers stay white through sun and smoke. The children call (host.him/her) the Bird Chief.
(Host)'s face grows brighter and younger under it. "Bright years for a kind roof."
The rain never leaks into (host)'s hut, and it gets very crowded during storms.
The bird comes back, touches (host)'s forehead with its beak, and (host) looks ten years younger.
Feathers that shine as if wet.
It hums like a shell held to the ear.
A soft purr.
"Bright years for a kind roof."

pieces.label: The Stone That Teaches
pieces.text: (researcher) finally lets (scholar), who loves learning, sleep with a hand on the Teacher, a black stone that teaches whoever sleeps on it something they didn't know, never the thing they wanted.

pieces.label: Ask for Something
pieces.text: (Scholar) whispers to the stone: "Teach me to be better at my work." Then (scholar.he/she) lies down beside it, with (scholar.his/her) hand on it, and closes (scholar.his/her) eyes...

pieces.label: Just Go to Sleep
pieces.text: (Scholar) doesn't ask. (scholar.He/She) just lies down with (scholar.his/her) hand on the cold stone, and lets (scholar.himself/herself) drift off, curious and a little scared...

pieces.label: Ask for Something Useless
pieces.text: Ask for Something Useless.

pieces.label: Sleep on It Two Nights
pieces.text: Sleep on It Two Nights.
For once the Teacher gives what was asked. "It never does that. It must like you."
Better at (scholar.his/her) work, and no wish to learn anything else. "Don't complain about what you get."
(Scholar) wakes knowing how many ripples a stone makes at noon, and proves it.
(Scholar) learns (scholar.he/she) doesn't need to know everything, and starts enjoying what (scholar.he/she) used to rush past.
A smooth black stone, cold under the palm.
How many teeth a shark has.
The chief's grandmother's favourite colour.
"Everything is worth knowing."

pieces.label: The Singing Boat
pieces.text: A big boat full of a whole singing family and a barking dog comes in from the open sea, and the old man in the stern calls out: "We are looking for a place where people sing back!"

pieces.label: Sing Back
pieces.text: (Greeter) doesn't know the words. (greeter.He/She) sings the chorus anyway, badly, as loud as (greeter.he/she) can. Behind (greeter.him/her), one by one, the whole village joins in...

pieces.label: Call for the Chief
pieces.text: (Greeter) runs to fetch the chief, who comes down the beach and makes a long, polite speech of welcome. The family listen politely. The old man looks a little disappointed...

pieces.label: Wave
pieces.text: Wave.

pieces.label: Drum Back
pieces.text: Drum Back.
The parents, their teenage daughter and their little son stay, and the dog barks at the waves every morning.
The old man stays. "I've found it. The rest of them can keep looking."
A polite speech, and the family sails on, singing. Someone hums the chorus, too late.
The chief, who has no voice at all, sings terribly. A young couple and their baby stay.
A dog on the prow barking at the waves.
A woven sail.
A chorus everyone can almost follow.
An accent nobody has heard before.

pieces.label: The Rain of Copies
pieces.text: A warm silver rain that "remembers faces" is falling, as it did once in (researcher)'s great-grandmother's time, and (soaked_one), standing in the biggest puddle, sees (soaked_one.his/her) reflection wink.

pieces.label: Stay in the Puddle
pieces.text: (Soaked_one) stays very still. The rain keeps falling round (soaked_one.him/her). In the puddle, the reflection is getting clearer and clearer, and more and more solid, and starts to lift its foot...

pieces.label: Step Out Quickly
pieces.text: (Soaked_one) jumps out of the puddle and runs for the nearest roof. Behind (soaked_one.him/her), the reflection stays where it was, in the water, looking up...

pieces.label: Splash the Reflection
pieces.text: Splash the Reflection.

pieces.label: Cover the Puddle
pieces.text: Cover the Puddle.
The reflection steps out, exactly (soaked_one). "A little more crowded."
It has (soaked_one)'s face and nothing else. "The rain only remembers faces."
The face rises from the puddle thirty steps away. "You left."
Just a soaking, and a lot of relief.
Drops as big as grapes.
Warm, silver-grey, heavy rain.
The reflection winks.
"A little more crowded."

pieces.label: The Wrong Jar
pieces.text: With (healer) sick and nobody else knowing where anything is, (patient) must pick between two jars of blue powder for (head_healer)'s rattling cough: the fish jar or the bird jar.

pieces.label: The Fish Jar
pieces.text: (Patient) mixes the blue powder from the fish jar with water and gives it to (head_healer), who drinks it, and makes a face like someone eating a lemon, and lies back...

pieces.label: The Bird Jar
pieces.text: (Patient) mixes the powder from the bird jar and gives it to (head_healer), who drinks it, coughs, and then goes very quiet...

pieces.label: Taste Both
pieces.text: Taste Both.

pieces.label: Ask the Researchers
pieces.text: Ask the Researchers.
The right one. (Patient) labels everything, and (healer) can never find anything again.
The fish jar is the chief's robe dye. (Head_healer) is blue for a season. "That's for cloth."
Two days of the best sleep of (head_healer)'s life, and the fever is gone.
The bird jar was the researchers' rare ground stone. (Head_healer) is cured; a year of work is gone.
One jar labelled with a fish, one with a bird.
"Which one has the chip in the lid?"
A face like someone eating a lemon.
"NOT COUGH."

pieces.label: The Fishing Contest
pieces.text: (Hard_worker), who is always working, has been entered in the yearly fishing contest by (hard_worker.his/her) friends without asking, and stands at the water with a borrowed spear while (fisher), last year's winner, wades out grinning.

pieces.label: Give It Everything
pieces.text: (Hard_worker) wades out and fishes the way (hard_worker.he/she) does everything: hard, fast, and without stopping for a moment. Fish after fish goes into the basket. The crowd starts to cheer...

pieces.label: Just Enjoy the Morning
pieces.text: (Hard_worker) wades out slowly, and stands in the warm water, and watches the little fish nibbling at (hard_worker.his/her) toes, and, for once, doesn't think about work at all...

pieces.label: Watch (Fisher Name) First
pieces.text: Watch (Fisher) First.

pieces.label: Fish With a Friend
pieces.text: Fish With a Friend.
(Hard_worker) wins by four fish, and the same attention makes (hard_worker.him/her) better at (hard_worker.his/her) own work.
(Hard_worker) fishes so hard (hard_worker.he/she) faints in the shallows, and still wins.
Two fish all morning, and the best morning of (hard_worker.his/her) life. (Hard_worker) starts taking mornings off.
Standing still, (hard_worker) sees a fish as big as a child, and wins without trying.
A whalebone fish-hook.
Little fish nibbling at (hard_worker.his/her) toes.
A fish as big as a child under a ledge.
Entered without asking.

pieces.label: The Flood
pieces.text: After nine days of rain, the stream has flooded the lower huts, and (rescuer) must choose between wading in for (elder), who can't walk without help, and saving the food stores before the water reaches them.

pieces.label: Go for (Elder Name)
pieces.text: (Rescuer) wades in, the water pulling at (rescuer.his/her) legs, and gets an arm round (elder), and starts back towards the bank, step by step, with the river shoving at them...

pieces.label: Save the Stores
pieces.text: (Rescuer) shouts to (elder) that help is coming, and runs up the hill to the stores, where the whole village is passing baskets hand to hand out of the water...

pieces.label: Throw a Rope
pieces.text: Throw a Rope.

pieces.label: Shout for More Help
pieces.text: Shout for More Help.
A whole tree comes down the river. (Rescuer) pushes (elder) clear, and the tree takes (rescuer).
(Rescuer) gets (elder) out, and half the stores go under. Nobody blames (rescuer.him/her).
The stores are saved, (elder) is pulled out bruised, and every hut is rebuilt on high posts.
The stores are saved, and the river takes the last hut and (elder) with it.
A brown roaring river carrying whole trees.
Water knee-deep in the paths.
Baskets passed hand to hand out of the water.
Huts rebuilt on high posts.

pieces.label: The Turtle Beach
pieces.text: Guarding the turtle nests all night, which the elders say will give a hopeful couple "a turn" of their own, (hopeful_parent) and (friend) hear a baby crying further along the dark beach.

pieces.label: Stay with the Nests
pieces.text: They stay. The crying goes on, far along the beach, and then stops. (Hopeful_parent) can't stop thinking about it. At dawn, the first hatchlings dig out of the sand and run for the sea...

pieces.label: Find the Baby
pieces.text: They leave the torch by the nests and run along the beach in the dark towards the crying. It gets louder, and closer, and then, round a rock, they find it...

pieces.label: One Stays
pieces.text: One Stays.

pieces.label: One Goes
pieces.text: One Goes.

pieces.label: Call Out
pieces.text: Call Out.
Every hatchling reaches the water, the old turtle looks at them, and (hopeful_parent) is pregnant.
They help a travelling family walk a colicky baby till it sleeps, and become much more patient people.
A baby left "for the turtles," hoping someone kind would be watching. Someone was.
It's a stranded young seal. The crabs get two nests, and (hopeful_parent) is pregnant anyway. "Close enough."
A great turtle crying turtle tears.
Hatchlings running for the sea at dawn.
A covered torch in the dark.
A cloth with a turtle-shell pattern.

pieces.label: The Talking Pig
pieces.text: One of the village pigs has started saying a name to (one_spoken_to), a name nobody in the village has, and today it has followed (one_spoken_to.him/her) to the gardens and climbed the tall garden wall to say it louder.

pieces.label: Answer to the Name
pieces.text: (One_spoken_to) looks at the pig, and sighs, and says, "Yes? What?" The pig looks enormously satisfied, and says the name once more, very softly, and climbs down off the wall...

pieces.label: Grab the Pig
pieces.text: (One_spoken_to) lunges for the pig as it wobbles, catches it round the middle, and both of them go over the other side of the wall together...

pieces.label: Tell the Elders
pieces.text: Tell the Elders.

pieces.label: Ask the Pig Why
pieces.text: Ask the Pig Why.
Everyone starts calling (one_spoken_to) "Obi," the pig's name, and nobody knows why.
The pig tells everyone else too, one by one, and the village calls (one_spoken_to) (made1).
(One_spoken_to) lands on (one_spoken_to.his/her) head with the pig on top, and the name is gone.
A soft compost pile, and the pig says "Thank you," and never speaks again.
The pig says it, and goes back to eating.
A tall garden wall and a wobbling pig.
A pile of soft compost.
A name nobody in the village has.

pieces.label: The Mask of Years
pieces.text: (Oldest_elder), the oldest elder, has a bad back and asks (wearer) to wear the Mask of Years at the Remembering festival, a mask said to "share the years" between wearer and elder for one night.

pieces.label: The Whole Festival
pieces.text: (Wearer) ties on the mask and dances, and sings, and leads the Remembering all night, while (oldest_elder) watches from (friend.his/her) seat. As the night goes on, (oldest_elder) sits up straighter...

pieces.label: Only the Opening Dance
pieces.text: (Wearer) wears the mask for the opening dance only, stamping slowly round the fire, then takes it off and gives it back to (oldest_elder), who holds it on (friend.his/her) knees all night...

pieces.label: Wear It Together
pieces.text: Wear It Together.

pieces.label: Give It to Someone Else
pieces.text: Give It to Someone Else.
(Wearer) wakes grey and lined, and (oldest_elder) young-faced. "I think it meant one night to do it."
The mask shared everything: (wearer) is in (oldest_elder)'s seat with (oldest_elder)'s bad back. (Wearer) needs a cushion.
One dance is enough for grey temples, and the young ones start asking (wearer) for advice.
Nothing happens, but (oldest_elder) tells (wearer) the stories behind the Remembering all night.
White hair of coconut fibre.
Eyes that seem to look at everyone at once.
Heavier than it looks, and warm.
"Share the years."

pieces.label: The Brave Child
pieces.text: (Brave_one), the smallest and most frightened child in the village, has decided to spend a night alone in the haunted hut on the hill, where (elder)'s "little bit magic" grandmother lived, and where brave children sometimes wake up older.

pieces.label: Go to the Hut
pieces.text: (Brave_one) climbs the hill at sunset with a basket and a blanket and a very small torch. The hut is dark and smells of old herbs. (brave_one.He/She) lies down, eyes wide open, and listens to every creak...

pieces.label: Stay Home
pieces.text: (Brave_one) looks at the hill, and the dark coming down, and unpacks the basket. (elder) sits down beside (brave_one.him/her) on the doorstep. "Brave isn't only doing the scary thing," (brave_one.he/she) says. "Want to hear about Grandmother?"

pieces.label: Take a Friend
pieces.text: Take a Friend.

pieces.label: Go at Dawn Instead
pieces.text: Go at Dawn Instead.
(Brave_one) walks down the hill fifteen and not afraid. "Grandmother liked brave ones."
Only creaks and an owl. Same age, much braver, and the owl becomes a ghost in the retelling.
(elder)'s grandmother was afraid of everything too. The next day (brave_one) walks past the pigs.
The next night (brave_one) goes alone after all, and comes down fourteen. "Especially stubborn ones."
A very small torch.
The hut smells of old herbs.
Every creak, eyes wide open.
"Not always. But sometimes."

pieces.label: The Moon in the Bowl
pieces.text: On the full moon night, (looker) has caught the moon exactly in the middle of a bowl of seawater, where the moon shows each face as it sees it, younger or old, and (looker.his/her) own face beside it is changing.

pieces.label: Keep Looking
pieces.text: (Looker) leans over the bowl and doesn't blink. The face in the water shifts and settles, like ripples finding their shape, and then holds still...

pieces.label: Tip the Bowl Out
pieces.text: Just as the face starts to change, (looker) loses (looker.his/her) nerve and tips the bowl over. The seawater runs off the stone into the sand, and the moon goes with it...

pieces.label: Call Someone to Look Too
pieces.text: Call Someone to Look Too.

pieces.label: Drink the Water
pieces.text: Drink the Water.
The moon sees (looker) young, and the whole village can see it in the morning.
The moon sees (looker) old and kind. "The moon thinks you're wise."
Half caught as it spills: a little younger, a little brighter. "Better than none."
The moon stays on the wet stone for a moment and fades. (Looker) is relieved.
The moon sitting exactly in the middle of the water.
Ripples finding their shape.
A flat stone behind the hut.
"Half a look. Better than none."

pieces.label: The Healing Rain
pieces.text: A warm, mint-scented rain falls from a clear sky, the once-in-a-lifetime rain that heals anyone who stands in it, "but only while it lasts," and the sick are lying in their huts.

pieces.label: Carry the Sick Out
pieces.text: (Healer) and the other healers run from hut to hut, carrying out anyone who can't walk on mats and on their backs, and laying them in the open, faces to the sky...

pieces.label: Gather the Rain in Pots
pieces.text: (Healer) puts out every pot, bowl and gourd in the village, and the rain fills them, and then it stops. (Healer) carries the first pot to the sickest hut...

pieces.label: Ring the Drum
pieces.text: Ring the Drum.

pieces.label: Lift the Roofs Off
pieces.text: Lift the Roofs Off.
Every sick villager is carried out in time, and sits up laughing, soaked to the skin.
The rain stops before the last huts. Three are cured, and (healer) catches a chill.
The rain in the pots still smells of mint, and still works, with a jar left over.
The first cup works; by the second it is only rain. The healers argue for a week.
Rain from a clear sky, smelling of crushed mint.
Faces to the sky.
Every pot, bowl and gourd in the village.
"Only while it lasts."

pieces.label: The Hut-Raising Song
pieces.text: Five huts are in pieces after last week's storm, and (elder) remembers the tune, but not all the words, of an old song that "makes the posts want to stand up," and asks (singer), who has the loudest voice, to lead it.

pieces.label: Lead the Song
pieces.text: At dawn (singer) stands on a tree stump in the middle of the broken huts and starts to sing, making up the words (elder) has forgotten. The whole village joins in on the chorus, and starts to work...

pieces.label: Work with the Builders
pieces.text: (Singer) decides hands are more use than a voice. (singer.He/She) spends the day lifting posts and tying thatch with the builders, sweating and swearing...

pieces.label: Sing and Work
pieces.text: Sing and Work.

pieces.label: Ask the Children to Sing
pieces.text: Ask the Children to Sing.
All five huts stand by sunset, and the words (singer) made up become the words.
A post stands up very suddenly and knocks (singer) off the stump.
An extra pair of strong hands, and the builders share their secret tricks.
(elder) sings half a song in a cracked voice all day, and the posts go up one by one.
A tree stump in the middle of the broken huts.
Everyone's voice is hoarse by sunset.
Sweating and swearing.
"Makes the posts want to stand up."

pieces.label: The Ghost Canoe
pieces.text: Out alone checking the fish traps on a still, foggy night, (fisher) finds the Ghost Canoe close enough to touch, its paddler wordlessly holding out a spare paddle.

pieces.label: Take the Paddle
pieces.text: (Fisher) reaches out and takes the paddle. It's cold and wet and very old, and it fits (fisher.his/her) hands perfectly. The paddler nods, and starts to paddle again, and (fisher)'s own canoe begins to drift along beside...

pieces.label: Turn Back
pieces.text: (Fisher) shakes (fisher.his/her) head, and turns (fisher.his/her) canoe for the shore, and paddles as hard as (fisher.he/she) can through the fog. Behind (fisher.him/her), there's the slow splash of another paddle, following...

pieces.label: Speak to the Paddler
pieces.text: Speak to the Paddler.

pieces.label: Sit Still and Wait
pieces.text: Sit Still and Wait.
(Fisher)'s empty canoe drifts in, and now there are two in the Ghost Canoe, and one of them waves.
(Fisher) paddles beside it all night, gives the paddle back at dawn, and knows the sea better than ever.
Paddling hard through the fog, (fisher) misses the gap in the reef.
(Fisher) runs all the way to the hut, and in the morning a very old paddle lies by the canoe.
Carved in a style nobody uses any more.
Paddling very slowly, never getting closer.
The slow splash of another paddle, following.
A spare paddle held out wordlessly.

pieces.label: The Grey Gull
pieces.text: A grey gull with a bad wing has followed (runner), who runs everywhere, for a week, and the fishers say it means "slow down, or you'll be made to"; now it lands on the steep path right in front of (runner.him/her).

pieces.label: Leap Over It
pieces.text: (Runner) jumps the gull without breaking stride, and lands on the loose stones on the other side, and the stones go out from under (runner.his/her) feet...

pieces.label: Stop
pieces.text: (Runner) skids to a halt, stones skittering away down the path, an arm's length from the gull. The gull looks up at (runner.him/her) with one yellow eye...

pieces.label: Shoo It Away
pieces.text: Shoo It Away.

pieces.label: Pick It Up
pieces.text: Pick It Up.
The loose stones go out from under (runner). (runner.He/She) walks with a stick from then on, and the gull sits quietly on the roof.
Bruised from head to foot but whole, and the next morning (runner) walks down, slowly, with the gull beside (runner.him/her).
The path ahead slides away with a roar where (runner) would have been, and (runner) walks everywhere after that.
A fishing line tangled round the bad wing. Freed, the gull flies straight up and is gone.
One yellow eye.
Loose stones on the steep path.
Flapping its good wing and squawking.
"Slow down, or you'll be made to."

pieces.label: The Doubling Pool
pieces.text: In the mangroves, (hanging_one) is hanging by one hand over the dark Doubling Pool, where anything that falls in comes out twice; the village has two canoes with the same crack in the prow to prove it.

pieces.label: Let Go
pieces.text: (Hanging_one) lets go. The water is cold, and so dark (hanging_one.he/she) can't see (hanging_one.his/her) own hands. (hanging_one.He/She) kicks up towards the light, and feels someone else kicking beside (hanging_one.him/her)...

pieces.label: Hang On and Shout
pieces.text: (Hanging_one) hangs on with both hands and shouts until (hanging_one.his/her) throat hurts. The branch bends lower, and lower, and (hanging_one.his/her) toes touch the black water...

pieces.label: Swing to the Bank
pieces.text: Swing to the Bank.

pieces.label: Pull (Himself/Herself) Up
pieces.text: Pull (hanging_one.Himself/Herself) Up.
Two heads come up, with the same weed in their hair, laughing the same laugh.
Three heads come up. "Well, this is going to be complicated."
Only a sandal falls in, and now (hanging_one) has three.
Only the toes touched the water, so only the outside came out.
A pool so dark it looks like a second sky.
Two canoes with the same crack in the prow.
Toes a hand's width above the water.
A spare sandal kept as a reminder.

pieces.label: The Mud Bath
pieces.text: A hot mud pool has bubbled up in the valley, and the pigs wallowing in it look years younger; the oldest sow even had piglets. (Bather)'s back has ached for years.

pieces.label: Get In
pieces.text: (Bather) wades in up to (bather.his/her) neck, between two delighted pigs. The mud is hot and thick and sucks at (bather.his/her) legs, and the ache in (bather.his/her) back starts to melt...

pieces.label: Take a Pot Home
pieces.text: (Bather) doesn't fancy the pigs. (bather.He/She) scoops up a big pot of the warm mud and carries it home, and spreads it on (bather.his/her) aching back, lying face down on (bather.his/her) mat...

pieces.label: Wait for the Pigs to Leave
pieces.text: Wait for the Pigs to Leave.

pieces.label: Ask (Healer Name) to Try It
pieces.text: Ask (Healer) to Try It.
(Bather) washes off fifteen years. Half the village is in the mud by nightfall.
One dunk of the head: a face fifteen years younger, and the same back.
The ache goes and doesn't come back, and (bather) stops complaining for a month.
The pot goes cold, and the hut smells of rotten eggs for a week.
Grey, warm mud smelling of rotten eggs.
Pigs running about like piglets.
Mud that sucks at the legs.
"Possibly a bit strong."

pieces.label: The Island Wedding
pieces.text: At (bride) and (friend)'s joining under the old flowering tree, (elder) holds up two strings of shells, one with one shell and one with three: "the number of babies the island will send."

pieces.label: The Three-Shell String
pieces.text: "Three," says (friend), before (bride) can stop (bride.him/her). The village roars with laughter. (elder) ties the three-shell string round both their wrists, and it rattles...

pieces.label: The One-Shell String
pieces.text: "One," says (bride), firmly. "One is plenty to start with." (elder) ties the one-shell string round their wrists, looking slightly disappointed...

pieces.label: Both Strings
pieces.text: Both Strings.

pieces.label: Neither String
pieces.text: Neither String.
The healers tell them to expect {#babies:a baby|twins|triplets}, and (friend) sits down under the tree.
A basket under the tree the next morning, with a baby nobody knows. "Well, that's one."
One baby, exactly as the string said. (elder) keeps the three-shell string for the next wedding.
The one-shell string, and the healers say {#babies:a baby|twins|triplets}. The island has its own ideas.
The old flowering tree at the top of the beach.
A string of shells that rattles.
A wicked smile.
"The number of babies the island will send."

pieces.label: The Long Night Fire
pieces.text: On the longest night, (fire_keeper) must keep the big fire burning till dawn while the village teaches each other, because the long night fire "makes skills take root," but at midnight the wood runs low and the rain starts.

pieces.label: Go for Wood
pieces.text: (Fire_keeper) wraps up against the rain and goes into the dark jungle with an axe, feeling for dry branches under the big trees, while behind (fire_keeper.him/her) the fire sinks lower and lower...

pieces.label: Burn the Spare Thatch
pieces.text: (Fire_keeper) drags the bundles of spare thatch out of the store and feeds them to the fire one by one. The fire flares up bright and hot and crackling, and the builders, asleep, don't notice...

pieces.label: Wake Someone to Help
pieces.text: Wake Someone to Help.

pieces.label: Move Everyone Under a Roof
pieces.text: Move Everyone Under a Roof.
(Fire_keeper) comes back just in time, the fire roars, and everyone learns something by dawn; (fire_keeper) most of all.
A root, an axe handle, a cracked rib, and the fire is out.
The thatch burns so bright nobody sleeps, and (builder) doesn't speak to (fire_keeper) for a week. Worth it.
A burning wisp lands on the research hut, and a season of notes goes up.
The fire sinking lower and lower.
Rain on the dark jungle.
Teaching each other till dawn.
"Makes skills take root."

pieces.label: The Seed Traders
pieces.text: A noisy, cheerful family of seed traders lays out a hundred kinds of seeds on the beach, wanting the village's seeds and "something to wear that we haven't got," and their tall grandson looks as if he'd like to stay.

pieces.label: Trade (His/Her) Clothes
pieces.text: (Trader) takes off (trader.his/her) outer wrap and holds it out. The grandmother claps her hands, delighted, and starts digging through the mats for her very best packets...

pieces.label: Trade the Village's Seeds
pieces.text: (Trader) fetches baskets of the village's own seeds from the store, and the trading goes on all afternoon, with a lot of shouting and laughing and arguing about yams...

pieces.label: Trade Stories
pieces.text: Trade Stories.

pieces.label: Invite Them to Stay
pieces.text: Invite Them to Stay.
The grandmother gives (trader) rare seeds and her own embroidered clothes, and the crop is new to everyone.
The grandson wades back to shore. "Yours is the first he meant."
A basket of new seeds, everyone eats too much, and the traders sail away singing.
The son, his wife and the grandson stay to see the new seeds grow. "Somebody has to."
A hundred kinds of seeds in little leaf packets.
Arguing about yams.
Clothes embroidered with seeds of every shape.
"Something to wear that we haven't got."

pieces.label: The Night the Roofs Flew
pieces.text: A night of howling wind pulls the thatch off three huts, and one roof ends up sitting almost whole in the taro patch.

pieces.label: Gather Everyone Now
pieces.text: (Organiser) walks from hut to hut, knocking on doors that are still standing and calling into the ones that aren't. Soon there is a line of villagers passing thatch up ladders, and (builder) is shouting directions from a rooftop...

pieces.label: Wait for Dry Weather
pieces.text: "Properly, then," says (organiser). The families with no roofs squeeze in with neighbours, and everyone waits for the sun, which takes its time...
By sunset every roof is back on, one with a coconut stuck in it that (builder) calls "structural."
Eight people carry the taro-patch roof home singing, and it fits perfectly.
Three dry days, and (builder)'s new roofs are better than the old ones ever were.
It drizzles for a week, everyone snores, and three roofs end up like birds' nests.
Bundles of thatch hang in the trees like washing.
A roof sits, almost whole, in the middle of the taro patch.
"Wet thatch rots," says (builder).

pieces.label: The Canoe Beyond the Reef
pieces.text: A canoe with a torn sail drifts outside the reef, and someone in it is waving a paddle slowly, as if they've been waving for a long time.

pieces.label: Swim Out to Them
pieces.text: (Rescuer) drops the net, wades in and starts swimming. The water over the reef is choppy and full of churned sand, and (rescuer.he/she) has to pick (rescuer.his/her) way carefully between the coral heads...

pieces.label: Light a Signal Fire
pieces.text: (Rescuer) runs up the beach, piles driftwood on the old fire pit and blows on the embers until the flames catch. (rescuer.He/She) throws green palm fronds on top, and a column of thick white smoke goes up...
A young couple and their laughing baby, nine days at sea, are guided through the reef and stay.
The coral cuts (rescuer)'s leg on the way out, but (rescuer.he/she) brings in an adult, a teenager and a sleeping child.
The canoe follows the smoke through the gap, and a young couple climb out with their baby. "We followed your smoke."
The current takes the canoe past the point. (Rescuer) keeps the fire burning all night anyway.
The sail is torn to ribbons.
The tide is turning over the reef.
A column of thick white smoke goes up from the green palm fronds.

pieces.label: The Fever and the Bitter Root
pieces.text: (Patient) has had a fever for four days, and (healer) knows of one more cure: a swamp root so bitter people faint from it.

pieces.label: Swallow the Root
pieces.text: (healer) wades into the swamp up to (patient.his/her) waist and comes back with a muddy black root that smells like a wet boot. (patient.He/She) grinds it to a paste. (Patient) holds (patient.his/her) nose and swallows...

pieces.label: Wait It Out
pieces.text: "No roots," whispers (patient). (healer) nods, piles on a third blanket and sits by the mat with a bowl of cool water and a cloth. (patient.He/She) stays all night...
The fever is gone by evening, but everything (patient) eats now tastes like a wet boot.
The root breaks the fever and is too strong for (patient)'s worn-out body. (patient.His/her) hands never stop trembling.
The fever breaks before dawn, and (healer), asleep sitting up, writes down every step.
A slow week of broth in the shade. (Patient) mends, slowly.
The black root smells like a wet boot.
(Patient) shivers under two blankets in the middle of the afternoon.
(healer) sits by the mat all night with a bowl of cool water.

pieces.label: The Old Fisher's Last Tide
pieces.text: The village's oldest fisher carries (fisher.his/her) canoe down into a heavy swell, and (young) is waiting at the shoreline, asking to come along.

pieces.label: Go Out Alone
pieces.text: "Not today," says (fisher), and pushes off. (young) watches the little canoe climb the swells, drop, climb again, until it rounds the point...

pieces.label: Take (Young Name) Along
pieces.text: (Fisher) jerks (fisher.his/her) head at the canoe. "In. Sit still. Don't talk." (young) scrambles in, and they paddle out together into the swell...
The canoe drifts back with the paddle still inside, and (fisher) is found peaceful on the sand. The village buries (fisher.him/her) facing the sea.
The canoe never comes back. "A fisher that old has earned the right to choose," say the elders.
(Fisher) shows (young) the dark water where the big ones wait. "Well. You'll do."
The swell turns them back, and half the village ends up on the beach hearing about the shark that stole (fisher)'s hat.
(Fisher)'s hands are knotted like old rope.
The canoe climbs the swell, drops, climbs again.
"Sit still. Don't talk."

pieces.label: The Glass Pool in the Cave
pieces.text: At the back of the cave behind the waterfall, (visitor) leans over a pool still as glass, and a second reflection of (visitor) appears beside the first.

pieces.label: Touch the Water
pieces.text: (Visitor) reaches out one finger and touches the surface. It isn't cold. It isn't wet, either. It feels like touching someone else's hand...

pieces.label: Back Away Slowly
pieces.text: (Visitor) doesn't move (visitor.his/her) eyes from the pool, and takes one careful step back, then another. The second reflection doesn't follow. It just keeps leaning, watching...
{#made:An exact copy|Two exact copies} of (visitor) {#made:steps|step} out, dry as bones, arguing about who carries the basket.
One steps out with (visitor)'s face and none of (visitor)'s tastes, and calls itself (made1).
(Visitor) gets out with the basket and covers (visitor.his/her) mirror for a month.
A drop from the cave roof smooths (visitor)'s face to what it was years ago. The pool kept the old one.
The water fell from a falling star, the elders say.
The surface feels like touching someone else's hand.
The children dare each other to go in.

pieces.label: The Vine Swing Over the Gorge
pieces.text: The teenagers have tied a vine over the gorge, and today they hold it out to (swinger), who has never liked heights.

pieces.label: Grab the Vine
pieces.text: (Swinger) takes the vine in both hands, closes (swinger.his/her) eyes, and runs off the edge. For one long moment (swinger.he/she) is flying...

pieces.label: Tell Them No
pieces.text: "No," says (swinger). "Not today." The teenagers groan and start teasing (swinger.him/her), and then one of them takes the vine and swings out to show (swinger.him/her) how easy it is...
(Swinger) flies across the gorge with birds under (swinger.his/her) feet, and the fear just lets go.
(Swinger) lets go too soon and cracks (swinger.his/her) head on a rock. The village calls (swinger.him/her) "?", gently, until the name comes back.
The vine snaps under (teen), who walks with a limp from then on.
(Swinger) watches from a rock and decides being scared is just a sensible feeling with a bad reputation.
The teenagers shriek as they swing out over the drop.
The river glitters far below.
"Unless you're scared."

pieces.label: The Red Moon and the Midwife
pieces.text: The moon rises red over the sea, and (midwife), the oldest healer, warns (mother) and (friend) that any child conceived under it comes into the world in company.

pieces.label: Stay and Watch the Moon
pieces.text: They laugh, and (midwife) shrugs and walks on. The red moon climbs higher and the sea turns the colour of embers...

pieces.label: Take the Advice and Go In
pieces.text: (Friend) laughs, but (mother) gets up. "Better safe," she says. They head back up the path, past the healers' hut, where a small sound is coming from the doorstep...
(midwife) listens to (mother)'s belly and holds up {#babies:one finger|two fingers|three fingers}. (Friend) has to sit down.
One baby, just one. "The moon can't be right every time."
A baby in a red cloth waits on the healers' doorstep. "Company, I said."
They sleep soundly. The neighbours who stayed out are very quiet at breakfast.
The sea turns the colour of embers.
(midwife) walks past with (mother.his/her) lantern.
Everyone else says it with a wink.

pieces.label: The Feast Nobody Planned
pieces.text: (Host) brings a single fish to the cooking fire, and by afternoon the whole village has piled on yams, stew, mangoes and sweet potatoes, and (cook) wants to know if there's a feast.

pieces.label: Call It a Feast
pieces.text: "It's a feast," says (host). A cheer goes up. The drummers fetch their drums, and (cook) throws (host.his/her) hands in the air and starts giving orders...

pieces.label: Pack It Away for Later
pieces.text: "Let's not waste it," says (host). There is some grumbling, but people start wrapping food in leaves and carrying it to the store. (cook) supervises, and finds the job oddly pleasant...
The drums come out and (cook) is carried around the fire, protesting.
(Host) eats everything so nothing goes to waste, and the smell of cooking makes (host.him/her) ill for a long time after.
The food store is cleaned out and filled in one afternoon, and the smell of ripe fruit stops turning (cook)'s stomach.
The children sulk, and the reheated stew is even better the next day.
Somebody's aunt brings stew "because it would only go to waste."
The children fall asleep in heaps.
"Is there a feast?"

pieces.label: The Grandchild's First Spell
pieces.text: (child), who has been following the village's spell-keeper for a month, runs up to (elder) with a bundle of herbs, a feather and a seashell. "It makes you young. Can I try it on you?"

pieces.label: Let (Child Name) Try
pieces.text: (Elder) sits down on a log and closes (elder.his/her) eyes. (child) waves the bundle around (elder.his/her) head three times and says a long word that (elder.he/she) gets wrong twice...

pieces.label: Gently Say No
pieces.text: "Not today," says (elder), "but tell me how it works." (child) sits beside (elder.him/her) and explains the spell at great length, with diagrams drawn in the dirt...
(Elder)'s face is forty years younger; (elder.his/her) knees creak exactly as before. "You only did the face."
The word was said backwards, and (elder) looks older than ever. The spell-keeper starts proper lessons.
(child) gives (elder) the seashell and the name of the hero in the spell-keeper's shell story, and the whole village takes it up.
The herbs turn out to be good for sore knees, once they are boiled.
(child) gets the long word wrong twice.
Diagrams are drawn in the dirt.
(Elder)'s knees agree loudly every morning that (elder.he/she) is an elder.

pieces.label: The Contest of Best Hands
pieces.text: (chief) announces a contest: by sunset tomorrow, everyone must bring the best thing they can make with their own hands, and (contestant) has never won anything.

pieces.label: Do What (He/She) Does Best
pieces.text: (Contestant) works all night by the firelight, doing the thing (contestant.he/she) knows best, slowly and carefully, the way (contestant.he/she) has always wanted to and never had the time...

pieces.label: Try Something New
pieces.text: (Contestant) decides to try something nobody has ever seen (contestant.him/her) do. (contestant.He/She) borrows tools, asks questions, and gets in everyone's way...
It's the best work (contestant) has ever done, and (contestant.he/she) wears the feathered headband to bed for a week.
Everyone works so hard that (chief) gives feathers to three other villagers.
(Contestant) builds a lopsided stool, and the splinters stop bothering (contestant.him/her). A feather "for nerve."
The driftwood tower falls four times, the last time on (contestant)'s foot. (contestant.He/She) never enjoys building again.
The winner wears the chief's feathered headband for a week.
(Contestant) works all night by the firelight.
(Contestant) borrows tools and gets in everyone's way.

pieces.label: The Lightning Under the Banyan
pieces.text: Lightning comes down through the banyan's hanging roots while (first) and (second) are arguing about whose turn it is to fetch water, and they sit up in each other's bodies.

pieces.label: Go Straight to the Healers
pieces.text: They stagger to the healers' hut together, each of them tripping over the other's feet. (healer), the head healer, listens to the whole story, looks at them both for a long time, and reaches for a clay pot with a stopper in it...

pieces.label: Fix It Themselves
pieces.text: "Lightning did it," says (second), in (first)'s voice, "so lightning can undo it." They stand back under the smoking banyan as the storm grumbles around the hills, waiting for it to strike again...
Pots, smoke, cold river, steam hut: nothing works. In the morning (first) fetches the water without a word.
A pot that smells like a burnt goat makes them sneeze back into their own bodies.
The storm moves on, and after a month of carrying each other's water jars, the fetching stops bothering either of them.
The lightning strikes again. They wake in the mud in their own bodies, with singed eyebrows.
The sky goes green over the hills.
Every root of the banyan is smoking.
Neither of them will be the first to walk away.

pieces.label: The Basket in the Mangroves
pieces.text: Cutting mangrove poles at low tide, (finder) finds a basket wedged in the roots with a furious baby inside and a little carved bird tied to the handle.

pieces.label: Take the Baby Home
pieces.text: (Finder) lifts the basket clear of the mud and carries it home on (finder.his/her) hip, the baby yelling the whole way. People come out of their huts to see what the noise is...

pieces.label: Search for the Family
pieces.text: (Finder) tucks the basket up high in the roots, safe from the tide, and starts wading along the shore, calling out. Around the bend, (finder.he/she) hears someone calling back...
"Whoever finds the basket keeps the basket." By the end of the week (finder) can change a wrap one-handed while eating.
The baby falls asleep in (name2)'s arms at once. "That's decided."
Around the bend a family is bailing a swamped canoe. The basket floated off in the night. They stay.
Nobody, only a heron watching from the roots. (Finder) raises the baby, and herons visit (finder.his/her) roof.
The baby is red-faced and furious.
A little carved bird is tied to the handle.
The tide will be back in an hour.

pieces.label: The Ring of White Stones
pieces.text: On a moonless night, the gaps in the ring of white stones on the ridge shimmer and hum like a hive, and (walker) can see them from the path home.

pieces.label: Step Into the Ring
pieces.text: (Walker) walks between two of the white stones. The humming fills (walker.his/her) ears, (walker.his/her) chest, (walker.his/her) teeth. The world on the other side of the gap looks almost the same as this one, but brighter...

pieces.label: Hurry Home
pieces.text: (Walker) puts (walker.his/her) head down and walks very fast. The humming follows (walker.him/her) all the way down the ridge, softer and softer, like someone calling (walker.his/her) name and then giving up...
(Walker)'s footprints stop between two stones. On the next moonless night, people swear someone waves from the other side.
(Walker) steps back out, and an exact copy follows. "I'm not going back in."
In the lamplight (walker)'s face is years younger, as if (walker.he/she) brought a little of the other side home.
Nothing follows. In daylight the stones are warm, with lizards on top.
The first people found the stones already standing.
The gaps shimmer like heat over a fire.
The humming fills (walker)'s teeth.

pieces.label: The Last Bundle of Thatch
pieces.text: (Builder) has one bundle of thatch left to tie on the meeting hut's peak, the light is going, and the rafter at the top has a crack (builder.he/she) meant to mention.

pieces.label: Finish the Roof
pieces.text: (Builder) climbs to the very top, straddles the ridgepole, and starts tying the last bundle on in the dusk. The cracked rafter creaks under (builder.him/her)...

pieces.label: Come Down
pieces.text: (Builder) sighs, looks at the cracked rafter one more time, and climbs down. "Somebody look at that in the morning," (builder.he/she) says. Everybody nods...
The rafter holds, and (builder) patches two more leaks by lamplight before the rain.
The cracked rafter snaps, and (builder)'s back is never the same.
The builders check every rafter in the village and find nine cracked ones.
A puddle the size of a pond in the meeting hall, and the children sail leaf boats in it.
The ladder is wobbly.
(Builder) straddles the ridgepole in the dusk.
"Somebody look at that in the morning."

pieces.label: The Coughing Season
pieces.text: A cough has the village barking like seals at night, and (healer), the healer on duty, must choose between the elders' steam hut and a traveller's eucalyptus salve.

pieces.label: Build a Steam Hut
pieces.text: (Healer) and the other healers heat stones in the fire all morning and roll them into a little hut of woven leaves. They pour water on them, and the hut fills with thick white steam...

pieces.label: Try the Traveller's Salve
pieces.text: (Healer) crushes a basket of eucalyptus leaves with a little coconut oil and rubs it onto (sick)'s chest and back. The smell is so strong it makes everyone's eyes water...
Half the village takes a turn in the steam hut, and the nights go quiet again.
Cured, but boiled pink, and (sick) never loves (healer.his/her) sleeping mat again.
The salve works and the village smells like a forest. The recipe gets the traveller's name.
The salve brings out a rash, and the cough eases slowly.
Half the huts are barking like seals at night.
The steam hut fills with thick white steam.
The salve makes everyone's eyes water.

pieces.label: The Traveller Who Collects Names
pieces.text: A traveller in a grey cloak sewn with knots of string, one for every name (subject.he/she) has collected, asks (subject) to tie one more knot and say (subject.his/her) name while doing it.

pieces.label: Tie the Knot
pieces.text: (Subject) takes the string, says (subject.his/her) own name out loud, and ties a knot. The traveller smiles for the first time. The knot tightens on its own...

pieces.label: Refuse
pieces.text: "No," says (subject). "Sorry. My name stays here." The traveller's pale eyes narrow. For a moment the knots on the cloak all seem to rustle at once...
The knot tightens on its own, and (subject)'s name goes with it. The village calls (subject.him/her) "?".
"Fair's fair." The traveller trades an old knot, and (subject) wakes as (made1).
In the morning (follower)'s footprints lead down to the water beside the traveller's.
"One day," the traveller sighs. A grey knot left on the doorstep burns with a whisper.
The cloak is sewn all over with tiny knots of string.
The traveller has very pale eyes.
The knots on the cloak all rustle at once.

pieces.label: The Wishing Well's Old Coin
pieces.text: At the bottom of the old dry well, (finder) finds a shell coin scratched with (finder.his/her) grandmother's saying: "Give back what you take, and the well gives back what time took."

pieces.label: Throw It Back In
pieces.text: (Finder) climbs back out, stands at the edge, and drops the coin. It falls a long way for such a shallow well. Somewhere far below, (finder.he/she) hears a splash, though the well has been dry for years...

pieces.label: Keep It
pieces.text: (Finder) decides that a three-generations-old coin is worth more in (finder.his/her) pocket than in a hole. (finder.He/She) takes it home and puts it on the shelf by (finder.his/her) sleeping mat...
The well breathes out a breath that smells of rain, and (finder) walks home ten years younger.
The well breathes in instead, and (finder) comes home ten years older. "I must have said it backwards."
The coin reminds (finder) of (finder.his/her) grandmother singing in the gardens, and the feel of soil stops bothering (finder.him/her).
The coin is back at the bottom of the well in the morning. (Finder) leaves it there.
The coin is worn smooth by many thumbs.
The coin falls a long way for such a shallow well.
A splash comes from far below, though the well has been dry for years.

pieces.label: The Game That Went Too Far
pieces.text: (First) and (second) have played stones on the same flat rock every evening for a year, and tonight half the village gathers to watch them glare at each other.

pieces.label: Call It Off
pieces.text: (First) sweeps the stones off the rock into the bag. "That's it," (first.he/she) says. "No more. It's not fun any more." The crowd goes quiet...

pieces.label: One Last Game
pieces.text: "One last game," says (first). "Winner takes all." (Second) nods. The crowd closes in. The first stone goes down with a click that everyone hears...
The fun never comes back, and neither of them wants to play anything again.
With empty evenings, they help in the gardens together, and the dirt stops bothering them.
A perfect draw, the first in a year. The whole crowd laughs with them.
(First) wins with the last stone, and (second) gives the bag to the children. "I'm done."
The first stone goes down with a click that everyone hears.
"You looked at the sunset on purpose."
The flat rock sits empty in the evenings.

pieces.label: The Elder Who Wandered Off
pieces.text: (Elder), an elder who has been forgetting things lately, went out for firewood and hasn't come back, and (searcher) has found (elder.his/her) half-full basket in the middle of the path at dusk.

pieces.label: Go Now
pieces.text: Go Now.

pieces.label: Alone
pieces.text: Alone.

pieces.label: Wait for Morning
pieces.text: It's too dangerous in the dark, and everyone knows it. (Searcher) lights a fire at the edge of the jungle and keeps it burning all night so (elder) can see it. At first light, ten people go in together...
(Elder) is eating roasted taro by the campfire of a family living rough in the hills. All five walk home, and the family stays.
(Searcher) finds (elder) at the bottom of a slope, already gone, and carries (elder.him/her) home.
Asleep in a fig tree, and a bit offended by all the fuss.
Three days of searching find only one sandal by the stream.
The basket of sticks sits in the middle of the path.
The jungle swallows the sound of (elder)'s name.
A fire burns all night at the edge of the jungle.

pieces.label: The Warm Stone of the Mothers
pieces.text: Beside the hot spring sits a black stone where a sea spirit once rested after giving birth to the first fish, and couples who want a child sit on it together.

pieces.label: Sit on the Stone Together
pieces.text: They sit on the stone side by side, holding hands, feeling a bit silly. The stone gets warmer and warmer until it is almost hot, and then, very gently, it hums...

pieces.label: Just Bathe
pieces.text: They decide not to bother the stone, and slip into the hot spring instead. The water is so warm they nearly fall asleep, floating under the stars...
(First) is pregnant, and the healers say it shouldn't be possible. "The stone decides."
The stone hums so loudly the spring trembles. {#babies:One big strong baby|Twins|Triplets}.
A baby is on the way, stone or no stone. The elders think the stone can reach the spring.
No baby yet, but the weekly soak turns two people who never liked the water into swimmers.
The stone is warm as a hand.
They float under the stars in the hot spring.
"The stone decides."

pieces.label: The Dream-Sharing Tea
pieces.text: (healer) has brewed a tea from the purple cliff flowers that lets two sleepers share a dream, and wants (first) and (second), who just fell out over a broken spear, to try it.

pieces.label: Drink It Together
pieces.text: They drink, grimacing, and lie down on mats side by side. Within moments both of them are asleep, and dreaming the same dream: a beach, a broken spear, and each other...

pieces.label: Hand It Back
pieces.text: "I'm not drinking anything purple," says (first). (Second) agrees for once. (healer) sighs, looks at the cups, and before anyone can stop (first.him/her), drinks one (first.himself/herself), and hands the other to (first.his/her) assistant, (assistant)...
They forgive each other in the dream, then wake on each other's mats in each other's bodies, for good.
A night and a day of fishing together in a shared dream, and the wet nets and fish guts stop bothering them.
The healers drink it themselves and wake in each other's bodies. "How do you live with these knees?"
The healers snore all afternoon, and the argument is forgotten.
The tea is made from the purple flowers on the cliffs.
"It'll help. Probably."
The same dream: a beach, a broken spear, and each other.

pieces.label: The Baby in the Whale's Wake
pieces.text: A whale swims along the reef all morning, and when it turns out to sea, it leaves a kelp bundle on the sand with a baby inside, fast asleep.

pieces.label: Take the Baby In
pieces.text: (Finder) picks up the bundle. The baby opens its eyes, looks at (finder.him/her) very seriously, and grabs (finder.his/her) finger in a tiny fist...

pieces.label: Ask Along the Coast
pieces.text: The healers take the baby in, and (finder) sets off along the coast in a canoe, stopping at every cove and fishing camp to ask...
The baby grabs (finder)'s finger, and every year the whale comes back to be waved at.
"Only you would come home from watching a whale with a baby." They raise it together.
At the third cove, a frantic young couple. "The whale chose your beach. So do we."
Nobody is missing a baby, and it reaches for (finder) the moment (finder.he/she) walks in.
The whale blows great clouds of spray.
The kelp bundle is tied neatly with a strip of bark.
The baby smells of salt.

pieces.label: The Echo Conch
pieces.text: (keeper), the spell-keeper, has finished a spell to make a conch answer back in the voice of whoever blows it, and asks (tester) to blow it, very gently.

pieces.label: Blow Gently
pieces.text: (Tester) puts the shell to (tester.his/her) lips and breathes into it, very softly. The conch sighs back, in (tester)'s own voice, and then the sound keeps going, getting louder, and starts to take a shape...

pieces.label: Give It a Proper Blast
pieces.text: (Tester) fills (tester.his/her) lungs and blows as hard as (tester.he/she) can. The conch roars like a storm. (keeper) throws (tester.himself/herself) flat on the ground...
The sound folds into an exact copy of (tester). "Oh no. Too much."
Not a perfect echo: (tester)'s face, a different person, who hates yams.
The roar becomes {#made:an exact copy|two exact copies}. "I said gently."
The conch cracks down the middle. "A whole month."
"Gently. Very gently. I mean it."
The conch roars like a storm.
(Tester) is carrying an armful of yams.

pieces.label: The Termites in the Rafters
pieces.text: A doorpost crumbles under (builder)'s hand: termites have hollowed the rafters across the village, including the shelves of the scroll hut.

pieces.label: Prop Up the Huts
pieces.text: (Builder) runs from hut to hut, shouting for the builders. They drag in every spare pole in the village and start jamming them under the sagging rafters, one hut after another...

pieces.label: Save the Scrolls
pieces.text: (Builder) runs to the scroll hut and starts carrying scrolls out into the sun by the armful. Behind (builder.him/her) the shelves are already beginning to lean...
Every hut stands, but the scroll shelves give way and the scroll-keepers spend a week copying chewed scrolls.
(Builder) teaches every builder to hear the dry papery sound of termite wood.
Every scroll comes out, and the village props up the huts by torchlight.
Two huts fall in the night, and (builder) rebuilds both alone out of guilt.
The doorpost crumbles to powder.
Wood eaten from the inside makes a dry, papery sound.
Termites won't touch ironwood.

pieces.label: The Old Healer's Last Season
pieces.text: (Healer), a healer for fifty years, has started to shake and mix up jars, and the chief tells (healer.him/her) it is time to rest.

pieces.label: Keep Working
pieces.text: "I'll rest when I'm dead," says (healer), and goes back to the healers' hut. (healer.He/She) works the whole season, slowly, carefully, double-checking every jar...

pieces.label: Step Aside
pieces.text: (Healer) hangs (healer.his/her) healer's bag on the hook by the door and walks out into the sun. The first morning, (healer.he/she) doesn't know what to do with (healer.his/her) hands...
(Healer) dozes off on the bench outside the healers' hut with a bowl of leaves in (healer.his/her) lap, and doesn't wake.
A strict, impatient season of lessons, and every healer is the better for it.
(Healer) finds (healer.he/she) doesn't miss healing at all. "Ask someone who still cares."
Fifty years of stories at the cooking fire, mostly about the people sitting right there.
(Healer) has delivered half the village.
A fisher sneezed for a day.
The healer's bag hangs on the hook by the door.

pieces.label: The Statue Under the Lagoon
pieces.text: The lagoon is clearer than anyone can remember, and from the canoes (diver) can see a huge stone ancestor's face on the bottom, with fish swimming through its mouth.

pieces.label: Dive Down to It
pieces.text: (Diver) takes three long breaths and goes over the side. The water gets colder and greener as (diver.he/she) goes down. The stone face gets bigger and bigger. Its eyes seem to follow (diver.him/her)...

pieces.label: Leave It Alone
pieces.text: (Diver) looks down at the stone face for a long time and then picks up (diver.his/her) paddle. "It's been sleeping a long time," (diver.he/she) says. "Let it sleep." As they paddle away, the water ripples, though there's no wind...
(Diver) touches the stone cheek and comes up with a young face. "It said thank you. For visiting."
(Diver) touches the face and never comes up. Fishers hear laughing under the lagoon.
The face looks disappointed in a dream, and (diver) wakes with the statue's lines on (diver.his/her) own face.
The lagoon clouds over, and a fish jumps every time (diver) passes the spot.
The face is as big as a hut.
Fish swim in and out of its open mouth.
The water gets colder and greener.

pieces.label: The Night the Hill Moved
pieces.text: After a week of rain, the hillside slides down between the huts in the night, and (trapped) is shouting from inside a half-buried hut.

pieces.label: Dig Right Now
pieces.text: (Rescuer) throws (rescuer.himself/herself) at the mud with (rescuer.his/her) bare hands, scooping it away from the doorway. It's heavy and cold and keeps sliding back...

pieces.label: Run for Help
pieces.text: "Hold on!" (rescuer) shouts, and runs, pounding on doors and yelling. Within minutes the whole village is out in the rain with sticks, baskets and bare hands...
(Rescuer) drags (trapped) out, but a fallen rafter has crushed (rescuer.his/her) leg, and it never heals straight.
(Rescuer) pushes (trapped) out, then the second slide comes. (Rescuer) is found at dawn, holding up the rafter.
With the whole village digging, (trapped) is out within the hour and the huts are rebuilt on stone footings.
(Trapped) has dug out through the back wall and is waving from the roof, plastered in mud.
A sound like a giant clearing its throat.
The mud is heavy and cold and keeps sliding back.
Someone plants bamboo along the new path to hold the soil.

pieces.label: The Mask Carver's New Faces
pieces.text: (carver) has been carving driftwood masks that tell (wearer.him/her) who they're for, and brings (wearer) a red and white one. "This one's yours."

pieces.label: Put It On
pieces.text: (Wearer) ties the mask on. It's warm inside, warmer than wood should be, and it smells of salt and smoke. (wearer.He/She) counts to three and takes it off...

pieces.label: Hand It Back
