pieces.text: (Subject) puts down the washing and stands in the middle of the path, face turned up, while the golden cloud drifts down around (subject.him/her)...
(Subject)'s face is unchanged, but the washing stays gold forever.
The wet cloth let the dust through, and (subject) wakes looking like an old carving.
The moths settle like a mask and lift away, leaving a new face.
Half the village comes out, and everyone is gold by morning.
Moths bump against the cloth like soft raindrops.
The paths glitter in the morning.
The elders cover their faces with cloth.

pieces.label: The Rainbow Over the Waterfall
pieces.text: When the morning sun makes a rainbow that touches the pool below the waterfall, the old story says a couple who swim through it will be blessed with children, as many as the sea spirit's daughter decides.

pieces.label: Swim Through It
pieces.text: They wade in hand in hand and swim through the rainbow. For a moment the water around them glows every colour at once...

pieces.label: Watch From the Rocks
pieces.text: They sit on the warm rocks and watch the rainbow until the sun climbs too high and it fades. Then, from behind the waterfall, they hear a baby crying...
The healers hear {#babies:one strong heartbeat|two heartbeats|three heartbeats}. "She must have been in a generous mood."
One baby, a sleeping basket painted every colour, and a laugh every time the sun hits the water.
A baby behind the waterfall, in a cloth that shimmers like spray.
Only baby birds squawking for their mother.
The rainbow touches the pool.
The water glows every colour at once.
The warm rocks by the pool.

pieces.label: The Lost Recipe for the Shaking Sickness
pieces.text: (sick) has the shaking sickness, and the old cure of three roots and a flower was lost in a flood; (healer) thinks the flower is red ginger, the oldest healer thinks it is the poisonous white trumpet flower.

pieces.label: The Red Ginger
pieces.text: (Healer) grinds the three roots with the red ginger blossom into a sharp, sweet-smelling paste, and rubs it into (sick)'s hands and legs, morning and night...

pieces.label: The White Trumpet Flower
pieces.text: The old healer measures out the trumpet flower with great care, one tiny petal at a time, and grinds it into the paste. (Healer) watches nervously...
It was ginger. Every healer gets a copy and a lesson, and the old healer asks for one too.
It does nothing, and the tremor never leaves (sick)'s hands.
The old healer was right, and remembers eleven more lost recipes.
Cured, but one petal too many. ONE PETAL LESS.
Three roots and a flower.
One tiny petal at a time.
The scroll was lost in a flood years ago.

pieces.label: The Games With the Hill Village
pieces.text: The hill village challenges the village to running, climbing, swimming and canoe racing at the next full moon, loser hosts the feast, and (chief) puts (organiser) in charge.

pieces.label: Train the Best Four
pieces.text: (Organiser) picks the fastest runner, the best climber, the strongest swimmer and the canoe crew, and works them from dawn to dusk for a month...

pieces.label: Everyone Practises
pieces.text: (Organiser) announces that every villager who wants to can practise, and every evening for a month the beach is full of people racing, climbing palms and splashing in the shallows...
Three wins out of four, and the two villages dance until dawn.
(runner) tears something three days before, and it never heals right.
No win, but dozens of better runners and swimmers. "Next year."
(champion), never picked for anything, wins the swimming by a length.
The loser hosts a feast for the winner.
The beach is full of people racing.
Palms climbed, shallows splashed.

pieces.label: The Dolphin Who Wouldn't Leave
pieces.text: For a month a young dolphin has followed (swimmer) everywhere, and the elders say dolphins were people once who chose the sea; this morning it whistles at (swimmer) and swims out to the reef and back, as if asking (swimmer.him/her) to follow.

pieces.label: Swim Out With It
pieces.text: (Swimmer) wades in and swims after the dolphin, out over the lagoon, past the reef, into the deep blue water. The dolphin circles (swimmer.him/her), whistling happily...

pieces.label: Stay on the Beach
pieces.text: (Swimmer) sits down on the sand. The dolphin swims out and back, out and back, whistling more and more sadly...
(Swimmer) never comes back, and now there are two young dolphins by the reef.
Hours in the blue, and (swimmer) comes home at sunset with a young, bright face.
One high leap, and the dolphin never comes back. Swimming isn't worth it without it.
It herds a shoal of fish into the shallows. "That's for staying."
Leaping and whistling beside the canoe.
Out and back, out and back.
The deep blue water past the reef.

pieces.label: The Smoked Fish Contest
pieces.text: (Challenger) challenges (cook), the head cook who says nobody else smokes fish right, to a contest: green coconut husks against the elders' ironwood chips.

pieces.label: Coconut Husks
pieces.text: (Challenger) smokes (challenger.his/her) fish over the green husks all day, turning them carefully. The smoke is white and sweet and drifts all over the village...

pieces.label: Ironwood
pieces.text: Ironwood.

pieces.label: But Better
pieces.text: But Better.
The village chooses (challenger)'s by a lot. "It's better." And the cooking fire loses its joy for (cook).
Wonderful the first day, sticky by the third. (cook) shows (challenger) the ironwood trick, just once.
A draw, then the best batch ever, smoked side by side, arguing.
The herbs catch fire and the fish taste like a burnt sandal.
The smoke is white and sweet.
Low and slow.
Twenty years at the cooking fire.

pieces.label: The Map of Wrinkles
pieces.text: (elder), whose face the children call a map, offers to give (receiver) the line that holds the way to the best fishing grounds, but warns that lines carry years with them.

pieces.label: Take the Line
pieces.text: (elder) puts (receiver.his/her) thumb on (receiver)'s forehead and draws it slowly down, the way a person draws in the sand. It feels warm, then heavy...

pieces.label: Politely Say No
pieces.text: "Thank you," says (receiver), "but I'd like to earn my own lines." (elder) laughs, a dry laugh like leaves, and pats (receiver.his/her) hand...
Ten years in a night, and the way to the fishing grounds as clear as (receiver.his/her) own name.
"I gave you the line, not the years." A lined face and a young body.
The secret goes to the grave, and (receiver) finds the grounds alone, years later. "Earned it."
"Good answer." An hour of the most useful advice (receiver) has ever had.
Every line is a place (receiver.he/she) has been.
A dry laugh like leaves.
The thumb draws down like drawing in the sand.

pieces.label: The Teenagers in the Cave
pieces.text: (teen) went into the hill caves on a dare and a passage collapsed behind (rescuer.him/her), and the two friends who came back can hear (rescuer.him/her) calling from under the rocks.

pieces.label: Go Straight In
pieces.text: (Rescuer) follows the two friends into the cave with a single torch. The calling gets louder as they go deeper. (Rescuer) starts pulling rocks away from the collapse with (rescuer.his/her) bare hands...

pieces.label: Get More Hands
pieces.text: (Rescuer) sends one friend running for the village and goes in with the other to keep (teen) talking. Within the hour, ten villagers arrive with torches and digging sticks...
(Rescuer) gets them all out, then a stone from the roof takes (rescuer.his/her) name.
(teen)'s pinned leg never mends straight. The glint was a puddle.
Ten diggers, a cheering village, and a month of grounding full of visitors.
Dug out clutching an old tablet about finding water underground.
The two friends are white-faced.
A single torch.
Torches and digging sticks.

pieces.label: The Second Naming
pieces.text: (elder) brings back the old custom of a second name given for a deed worth naming, and chooses (honoured), who pulled two children out of the surf last month.

pieces.label: Let the Elders Choose
pieces.text: The elders put their heads together and whisper for a long time. Then (elder) stands up, clears (honoured.his/her) throat, and announces it...

pieces.label: Choose (His/Her) Own
pieces.text: (Honoured) stands by the fire, looking at all the faces looking at (honoured.him/her), and thinks about what name (honoured.he/she) would want to be called for the rest of (honoured.his/her) life...
The name of the first people's best swimmer. Within a month (honoured) has to think to remember the old one.
A fine old name, and then everyone wants one. Three nights of naming.
The name of the grandparent who taught (honoured.him/her) to swim.
"I'll keep the one I have." The wisest answer in years.
Two names: one given at birth, one earned.
The children cheer.
The fire burns low.

pieces.label: The Bundle in the Breadfruit Tree
pieces.text: High in the breadfruit tree, planted by a mother who lost her child at sea, (picker) spots a wriggling bundle of leaves with a tiny fist poking out.

pieces.label: Climb Up Now
pieces.text: (Picker) climbs, hugging the trunk, then edges out along the thin branch, which bends lower and lower under (picker.his/her) weight...

pieces.label: Run for a Ladder
pieces.text: (Picker) runs to the village shouting for a ladder. By the time (picker.he/she) comes back with two builders and a bamboo ladder, (picker.his/her) partner, (partner), is already standing under the tree...
The branch bends low and the bundle almost lands in (picker)'s arms. A sticky, gurgling baby.
The branch snaps and (picker) lands so the baby lands on top. Never once regretted.
(partner) waits at the bottom with arms out. The tree gets a ribbon.
Just a caterpillar in the leaves, and the biggest breadfruit crop ever.
The bundle is sticky with breadfruit sap.
The branch bends lower and lower.
A tiny fist pokes out of the top.

pieces.label: The Moon Bath
pieces.text: At midnight, waist-deep in the full moon's silver path on the lagoon, (bather) realises (bather.he/she) doesn't know whether (bather.he/she) is facing the moon, which decides if the years are washed off or the youth.

pieces.label: Turn to Face the Moon
pieces.text: (Bather) turns slowly in the water until the full moon is right in front of (bather.him/her), huge and white. (bather.He/She) takes a breath and ducks under...

pieces.label: Duck Under As (He/She) Is
pieces.text: (Bather) decides not to risk turning the wrong way, and ducks under right where (bather.he/she) stands, with the moon somewhere behind (bather.him/her)...
Warm water, and the face (bather) had at twenty. "It's all in the facing."
Cold water, a lined face. "Sometimes the moon is just in a mood."
Back to the moon after all. "It doesn't undo. It only does."
Facing it all along without knowing. "Pure luck." (Bather) says skill.
The moon rises straight out of the sea.
A silver path on the lagoon.
"Never with your back to it."

pieces.label: The Morning After the Tremor
pieces.text: The ground shook in the night, and in the morning half the huts have cracked posts and leaning walls; the elders say the old fire under the mountain may turn over again.

pieces.label: Mend at Once
pieces.text: (Builder) gathers the builders and starts with the worst huts, propping walls and replacing cracked posts while the families watch from outside...

pieces.label: Wait a Few Days
pieces.text: (Builder) tells everyone to sleep in the open, away from the leaning walls, and waits. The village camps on the beach for three nights...
New posts set on flat stones, and the next tremor cracks none of them.
The second tremor throws (builder) off a roof, and (builder.he/she) shouts directions from a mat.
Three nights under the stars, the best thing all year for the children.
Two cracked huts fall flat with nobody in them, and the scroll-keepers write it all down.
Pots knocked off shelves.
Every baby in the village awake.
The old fire under the mountain turns over in its sleep.

pieces.label: The Sweet Spring and the Sour Spring
pieces.text: Two springs bubble side by side in the hills, one sweet and one sour, and nobody remembers which is which because whoever drinks from the sour one forgets.

pieces.label: The Left Spring
pieces.text: (Drinker) kneels at the left spring, cups (drinker.his/her) hands, and drinks deeply. The water is cold and tastes of stone...

pieces.label: The Right Spring
pieces.text: (Drinker) kneels at the right spring, cups (drinker.his/her) hands, and drinks. The water is warm and tastes faintly of flowers...
Swimming, which (drinker) loved more than anything, just seems wet now.
A taste of honey, and work isn't the weight it used to be. "The left one's sweet."
It tastes lovely, and (drinker), who was always first up to dance, stays sitting down.
Sweet and remembered, and (drinker) sits down in the middle of the noisy meeting hut.
A hand's width apart.
Cold water that tastes of stone.
Warm water that tastes faintly of flowers.

pieces.label: The Mist That Takes Names
pieces.text: The Forgetting Mist, made long ago by a grieving spell-keeper, sits thick in the valley behind the village, and (traveller) has to cross to the far gardens.

pieces.label: Walk Through
pieces.text: Walk Through.

pieces.label: Calling (His/Her) Name
pieces.text: Calling (traveller.His/Her) Name.

pieces.label: The Long Way Round
pieces.text: (Traveller) climbs the ridge, which takes half the morning, and looks down at the mist sitting in the valley below like milk in a bowl...
Another voice says (traveller)'s name louder and louder until (traveller) has none.
The other voice walks out behind (traveller), made of everything the mist ever took.
From the ridge, (traveller) watches (other) walk in and never walk out.
A long, hot walk, and everything arrives where (traveller) left it.
People in the mist can't see their own hands.
The mist sits in the valley like milk in a bowl.
The mist swallows the sound.

pieces.label: The Harvest Moon Dance
pieces.text: At the harvest moon dance, (mother) and (friend) are the last couple still dancing at midnight, and the saying goes that the couple who dances longest will have a child before the next harvest.

pieces.label: Dance Until Dawn
pieces.text: They dance on, slower and slower, holding each other up, while the drummers swap places three times and the village cheers them on...

pieces.label: Stop Now
pieces.text: "We've won," gasps (friend). "Sit down. Please." They sit by the fire, and someone brings them coconut water, and the drums play on...
A heap by the embers at dawn, and the saying holds.
A traveller steps out of the firelight with a baby. "A village where people love each other this much."
"It's the winning, not the dawn." Pregnant before the harvest.
No baby yet, and the dancing was the point.
The drummers swap places three times.
Holding each other up.
Coconut water by the fire.

pieces.label: The Shell of Turning Years
pieces.text: A trader gave (holder) a spiral shell from an island where nobody grows old: turn it the way the spiral goes and grow younger, the other way and grow older, and only once.

pieces.label: Turn It Left
pieces.text: (Holder) turns the shell slowly to the left. The sea inside rushes, roars, and then goes very quiet...

pieces.label: Turn It Right
pieces.text: (Holder) turns the shell slowly to the right. The sea inside rushes and roars, and then a voice inside it says, very clearly, "Oh, not that way"...
Ten years gone like water down a drain, and a silent shell kept on the shelf.
Ten years in a moment. "It was right. Of course it was right."
"Oh, not that way." A younger face and the same knees.
Nothing at all, but the children say they can still hear the voice.
Cream and brown, spiralling.
The sea inside is very loud.
Only once. The shell only turns once.

pieces.label: The Canoe That Came Back Twice
pieces.text: Paddling home from a glass-flat calm where sea and sky looked the same, (fisher) sees a second, identical canoe following, its paddler stroking exactly in time.

pieces.label: Wait for It
pieces.text: (Fisher) waits. The other canoe drifts closer and closer, until it bumps gently against (fisher.his/hers). The other paddler looks up...

pieces.label: Paddle Hard for the Beach
pieces.text: (Fisher) digs in and paddles as hard as (fisher.he/she) can. The other canoe keeps pace, stroke for stroke, until the edge of the calm...
It's (fisher), down to the fish scales. "The calm made two of us."
Sky and sea swap places, and only one canoe comes back, with someone who answers only to (made1).
The other canoe stops at the edge of the calm and waves, and the calm closes like a lid.
Two canoes hit the beach at once. "At least you caught twice as much fish."
The sea like glass.
Stroke for stroke.
The calm closes over it like a lid.

pieces.label: The Healer's Sweet Tonic
pieces.text: (healer) has made a cough tonic of honey, wild ginger and crushed coral that tastes wonderful, which is suspicious, and (patient) is tempted to drink the whole gourd at once.

pieces.label: A Spoonful at a Time
pieces.text: (Patient) takes one spoonful every morning, as told, and makes the gourd last a whole week, which takes a great deal of willpower...

pieces.label: Drink the Lot
pieces.text: (Patient) drinks the whole gourd in one go, licking the last drops off the rim. It is the best thing (patient.he/she) has ever tasted. For a moment...
Cured, and several villagers develop suspicious little coughs whenever a new batch is brewed.
"It's lovely. For the first three days." Even the healers' hut makes (patient) wince.
Too much coral. ONE SPOONFUL. IT MEANS IT.
Not enough coral, too much honey, and food loses its appeal.
Good medicine tastes terrible.
Honey, wild ginger and crushed coral.
Licking the last drops off the rim.

pieces.label: The Ghost in the Empty Hut
pieces.text: The hut at the end of the row has stood empty and falling apart for a year, and at dusk (subject) hears someone inside it humming, sad and tuneless.

pieces.label: Go Inside
pieces.text: (Subject) pushes the sagging door open. Inside it is dark and smells of old thatch. The humming stops. Something brushes past (subject.his/her) face, cool as a breath...

pieces.label: Fetch the Builders in the Morning
pieces.text: (Subject) goes home and sleeps badly. In the morning, (subject.he/she) brings the builders, and they stand outside the empty hut listening. The humming is still there, in broad daylight...
Happier humming beside (subject)'s ear, and a face shaped a little like the carved doorposts.
A cracked ridgepole that hums in the wind, and three more found and mended.
The hut is mended just in time for a young family coming over the hill.
Nesting doves in the rafters, left in peace.
The roof sags and the walls lean.
Cool as a breath.
A sad, tuneless sort of hum.
